text.en: Minimalist is a Durin structural engineer and architect. He suffers from advanced Oripathy and is currently undergoing treatment at Rhodes Island. He works in the Engineering Department and occasionally participates in field missions in that capacity.
text.zh: 至简，杜林族结构工程师、建筑设计师，重度矿石病感染者，目前于罗德岛接受治疗，于工程部任职，偶尔作为工程干员参与外勤任务。

text.en:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 9.6%
Small traces of infection are visible on his right leg.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.27u/L
Minimalist is prone to forgetting about his treatment. At such times, a single phrase will put him on the examination bed in seconds: 
'Hey, is that Gavial?'
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓模糊，可见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测异常，有矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】9.6%
右腿可见少量源石结晶。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.27u/L
至简时常因为太过沉浸于设计而忘记按时到医疗部接受治疗，这个时候有一句话非常管用，说完之后三秒钟就能看到至简躺在体检床上：
“嘉维尔来了！”

text.en:
While on duty, Rhodes Island operators are not especially concerned with Durin operators from underground, but off-duty, they can't help but be curious. From Durin's clumsiness and Myrtle's energy, to Chestnut's down-to-earth attitude, our operators had wonderful illusions about the Durin. That is, until they met Minimalist.
Though Gavial says he's much more approachable than he used to be, Minimalist continues to occasionally do things that make his colleagues speechless. These include suddenly showing up in a room to critique the interior design, submitting 80 applications to renovate his quarters in a single month, and most characteristically, insisting that he is kept clean and tidy from head to toe. No matter how urgent the situation, his pencil must be wiped clear of dust and secured behind his ear, lest it bump into any corner of his body. Every time he does this, the medic who completed the handover with Gavial's team on the initial field mission would put on an expression that says, 'I told you so.'
On the other hand, Minimalist's talent for design is beyond question. His interior design proposals are simple but effective, and many have reluctantly admitted that they have gained useful inspiration from his incessant nagging. As for the positive side of his personality, there are no (MISSING RECORD)

Attachment 1:
I'm sorry. I should not overwrite other people's documents. I should not delete data from the terminal without permission. (100 repetitions omitted) —Minimalist
text.zh:
在工作中，罗德岛的干员们不会对来自地底的杜林干员有过多的关注，但在生活中，干员们对杜林人还是很感兴趣的：有杜林小姐的迷迷糊糊，桃金娘小姐的活力满满，还有褐果的认真踏实，干员们对杜林一族的幻想保持在一个美好的基准上，然后他们遇见了至简。
虽然嘉维尔说他已经好了许多，但有时候至简的行动还是会让一些干员半天说不出话来。比如突然出现在哪里并对四周的室内设计指指点点，一个月提交了八十次申请要改造自己的宿舍，还有就是他最明显的特点：一定要保证自己浑身上下都是完全干净的，不论遇到多紧急的情况，那支绘图的铅笔都要擦干净笔屑、稳稳地别在耳后，以免蹭到身上任何一个角落。而每当这种时候，当初出外勤与嘉维尔一行人完成对接的那位医疗干员总是会摆出一副“我早就和你们说过了”的表情。
不过至简做的设计是真的很有水准，对于房屋内部改造，他会提出很多十分简洁但有效的构架。有时有什么加急的活做不完，只要有他在旁边絮絮叨叨，很快就能有新灵感。笔者写到这里时被身边的同事询问至简性格上有什么优点，笔者的回答是没（以下记录缺失）

附件一：
我不应该在文件上乱涂乱画，不应该擅自删除终端资料，我错了。——至简

text.en:
Despite all this, no operator truly dislikes Minimalist. It is clear to everyone that he is experiencing growing pains while trying to learn how to get along with others. For example, while other operators might seek help from more experienced colleagues when they run into trouble, Minimalist would mull over it on his own without speaking to anyone. He knows he should ask for help, but would instead drag things on for days. And when he finally makes a decision, the state of his hair will reflect the scale of the issue as he goes off on various unrelated tangents until he finally, reluctantly, talks about the problem.
Some operators have reported this to Closure: when helping someone else with a design, he struts like a fowlbeast that caught a dozen slugs that morning, but he has great difficulty asking for help when he runs into trouble himself. Perhaps it is a matter of pride—which is not a bad thing for a designer—but Minimalist needs to learn that anyone can run into problems, no matter how good they are, and that he should accept that rather than deny it.
'He can be pretty docile in that state. After you help him, follow up with a few words, and he'll do much better the next time.' —Unnamed Engineering Operator
text.zh:
不过虽然如此，并没有哪位干员会真的去讨厌至简，大家能看出来，至简在很努力地学着如何和众人好好相处，只不过他现在还不能特别好地掌握那个度。比如其他干员在遇到困难时总是会赶紧向经验丰富的前辈求救，或者是和同龄干员一起讨论，至简则会先独自一个人想来想去，和谁也不说。他也知道自己应该去寻求帮助，但总是会拖上好几天，然后顶着一看就是遇到大问题了的发型别别扭扭地讲一大堆无关的事，最后才说出自己无法解决的问题。
一部分工程部干员向可露希尔反映过这个问题，明明至简在帮别人想设计的时候脸上表情看起来十分得意，像是一早起来就抓到十条大肥虫的小羽兽，但他自己在遇到困难的时候却这么难去开口寻求帮助。或许他还是太过自矜了，对一个设计者来说，自矜不算坏事，但至简也需要更多的时间和经历来意识到——再厉害的人也会遇到瓶颈，设计者要做的事是接受这一事实，而不是对抗它，更不要因此否定自己。
“不过他其实还是挺听话的，你在帮完他之后趁热打铁说上几句，下次他的状态就能好上很多。”——某工程部干员

text.en:
Minimalist never thought he would leave Zeruertza, nor could he have imagined that he would work on repairing the great dome in the same way that a mortuary artist works on the dead. He did his best with the time he had, left the city where he grew up in slumber, and awoke to the sights and sounds of Acahualla. Most of the former residents of Zeruertza stayed with the tribespeople and began to build a new home, while Minimalist and a few other Infected came to Rhodes Island for treatment.
He rarely brings up Zeruertza, nor does he display much in the way of homesickness. Like many other former Zeruertzans, Minimalist's outlook is optimistic, believing that they will find a new home. He cannot help but feel a pang of regret, however, that the recognition that he finally earned must be buried underground, never again to see the light of day. At first, he wanted to help rebuild the new home. Whatever time he had left, he would use it, as the current Design Representative, to help the people of Zeruertza build a sustainable city. The plan eventually fell through, not because the Zeruertzans did not want to burden him with the responsibility, but because most of them were too busy enjoying their new lives on the surface to work together. So he accepted Gavial's proposal, and traveled to Rhodes Island to receive treatment for his Oripathy, somewhat to his chagrin.
Minimalist looked back at the rainforest on the day he departed. Lightrace had left to find his teacher, and the Zeruertzans had begun to build a scattering of temporary dwellings. Minimalist told Gavial that he expected his trip to Rhodes Island to be temporary, that someday, he'd return to build a home that everyone would be happy with.
text.zh:
至简在之前从未想过自己有一天会离开际崖城，也从未想过自己修缮大穹顶的契机竟然是为了留下它一个完美的遗容，但事情就是这样发生了。他在仓促之间尽力做到了最好，在睡梦里离开了那座生活已久的城市，等到他再次睁开眼的时候，周围已经是阿卡胡拉的地上风景了。绝大部分的际崖城居民们留在部落中开始搭建新的家园，至简和其他几位感染者来到了罗德岛，接受治疗。
他不怎么提起际崖城，也不怎么流露出怀念的情绪，和众多际崖城居民一样，至简展示出了一种豁达的态度：他们还会有下一个家园。只是至简在心里还是觉得微微可惜，他最终得到了认可，但这份认可的证明却只能被埋在地下，而且应该不会再有可以重见的那一天，所以他原本也想一同加入修建新家园的行列——如果自己的生命注定短暂，他要用这些时间以现任设计代表的身份，为际崖城居民们设计出可以让他们长久居住的城市。但这件事最终也是因为际崖城的居民们，没有继续推进下去，倒不是因为他们不愿至简辛苦，而是大部分人完全沉迷于在地上玩耍，没有人一起干活。在看到这幅景象后，至简苦笑着被嘉维尔说动，决定先前往罗德岛治疗矿石病。
在离开的那一天，至简回头看向这片雨林，叙光已经出发去寻找老师，零零散散的一些际崖城居民开始建起暂住的房屋。至简告诉嘉维尔，自己只是暂时前往罗德岛，总有一天，他还要回到这里，建出能让自己和所有人都满意的家园。

text.en:
Minimalist received his first major solo project several months after joining Rhodes Island: modifying a storage space on the lower levels of the ship, which had accumulated too much random equipment and items over the years due to a lack of planning, making any modification a complicated process. The Engineering Department hoped that the assignment would improve his approach, while also making preparations in case anything unexpected came up. As expected, Minimalist's face fell when he saw the storage space, but he surprisingly refrained from the long tirade that he might have went on under normal circumstances. Instead, he calmly accepted the assignment, and began working on a draft. One month later, Minimalist submitted a design that far exceeded expectations: the space was thoroughly reorganized, and areas previously wasted were put to good use. He went around the various departments that used the items kept there, working out their optimal method of storage, and discussing the design with other engineers. Each iteration took less and less time, the entire process went smoothly, and he was in good spirits.
Minimalist did not explain the surprising result, only expressing that he is enjoying designing on his own now because he wanted to see his teacher again, and to show them that he is strong, independent, and at peace.
We do not understand what happened between Minimalist and his teacher, or how Gavial changed him, but at least he seems to be in a good place right now. In one instance, when Minimalist realized that he had not felt pain for a while after undergoing treatment, he opened a barrel of Zeruertza berry tomato wine for the first time and enjoyed it in his quarters, feeling that time has slowed down, and that he had begun to understand why his fellows want to enjoy life to the fullest.
Since then, a change can be observed in Minimalist's designs: his quarters, for example, have begun to incorporate more gentle lines and colors other than white, as well as furniture with what he used to call 'meaningless' and 'aesthetically unsound' features.
In Gavial's words, they are finally suitable for habitation.
text.zh:
在来到罗德岛几个月后，至简接到了他第一个独立大型任务：改造舰船下层的杂物间。那是一块很久以前就开始使用的底层空间，在并没有做好规划的情况下已经放入了太多物品和设备，并随着时间的推移逐渐混乱起来。这给后续的工作带来了很大的麻烦，改造中不可避免地会遇到十分多的问题。工程部希望能用这次任务进一步改善至简的工作状态，同时锻炼他的心态，自然，他们已经做好了相应的准备，以免出现无法应对的问题。至简看到杂物间的状态后意料之内地脸色黑了几度，但意料之外地没有对这里的状态发表他平日里会发表的长篇言论，反而是相当平静地接下了任务，回到他的设计台开始打草稿。一个月后，至简给出了一份超出工程部期待值的设计稿。原本杂乱的空间被分割有序，一些之前被浪费的拐角被重新利用，甚至做出了很多视觉上的错落。根据工程部的观察，至简主动询问了这些物品和设备的所有部门，规划出最合适的收纳状态，也时常和其他工程部干员讨论设计，修改设计稿所用的时间一次比一次少，整个流程十分顺畅，至简的精神状态也十分良好。
对于这个出乎工程部意料的结果，至简本人并没有过多的解释，他只是表示，自己现在能够做到享受自己的设计，最主要的原因是，他希望有一天能再见到自己的老师，而他想给老师展示的，是一个平和的、独立的、强大的自己。
我们并不是十分了解至简与他老师之间究竟发生过什么，嘉维尔又是如何改变了他，最起码现在，至简展现出来的状态不错。尤其是那一次，在至简一次次地接受治疗，突然发觉自己已经很久没有感受到来自这些石头的疼痛后，他第一次打开了一桶来自际崖城的浆果番茄酒，坐在宿舍里品尝着这种他之前从未仔细品尝过的甜味，时间似乎在变缓，至简感觉自己好像理解了族人们开心享乐的意义。
在那之后，至简也在下意识地逐渐转变着设计的风格：如果你得到允许进入至简的宿舍，你就能看到那些增加了许多柔和线条，以及出现了白色以外色彩的全新装潢，甚至他之前最厌恶复杂设计的各类家具上，也能看到原本他口中“毫无意义”的“美学失败品”。
“总算像人住的地方了。”嘉维尔这样评价。

text.en:
Have you ever seen Minimalist dressed up as a flower doll by Myrtle? It's truly a sight to behold.
It began when Myrtle held the 1st Rhodes Island Durin Party, which was also open to non-Durin. Minimalist never stopped complaining, but nevertheless decorated the activity room per Myrtle's instructions, all flowery and stuff.
As more and more people arrived, some of them got drunk on fruit wine—I won't say who brought it—and they began to dress each other up with the flowers in the room, in the style of a certain Durin festival. That's what happened to Minimalist, and Myrtle and Chestnut were the main culprits. They did an amazing job, let me tell you, and surprisingly Minimalist never got mad. He ended up joining in the fun, jumping all over the place to put flowers into other people's hair.
Like I said, I guess deep down, he actually loved it!
text.zh:
你如果见过至简被桃金娘小姐打扮成花朵娃娃的样子，相信我，你绝对会因为这件事笑上三天。
起因很简单，桃金娘小姐举办了罗德岛第一届杜林人联欢会，当然，不是杜林人也可以去参加，我就去了。至简嘴上说着又烦又复杂，还是按照桃金娘说的去布置了那个小活动厅，哇，真的是，花枝招展。
后来来参加的人越来越多，里面也越来越热闹，还有人偷偷带了点果酒——是谁我就暂时先保密了，大家开始用装扮房间的花朵互相打扮，模拟某个杜林城市的庆典，至简就被大家弄成那个样子了——主要还是桃金娘小姐和褐果的功劳，他俩审美还真不错！至简居然没生气，最后甚至跳起来往所有人头上插花，玩得开心得很！
我就说了，其实他心里说不定还挺喜欢的嘛！

value.en: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.
value.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为非感染者。

infectionStatus.en: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.
infectionStatus.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为非感染者。

text.en:
Pozëmka, or Avdotya Razorpen, as she calls herself. We can confirm that Avdotya is her actual first name, but she has been unwilling to provide her actual surname. After a risk evaluation, the HR Department has decided not to further press the issue.
Pozëmka was introduced to Rhodes Island by the Zeruertza business representative Croque Diamondface as a surveyor, and she now participates in our field operations as a Sniper Operator.
text.zh:
鸿雪，自称阿芙朵嘉·锐笔。可确认阿芙朵嘉为其本名，但本人不愿透露真实姓氏。在风险研判后，人事部决定不进行进一步的询问。
经际崖城商业代表克罗绮·砖石介绍来罗德岛考察，现作为狙击干员参与外勤任务。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Pozëmka shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L
Operator Pozëmka rarely comes into contact with Originium.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员鸿雪没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.12u/L
干员鸿雪甚少接触源石。

text.en:
Avdotya Razorpen, the literature representative of Zeruertza, played a crucial role in persuading the Durins to evacuate to Acahualla, although it's difficult to imagine that this Lupo woman standing before us is really the person described in the reports. As a Lupo serving as a Durin city's literature representative, there had to be a story behind it.
Our hunch was right, but Pozëmka is also extremely cautious around most non-Durin operators. While very courteous, she never reveals anything unnecessary. All the operators who came back from Zeruertza have apparently been told her backstory, but they all tacitly avoid going into the subject.
After a very long time, Pozëmka finally went briefly into her past before making it to Zeruertza: she used to be the daughter of an Ursus noble, and her family members all died one after another in a despicable political conspiracy. She was the only one fortunate enough to make it out alive, and, completely by chance, managed to stumble her way to Zeruertza.
She told us all this very calmly without going into any of the finer details, but her ice-cold tone clearly conveyed to us the pain, disillusionment, and horrors she had suffered.
Since then, she has lived in Zeruertza for years, enjoying a peace and quiet that she could only have dreamt of in the past, until Zeruertza's everlasting summer finally came to an end. Not only did the carefree Durins play no small part in soothing the pain left by her experiences, they also allowed her to stay in the city as one of their own. However, she too began to hold an almost prejudiced distrust towards anything created by non-Durins (or 'surface-dwellers'), from their works of culture to industrial products.
This is not her fault, much less the Durins'.
text.zh:
阿芙朵嘉·锐笔，际崖城的文学代表，在说服杜林人前往阿卡胡拉避难的过程中发挥了重要作用——很难想象报告上的这些话是在描述我们眼前的这位鲁珀族女性。杜林城邦的鲁珀族文学代表，这背后一定有故事。
我们的猜测没错，但鸿雪对绝大多数非杜林族干员保持着强烈的警惕性，在过分礼貌之余拒绝透露任何非必要的信息。从际崖城回来的干员们似乎听鸿雪讲过内情，但大家默契地三缄其口。
很久以后，鸿雪才略微谈到自己进入际崖城之前的经历：她原本是一名乌萨斯贵族的女儿；在一场乏善可陈的政治阴谋中，她的家人相继死去，最终只剩她一个人侥幸逃脱，误打误撞地进了际崖城。
她平淡地把这几句话说了出来，没有补充任何细节，但谁都能从她异常冰冷的语调中感受到她曾经历过的悲痛、恐怖和幻灭。
在那之后，她在际崖城度过了许多年，享受着对她而言来之不易的安宁与和平，直到际崖城的长夏终结。无忧无虑的杜林人很大程度上抚平了那段经历给她留下的创伤，让她从此以杜林城邦的一员自居，但也让她开始对非杜林人（或者说“地上人”）和他们创造出来的东西，从文化到工业产品，抱有近乎偏执的不信任感。
这不是她的错，更不是杜林人的错。

text.en: Unlike the courteous yet distant way she treats other operators, Pozëmka shows a level of adoration and care toward the Durins aboard Rhodes Island. According to Operator Minimalist, this wasn't at all how she was like in Zeruertza. At the time, she preferred to take strolls, space out as she sat alone in an open area, or write something—in other words, she wasn't the kind of person who worried about others. That all changed when she came to Rhodes Island. Pozëmka has started to pay careful attention to all aspects of our Durin operators' lifestyles: if they are eating well, if they are working too long, whether their equipment is properly sorted out before field operations, etc. Even Minimalist, who's known to be particularly difficult, had no choice but to admit next to his bucket full of pencils: 'The other day I complained about not having even pencils, and she immediately got me all these... I probably haven't been giving her enough credit before.' Pozëmka isn't ashamed to confess her reasons either: 'I'll admit that Rhodes Island is a good place, but it can never truly fulfill the needs of a Durin like Zeruertza did. I do this because I'm worried about them, and I thought I would help them take care of whatever they needed. That's all there is to it.' We've tried over and over to persuade her that her excessive wardship could actually have negative consequences, that it could keep the Durin operators from adjusting to their new lives on board. In the end, we might have managed to talk her out of it, or perhaps a Durin said something to her, but she finally started to see things a little differently and stopped meddling with every aspect of their lives. Even so, she still spends a lot of time with the Durins, and the Durins like her, too. It is only during these moments that she finally forgoes her vigilance and relaxes. Eventually, this relationship also expanded to the children on board Rhodes Island, but that's as far as it ever progressed. I'm not playing with toy blocks! I'm an adult! —Myrtle Erm... These are no ordinary toy blocks. This is a contest to see who can build the tallest tower. Wouldn't you enjoy such a thrilling, exciting competition, Generalissimo? —Pozëmka I'll do it! I'll do it! —Myrtle
text.zh:
与对待其他干员时礼貌而疏远的态度不同，鸿雪对罗德岛上的杜林族干员展现出非同一般的关爱。
据干员至简透露，鸿雪在际崖城的时候并不是现在这样的。那时她更喜欢到处散步，或者一个人坐在开阔的地方发呆，再就是写写东西——总而言之，不是喜欢替人操心的类型。
到了罗德岛之后可就不一样了。鸿雪会从各个角度关照岛上杜林族干员的生活，从餐食是否可口、工时是否太长，到外勤任务前的装备整理是否妥当，都在她的关注范围之内。就连性格别扭的至简都不得不坐在满满一铁皮桶的铅笔旁边承认：“我那天抱怨了一句铅笔不够，她就帮我弄来这么多……我以前可不知道她这么厉害。”
鸿雪本人倒不讳言这么做的理由：“罗德岛是个好地方，我承认。但罗德岛无论如何都不可能像际崖城一样满足杜林族干员的需求。我只是不太放心他们，然后顺手帮他们把事情办了而已。”
我们多次劝说她，过度的关爱可能会起到反作用，延缓杜林族干员适应新生活的进程。最后，不知道是我们的劝说起了效，还是哪位杜林族干员对她说了什么，鸿雪终于在一定程度上改变了原来的想法，至少不再帮杜林族干员包办生活琐事了。
尽管如此，她还是会花很多时间和杜林族干员们在一起，杜林族干员们也喜欢她。只有在这种时候，她才会露出完全放下戒备的放松表情。
后来这种关系扩展到罗德岛上的小孩子们身上，但范围也就到此为止了。

我不要玩积木，我已经成年了！
——桃金娘

呃……这可不是单纯的玩积木。你想，这可是一场比谁积木堆得最高的比赛，大将军不想享受这场紧张刺激的比赛吗？
——鸿雪

我要去我要去！
——桃金娘

text.en: As the 'literature representative,' Pozëmka penned a large amount of advertising and packaging copy in Zeruertza. Unlike the Zeruertza Durins' disorganized language, her advertising copy always stood out from the competition, and thanks to her masterful use of exoticism (to the Durins, at least), she always grabbed their attention in no time. There was no need to worry about not getting enough orders with her writing your advertisements. Pozëmka also writes literature—poems, novels, and plays—when she is not working on her commercial writings. Unlike her simple, straightforward advertising copy, the native Zeruertzan citizens tend to have a hard time understanding her plots and metaphors. Hunger, cold, conspiracy, and murder... These nouns are simply too unrelatable to the Durins. Even if they can by instinct recognize that conspiracy means plotting against someone, the most objectionable conspiracy they can think of is adding half a bottle of vinegar to someone else's mead. To Pozëmka, these two things have become the manifestation of a certain kind of contradiction. The exaggerated, fanciful marketing language represents the Durins' carefree lifestyle, while her ice-cold, gory literature ties her back to the past that she cannot bear to face. The Durins like the former, and so does she, but she has yet to be able to convince herself to not spend her free time on the latter. Instead, she's started to deliberately use different tools for her different writing tasks: she uses her typewriter exclusively for marketing copy, while she opts for a fountain pen and ink for her more personal creations. It's worth mentioning that when she participates in battle as a field operator, Pozëmka's two weapons of choice are both also derived from fountain pens and typewriters. She came into possession of her crossbow because of miscommunication when she first arrived in Zeruertza; it was actually a fountain pen that she wanted—and indeed the biggest piece of furniture in her dorm room right now is a fountain pen showcase—yet the Durin artificer made her a crossbow instead. As for her typewriter, it was modified by our Engineering Operators after she came to Rhodes Island. According to her, 'my guess is this typewriter won't see much use from now on. I'll be living on the surface and fighting plenty of battles. In which case, I might as well use it as a weapon.' Nevertheless, even aboard Rhodes Island, Pozëmka still receives requests to write advertising copy and slogans from time to time. While her typewriter can no longer produce words, she continues to accept these requests with pleasure. With her fountain pen, she plans out her ideas and writes her drafts. The final results that her clients receive are completely different from what she used to write in Zeruertza, with only her vivid rhetoric unchanged.
text.zh:
作为“文学代表”，鸿雪在际崖城承担了大量广告标语和文案包装之类的工作。与际崖城杜林人散漫的语言组织方式不同，她的广告词总能别出心裁，在融合（对杜林人而言的）异域风情的同时以最快速度抓住杜林人的眼球，很快就不愁没订单了。
在商业写作之余，鸿雪也在进行文学创作——诗歌、小说、剧作。与简单明快的广告词不同，土生土长的际崖城居民很难理解鸿雪笔下的情节和隐喻到底想表达什么。饥馑、严寒、阴谋、凶杀……这些名词对杜林人来说实在太遥远，就算他们在理性上认识到阴谋就是给别人使绊子，他们所能想象的最令人发指的阴谋也不过是往别人的蜜酒里兑半瓶醋。
对鸿雪来说，这两件事成了某种矛盾的具象化：浮夸有趣的广告词象征着杜林式惬意而无忧无虑的生活，而混合着寒冷与血腥味的文学创作连接着不堪回首的过去。杜林人喜欢前者，她也喜欢前者，但她始终无法说服自己，不要把闲暇时间投入后者之中。
她只是开始有意识地区分写作用的工具：写广告词时用打字机，而创作更私人的东西的时候，就用墨水和钢笔。
顺带一提，在作为外勤干员参与战斗时，鸿雪的两样武器也脱胎自钢笔和打字机。她的弩是初到际崖城时沟通不畅的产物，她想要一支新钢笔——现在她宿舍里体积最大的家具就是钢笔陈列柜——杜林工匠却做出了一把弩；她的“打字机”则是到罗德岛后工程干员的改装产物。按照本人的说法，“我预感这台打字机以后可能派不上用场了。反正以后要在地面上生活，战斗是少不了的，不如改装成武器吧。”
尽管如此，她在罗德岛上偶尔仍会接到一些广告和标语创作之类的请求。打字机已经无法打字，但她还是欣然接受。她用钢笔记录构思，打草稿，委托人得到的最终版本与她在际崖城写下的东西迥然不同，只有生动的修辞始终如一。

text.en:
'Pozëmka, I have actually had an opinion for a while that might perhaps offend you...'
'Please, Istina. I am very glad to have met a reader as perceptive as yourself. How could I possibly be offended?'
'I can tell that your characters really wish to cut ties with their homeland. However, at the end of your stories, those relationships are always brought to the fore in much more intense ways.'
'You're right. At first, I wanted them to cut ties with Ursus completely. However, every time I write an ending to that effect, I'm struck with a particularly strong sentiment... That it's something that I'm forcing onto the character; it's not the character's own will. I was never that brilliant of a writer. If I were to forcefully bend my characters' will based on my own preferences, then my writings would be completely meaningless.'
'You're too humble.'
'No, no... Actually, just recently, I've even come to the realization of just how ignorant I am.'
'What do you mean?'
'After I heard your story, it's been made all too apparent to me that... compared to me, the daughter of an Ursus noble who escaped to Zeruertza in my early years, you've experienced Ursus's cruelty in far more complicated and profound ways than I could ever imagine.'
'But you found the courage to pick up your pen nonetheless.'
'I merely scribbled away.'
......
'Pozëmka, supposing—and this is nothing more than a suggestion—supposing it could take your writings to new heights, would you go back to Ursus if you had the chance?'
'No, even if my writing never improves beyond what it is now, I don't want to experience that kind of pain and despair ever again.'
'Hm...'
'Do you not feel the same, having experienced so much yourself?'
'I... I would like to go back, actually. It's my homeland, after all.'
'Your homeland?'
'I'm sorry, Pozëmka, did I perhaps—'
'It's okay. It's no problem at all. It's just that the meaning of the word 'homeland' is becoming more and more unclear to me. Speaking of which, right now, the only place I really would like to go back to is Zeruertza.'
......
'Okay, let's not talk about this. Come, try this Durin-style beverage.'
'Is this... mead?'
'Relax. This is non-alcoholic. I put in a special order with the Logistics Department.'
......
'Istina. Istina? Did you fall asleep? Don't tell me Logistics gave me alcoholic mead—
'Oh... Now I remember...'
'Honey drunk—right, she's honey drunk!
'How many years has it been since I last heard that term?'
text.zh:
“鸿雪小姐，其实我一直有一个感受，可能会有点冒犯……”
“请说吧，真理。我很高兴能遇到你这样敏锐的读者，怎么会觉得冒犯呢。”
“我能感受到，您笔下的角色很想切断自己和故乡的联系，但无论如何，这种联系都会在书末以更激烈的形式呈现在读者眼前。”
“没错。我一开始其实是想让他们彻底与乌萨斯撇清干系的。但是，每当我写出那样的结尾，我就有一种很强烈的感受……那是我强加给角色的东西，不是角色自己的意志。我本来就不是什么高明的作家，如果还要按照自己的喜好强行扭转人物的行为，那我写的东西就彻底没有意义了。”
“您太谦虚了。”
“不，不……其实最近，我甚至更深刻地体会到了自己的无知。”
“您是说？”
“在听过你们的故事之后，我更强烈地意识到，对于我，一个年纪轻轻就逃到际崖城避难的乌萨斯贵族的女儿来说，乌萨斯的残酷比我经历过的，比我能想象的，要复杂得多，也深重得多。”
“但您还是鼓起勇气去写了。”
“仅仅是去写而已。”
……
“鸿雪小姐，做个假设，仅仅是个假设——为了您在文学上能更进一步，假如有机会的话，您想回乌萨斯看看吗？”
“不。就算我只能止步于此，我也绝对不想再去体验那种痛苦和绝望了。”
“唔……”
“难道在经历了那么多之后，你不这么觉得？”
“我……其实是想回去看看的。那里毕竟是我的故乡。”
“故乡？”
“抱歉，鸿雪小姐，我是不是——”
“没关系，没关系的。我只是越来越搞不懂故乡这个词是什么意思了。话又说回来，此时此刻，能让我想‘回去’的地方，仍然只有际崖城。”
……
“好了，不聊这些了。来，尝尝杜林风格的饮料。”
“这个是……蜜酿？”
“放心，这是去除了酒精的版本，我特地找后勤部定制的。”
……
“真理，真理？你怎么睡着了？难道后勤部给我的是有酒精的——
“呃……我想起来了……
“醉蜜——对，一定是醉蜜！
“这个词已经有多少年没听人说过了？”

text.en:
[Classified Log]
January 18th
I came back to Sargon for a field mission. I've promised Inam already. I will control my urge and delay my return to Acahualla. First, we must have an audience with another lord ameer and seek their cooperation as Rhodes Island's representatives.
The tribes there are fighting over their water source. How pathetic.

January 25th
The tribes have made peace, though they are merely calling an armistice because of pressure from the lord ameer. Once the lord ameer relaxes his grip, they will most certainly start fighting again.

February 9th
We've wasted a dozen or so days because we found a secret Infected settlement in the area. I had never seen such poor living conditions.
I sounded the lord ameer out, and he very casually told me that if there were really any Infected under his rule, they must all be buried alive. It was all I could do to keep myself from shooting a bolt through him.

February 12th
I cared for an Infected. We have a patient who is in very poor condition. She told me she would die at the water source and poison it so that everyone would have to die of thirst too.
I tried to convince her that this would not alleviate anyone's suffering, but she would not listen.
I was in no position to criticize her, but it made me think of my days in Zeruertza all the more.

February 14th
How could this be?!
The patient really snuck away in the middle of the night while no one was watching. I made my way to the water source immediately, and she was walking back and forth by the waterside.
Again and again, she circled around it, and in the end... she walked into the desert, never to return.
I didn't go after her.
After I made it back to the settlement, I found a letter she had left for me. She told me she had thought it through. Even though everyone in the tribe were morons, she must at least think of their children in their stead. The children bear no blame.
This... would never have happened in Zeruertza. You cannot sow tragedy in Zeruertza's soil.
Once, I thought this would never happen even on the surface; the surface is home to no shortage of tragedies, but no one would abandon their hatred for the sake of children whom they have never met. Surely such plot points exist only in my novels, as a way to deceive myself, but—but!
I need to talk to someone!
text.zh:
【权限记录】
1月18日
因为外勤任务重回萨尔贡。和依娜姆说好了，我得先克制一下迫不及待的心情，晚些再去阿卡胡拉。我们要先谒见另一个王酋，代表罗德岛寻求与他们的合作。
当地的几个部落为水源打了起来，丑陋。

1月25日
那几个部落终于握手言和了，但也只是因为王酋的压力休战了而已。王酋的压力一减轻，他们多半还要打。

2月9日
耽搁了十几天，因为发现了当地一个秘密的感染者聚落。我从来没见过那么恶劣的居住条件。
我试探了一下，王酋轻描淡写地说，如果他治下真有感染者，就全部活埋掉。我不得不克制住给他一箭的冲动。

2月12日
护理感染者。有个患者的状况很不好，她说自己要死就死在水源地，把水源污染掉，让所有人一起渴死。
我试图说服她这么做不能减轻任何人的痛苦，但她完全不听。
我无权指责她，但她让我更加思念在际崖城度过的时光了。

2月14日
怎么会这样？！
那个患者真的趁人不备，在半夜偷偷溜走了。我第一时间赶到水源地，她就在水边徘徊。
她在水边绕了一圈又一圈，最后……走进了沙漠，再也没出来。
我没追上她。
回到聚落，我发现她给我留了一封信。她说自己想清楚了，就算部落里的家伙全都是混蛋，她至少要替那些人的孩子想一想。孩子是无辜的。
这种事情……永远都不会在际崖城发生。际崖城没有悲剧的土壤。
我曾经以为地上也不会有这种事——地上不乏悲剧，但没人会为几个素不相识的孩子放弃切齿的仇恨，这样的情节只可能出现在我的小说里，是我的自欺欺人，但是——但是！
我需要找个人谈谈！

text.en: Medjehtiqedti, Curator of Varjavandabad Museum. Only her friends can call her 'Titi'. Currently works with Rhodes Island as a field operator, and strives to repair relations between Sargon and Minos.
text.zh: 法尔贾万达巴德博物馆现任馆长梅捷缇克缇，只有朋友才可以称她“缇缇”。现以外勤干员的身份与罗德岛展开合作。她也希望能尽自己的全力，修复萨尔贡与米诺斯的关系。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Titi shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.021u/L
Operator Titi rarely comes into contact with Originium.

Operator Titi has quite the sweet tooth, possibly as a result of the traditional diet of her native region. I tried getting her to make some changes to her diet, to no avail.
I asked Operator Papyrus for advice, and she came up with a list of names which she told me to give to Titi. Titi spent some time looking at the list, then became extremely pale. She stayed away from high-sugar candied fruit for a long time afterwards.
Later, I learned that Papyrus had given me a list of famous padishahs who all lived to an old age, but suffered from tooth decay because they ate too many sweets.
—Hibiscus
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员缇缇没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.021u/L
干员缇缇甚少接触源石。

干员缇缇极度嗜甜，这一点可能与她居住地的传统饮食结构有关。我尝试过让她做出一些改变，但她始终不以为意。
不过，听说了我的苦恼之后，干员莎草帮我整理了一份名单，让我拿给缇缇，叫她在其中寻找规律。缇缇看到名单，认真思索了一番，突然脸色大变，而后在很长一段时间里，都放弃了那些重糖高甜的蜜饯。
我后来才知道，莎草列出来的那些名字，都属于萨尔贡历史上赫赫有名的帕夏，他们的共同特征，是长寿却因为嗜甜而烂牙。
——芙蓉

text.en:
Operator Titi almost immediately became integrated into the Rhodes Island community.
Her adventure began as soon as she parted ways with the HR operator who showed her the main facilities. There was hardly a corner of Rhodes Island that she didn't explore. After dining at the cafeteria, she exchanged a rare photocopy of an old Vine-Bead Court cookbook for Operator Matterhorn's collection of Kjeragi recipes. While visiting the Engineering Department, she expertly repaired an important part using glue meant for relic restoration. She even wandered into the mobility layer, making friends with the Sarkaz boiler workers on her first day.
As we got to know her, however, we grew even more perplexed. The seemingly insignificant accessories she wears are in fact valuable ancient relics, which she seems to treat with complete nonchalance. Her white ribbon in particular is more than decorative: driven by Originium Arts, it practically serves as an extra arm, allowing her to grab distant objects, and move or support herself during activities such as climbing. It is also a medium for her to take notes, record her discoveries and data, or even act as a cheat sheet for public speaking.
We soon learned that, while making friends with Titi is easy, truly getting to know her is a different story.

[Weapon Evaluation]
Titi's staff stands in contrast to her short stature. At her checkup, we immediately found that the staff amplified her Arts considerably. The antiques she wears and the classical design of the staff gave us the impression that it was a family heirloom passed down through generations, but she had in fact designed and assembled it herself.
Titi says that its design was inspired by ancient Sargonian artifacts. The scarab sealed inside a piece of golden amber in the middle represents eternal life and resurrection, an ancient symbol dating back to Lugalszargus, the 'Shah of Past and Future,' making it an ideal fit for her conservation Arts. Our discussion turned into an impromptu semiotics lecture, as at one point we thought the symbol represented some kind of power boost Arts, a misconception that she soon dispelled.
'Power boost? Oh, that's because of the seven amplifiers I installed on the staff, on the ring around the amber.'
text.zh:
干员缇缇一来到罗德岛，便以惊人的速度与大家熟悉起来。
在告别了带她了解罗德岛常用设施的人事干员之后，她立刻开始兴致勃勃地冒险，将罗德岛的上上下下都探索了个遍：在罗德岛食堂就餐后，她用一本稀有的影印版蔓珠院旧膳典，交换了干员角峰拿手的谢拉格特色菜菜谱；在工程部参观时，她掏出了随身携带的据说是文物修复用的胶水，熟练地帮忙粘好了重要的零件；最不可思议的是，她甚至还漫游到了动力层，只用了半天就与萨卡兹锅炉工们交上了朋友。
但在与缇缇成为朋友的过程中，我们的疑惑反而加深了：她身上许多看似不起眼的小饰品，其实都是贵重的古董，但她对待它们的态度十分随意；她身上的白色长带，我们本以为只是装饰品，后来发现她将它用作“附肢”，借助源石技艺，她可以用它来拿取远处的物品，在攀爬等活动中提拉、支撑身体，与此同时，这白色长带子又是她随手记录发现和数据的载体，甚至是她发表演讲时藏小抄的利器。
我们很快就意识到，与缇缇交上朋友可以很迅速，但要真正地了解她，恐怕没那么容易。

【武器鉴定】
在个子小小的缇缇手里，这把法杖十分显眼，当她带着它参加综合体检测试，我们立刻就发现，它对她的源石技艺有着明显的增幅作用，而且幅度还不小。缇缇身上佩戴着不少古董，这把法杖的设计看起来又有些古典，这些都导致我们产生了先入为主的想法，以为它又是源自缇缇家祖上丰厚的家底，但事实上，它是缇缇自己设计、拼装、制作的。
按照缇缇的说法，法杖的设计参考了一些古老的萨尔贡文物，法杖正中的金黄色琥珀里封存的圣甲虫代表永生与复活，是自“过去与未来之王”路加萨尔古斯时代便已开始流传的古老符号，正适合她那保存文物用的源石技艺。就这一点，她给我们来了一个小小的即兴符号学讲座，让我们一度甚至以为这种符号是我们尚未掌握的某种力量增幅术式，不过，很快她就打破了我们的这种幻想。
“力量增幅？哦，那是因为我在法杖上安了七个增幅器。喏，琥珀外围那一圈就是。”

text.en: [A Trimounts University Transcript] Museum Design: A- Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates a thorough understanding of modern museology theory, as well as a mind open enough to effectively implement new media to enrich the exhibition experience. Can sometimes be overly fixated on new forms, in particular conceptual interaction designs advocated by the Columbia Art and Design Center, leading to the exhibition's content being overshadowed by the presentation. Archaeological Analysis and Technology: A- (Joint course with Trimounts Academy of Technology) Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates high proficiency in technological methods for analyzing the materials and techniques of relics. Occasionally prone to spur-of-the-moment ideas, resulting in outlandish experiments, and insists on analyzing the failed results. Conservation and Restoration: A- Instructor Comments: Student demonstrates excellent grasp of conservation and restoration techniques for relics of various materials. Capable of independently coming up with restoration proposals for working with heavily damaged artifacts, plans that are often risky, but the results have generally exceeded expectations. The only issue being occasional violations of lab rules and protocols—do not use the lab's specially blended glue to stick your classmate's shoe soles back on! ... The transcript is a long one, with far more credits on it than needed to graduate. It includes her compulsory coursework, subjects tangentially connected to her major like international history, languages, art history, architecture, and folklore, but also courses like 'Ingredient Analysis of Sami Herbal Remedies', 'Principles of Automated Flying Machine Control', and 'Literary Analysis of Flowers of Quinde and Kerespereia', taken for reasons unknown. Even more surprising is that she got an 'A-' in most of her coursework and excelled academically by any definition, yet had very few full marks in any of her courses: the instructors usually docked her points here and there for unusual reasons. Titi did not seem especially concerned with her grades—what mattered more to her was whether the course was interesting, and her definition of an interesting course was very different from others. While most look for variety, lively pacing, and humor, she judges courses by whether they satisfy her curiosity and stimulate her desire to explore further. 'I went to Columbia because I thought it would be fun. I had just graduated from school in Menat-Ha'mait when a Columbian merchant showed up with a bunch of newfangled things and told me that Trimounts University accepted students from all over Terra. It made me want to check it out for myself. I didn't think much about the distance from Menat-Ha'mait to Trimounts, or how I was actually going to get accepted and enroll. I just thought I would cross that bridge when I got there.'
text.zh:
【一份特里蒙大学的成绩单】
博物馆陈列设计：A-
导师评语：全面掌握各类博物馆学前沿理论，思路开阔，在实践课中能较好地将新媒体应用于展览，丰富展览体验。但该生有时会太过执着于新形式，尤其偏爱哥伦比亚艺术设计中心提出的概念性交互设计，最终导致展览形式大于内容。

文物分析与科技检测：A-
（该课程与特里蒙理工学院联合授课）
导师评语：熟练掌握分析文物材料和制作工艺的现有科技手段。但有时会突发奇想，做一些异想天开的实验，并就失败的实验结果强行分析。

文物修复：A-
导师评语：熟练掌握针对各类材质文物的修复技术。对于一些破损严重的文物，能独立提出自己的修复方案，它们常常会有些冒险，但总体来说，成果超过预期。该生唯一的问题是没有完全遵守实验室规范——不准用实验室专门调配的胶水帮同学粘掉了底的拖鞋！

……

这份成绩单很长，加起来的学分总和远超过毕业的基本要求。这其中不只有她的专业必修课，还包括了各国历史、各国语言、艺术史、建筑学和民俗学等多少与她专业沾边的科目，乃至“萨米草药成分检测”“飞行器自动控制原理”和“《坎德之花》与《克瑞斯拉纪》精读”之类完全让人不明白她为何要学的课程。
更让人惊讶的是，这些课程中的绝大多数，她拿到的成绩都是A-——以平均的分数来看自然称得上优秀，但逐项审视，就会发现满分很少，几乎每门课程都会在一些奇怪的地方被导师扣点分。对此，缇缇本人并不以为意，相比于最终拿到的成绩，她更在意课程是否有趣——说到“有趣的课程”，她的评价标准也与大众的认知不同，我们会将有趣与枯燥对立，认为那些形式上更多样、更活泼幽默的课程属于“有趣”，而她则更看重它们是否能满足她的好奇心，是否激发出了她进一步探索的欲望。
“我去哥伦比亚，也只是因为感觉可能会很有趣嘛。当时我刚从米纳特哈玛仪的学校毕业，正好有个哥伦比亚的商人带着一堆新奇玩意儿过来，他又说特里蒙大学会招收泰拉各地的学生，我就想去哥伦比亚实地看看。至于米纳特哈玛仪到特里蒙的距离，还有到了当地要怎么入学之类的实际问题，我当时也没多想，反正事情到眼前了总有办法解决。”

text.en: Operator Titi describes her younger self as a 'free range wild child'. Her father was known as a ne'er-do-well amongst Menat-Ha'mait's nobility, having no interest in fame or fortune, only literature, and in particular in collecting books brought back to Sargon from occupied Minos. Never in great health, he fell ill when Titi was young and virtually stopped leaving the house altogether. To Titi, her father was like a plant that grew on the chair of his study. He would tell her stories if she went to find him, and if she did not, he did not concern himself with what she was doing. As such, she enjoyed more freedom than most noble children. She had plenty of room to explore, think, and imagine, and to reveal the laws and truth behind what she saw, what she was interested in. Her conclusions were not necessarily correct, and her ideas young and naive, but she had arrived at them on her own. The process of thinking helped her build trust in her own judgment, taught her how to obtain the information she wanted, and opened doors to new horizons. It took a long time for her to understand that there were many things that did not need to be said. How to explore, how to study, how to defuse hostility, how to help friends, how to find one's path forward, how to commit to what one thinks should be done... she had already learned all these things from the stories her father told her, and her mother's tacit approval and indulgence. [Book Excerpt] ...And so the silent Siopi returned to his homeland, but still he never spoke. 'You are friendly and outgoing. You never know if you might accidentally reveal the secret you are trying to keep in conversation.' The safest way, therefore, was to never speak. Once full of vigor and spirit when he left home, the young man now shut himself away, shunned contact with others, and died as silently as he lived. It was only a long time later, when the news of victory came from afar, that his fellows learned the secret he carried, and thus he became known as Siopi, the Silent Hero. —Excerpt from Vol.3 of Minoan Heroic Legends, New Edition, 1101, Varjavandabad Museum Press [Book Review] Scholars are excited about the publication of Minoan Heroic Legends, New Edition, and for good reason. Mr. Khnum Nasutu Mashayer has long been known for his extensive collection of Minoan literature, and this six-volume collection, totaling more than three thousand pages, is more than just a compilation of the famous legends collected in the Mashayer Archives and their many variations, but also of rare oral traditions that he personally collected during his time in Minos. It is a landmark in scholarship that will undoubtedly be cited by researchers for decades to come. It is perhaps also worth noting that the publication of this work was sponsored by Mr. Mashayer's widow, and it was compiled and edited by their daughter. This is itself something of a legend.
text.zh:
干员缇缇用两个词概括她的幼年生活——“放养”和“野生”。
她的父亲是米纳特哈玛仪的贵族阶层中有名的“废物”，对建功立业没有丝毫兴趣，一心沉迷于文学，热衷于搜集萨尔贡占领者从米诺斯带回国的书籍。在缇缇年幼的时候，父亲本就羸弱的身体染上了慢性疾病，渐渐地连门都不怎么出了。对于那时候的她来说，父亲就像是生长在书房里椅子上的一株植物，要是去书房找他，那他会给缇缇讲些喜欢的故事，但要是不去，父亲也完全不会管她每天在做什么。
缇缇因此获得了比通常贵族家的小孩更多的自由，她有充足的空间去探究，去理解，去想象，去还原她所见到的、她感兴趣的一切背后的真相与规律。虽然不少结论并不正确，很多想法也显得十分幼稚，但那都是她自己独立获得的成果，思考的过程本身才是最重要的，它让她能够坚信自己的判断，让她知道怎么去获得想要的信息，而更广阔的天地也由此向她完全敞开了怀抱。
一直要到很久以后，她才明白，有很多事是不需要直接说出来的。该如何探索，如何研究，如何化解敌意，如何帮助朋友，如何寻找自己未来的方向，如何坚定地做自己认为应做的事……在父亲讲述的故事中，在母亲选择性的默许与纵容中，她早已学会了这一切。

【一则书摘】
……于是沉默的西尔比回到了故乡，他依然一言不发。“你是个活泼的年轻人，你永远不知道自己并不想说出的秘密，是否会在你与他人的交谈中不经意间流露。”是的，所以最好的办法就是一句话也不说。在离开家乡前曾经意气风发的青年，回到故乡后就开始深居简出，不再与人接触，沉默着生活，最后沉默着死去。
直到很久之后，胜利的消息从远方传来，家乡的人们才知道，那位被当做怪人的老头，身上曾经背负过怎样沉重的秘密。自此，“沉默的英雄”西尔比的名号，渐渐地传播开来。
——凯尼-娜苏图-玛夏耶尔于米诺斯北部乡村采集，摘自《米诺斯英雄传说故事集新编·第三卷》，1101，法尔贾万达巴德博物馆出版社

【一则书评】
《米诺斯英雄传说故事集新编》的出版是学界的一大盛事。凯尼-娜苏图-玛夏耶尔先生一直以其庞大的米诺斯文学收藏而闻名，此次出版的六卷本故事集厚达三千余页，不仅涵盖了整理自其藏书的各个知名传说的诸多变体，更有其亲自在米诺斯采集的稀见口述传说，毫无疑问将成为相关研究的权威定本，为学者提供研究的有力支撑。
另外，值得一提的是，该书由玛夏耶尔先生的遗孀出资赞助，其女为之整理、编辑后出版，堪称一段佳话。

text.en:
We initially thought that the entity known as 'Mio' who accompanies Operator Titi was simply an ordinary Feline Beast Steward, although in hindsight there were certainly telling signs. Mio is very similar to Titi in its sociability, and its investigation of Rhodes Island took place concurrently with Titi's explorations. Mio quickly found its turf, claiming the best fresh fin belly from the cafeteria every morning, as well as a cushion on the sunniest spot on the bridge, though it does not visit every day.
Other operators claim to occasionally see a small, strange-looking Feline who often accompanies Titi, at times getting her out of tight spots, while at others getting into arguments with her, like two close yet bickering friends.
This has led to us theorizing about Mio's true nature... by now, we have grown rather familiar with such beings. For now, at least, there seems to be little cause for concern, since Mio's intervention has been limited to providing occasional assistance to Titi and filling its own stomach.

[Classified Log]
Hey, I picked the girl myself, I can't very well let her fend for herself. I like her personality, and she's not burdened by stuff like legacy or history, like so many other humans. Getting out of the Grand Bazaar wasn't easy, and I'd like nothing more than to have some real free time with nothing to worry about, but I guess the girl's not gonna stay put.
She and that damn curiosity of hers. Yeah, I know where she wants to go, but the depths of the desert is just not a nice place. The old Shah... yes, interesting fellow. Woof and I liked him, but his one-time dream, his discoveries in the south, his invincible army, and all his outlandish ideas, have all been twisted beyond recognition. As for the current Shahanshah, the lion who has lain low in the depths of the desert for many years... Has his silence and inaction been by choice, or has something happened to that ancient city in the sands, something beyond the control of puny humans? I don't know, and I don't particularly care to know. Frankly, I would prefer not to return to Shar-Agade, if I had a choice.
You're an interesting one too, Doctor... There are many of my kind here. I know they are uneasy too. It's a fresh, unfamiliar feeling, and I don't like it one bit.
text.zh:
关于干员缇缇身边跟着的那位，被称作“米奥”的……我们在一开始确实以为它只是普通的菲林兽亲。不，仔细想想，其实也没那么普通。从某种角度看，米奥与缇缇非常相似，十分自来熟。在缇缇刚踏上罗德岛，展开她的探索与冒险之旅时，那位也对罗德岛展开了调查，并迅速地占好了地盘：似乎从它来的第二天起，食堂每日早晨现杀的鳞最好的腹部肉就专属于它了；舰桥上阳光最好的地方，也都摆上了它的垫子——虽然它并不一定会去。
但按照另一些干员的说法，他们在缇缇身边看到的，是一个个子矮小、长相怪异的菲林，他会开口为缇缇解围，有时又会与缇缇斗嘴，两人熟稔得像是关系很好的一对损友，只是这样的情况并不太多见。
这些信息让我们不由得有了一些猜测……如今的我们对这样的存在早已不再陌生，假如米奥只是出于某种原因陪伴在缇缇身边，偶尔帮她做点什么，又在绝大多数时间只是表现得像个蹭吃蹭喝的兽亲，那我们似乎也不必对它太过紧张。至少目前看来如此。

【权限记录】
小丫头可是我精挑细选出来的，我当然不能放着她胡来不管。这家伙性格很对我胃口，而且不像某些小人类，身上背负着什么这那的传承啦、历史啦之类的麻烦玩意儿。唉，我可是好不容易才从大巴扎脱身的，要是能过上一阵轻松快乐的日子，那肯定再好不过，但我怀疑小丫头不会那么老实。
这家伙哪哪都好，就是好奇心太强。她心里想去的地方，不用她说出口我也知道。但那沙漠的深处，哪里是什么好地方？当年的沙阿……那确实是个有趣的家伙，我和沃奥都挺喜欢他。但这么多年过去了，他曾经的梦想，他在南方的发现，他手下曾经所向披靡的军队，还有他那些奇思妙想，早已不知道被扭曲成了什么模样。而且，如今在王座上的万王之王，那位在沙漠深处蛰伏了许多年的狮子，他的沉寂与不作为，到底是出于什么原因，是他主动的选择，还是在沙漠中的那座古老都城里又发生了什么小人类无法掌控的事……很难判断，我也不怎么想知道。老实说，要是可以的话，我压根儿就不想回沙尔-阿加德。
你也是个有趣的家伙，博士，在你这儿……能遇到不少我的同类。我知道，那些家伙跟我一样，也很不安。很新鲜的感觉，但我一点儿也不喜欢。

text.en:
Operator Titi's time in Minos clearly left a deep impression on her, but when we asked for her thoughts on the trip, her answer was not what we expected.
'For a long time I've been thinking about a question, one that my mother and teachers have asked me as well: where will my curiosity take me?
'The incident at the museum planted the seed of an idea in my mind, and the journey to Minos made it sprout. My curiosity about history, society and how it works, science and how it develops ultimately comes from a desire to learn the reasons behind things, the things that shape us and our society, and make us who we are today.
'Having visited Athenius, I now know that stories of heroes form the roots of Minos, the desires of all Minoans converging upon the concept of 'hero'. What about us? What are the roots of Sargon, and what is our common goal, our shared aspiration? I'm afraid I don't know the answer, yet.
'But I think I'll find the answer one day, when I've gained sufficient knowledge. Or when the day comes that I visit the ancient city with over a thousand years of history.'
text.zh:
很显然，米诺斯之旅给干员缇缇留下了深刻的印象，但细问这趟文化交流之旅的感想，她的回答却与我们想象的不太一样。
“从很早以前我就在思考一个问题，我的母亲和我的导师也曾问过我——我的好奇心要将我带到哪里去。
“博物馆的那次事件之后，我就隐隐约约有了一点想法，雅赛努斯之旅更让我坚定了这个念头——我对历史，对如今的各类社会和社区运作的模式，对所谓的‘科学’以及它生发的方式，这种种的好奇，归根结底是因为我想知道一切背后的原因，是什么塑造了我们和我们的社会，让我们变成了现在的模样。
“去过雅赛努斯之后，现在的我很清楚地了解，米诺斯的根源是英雄的故事，所有米诺斯人的渴望都在‘英雄’这个词语上凝聚。那么我们呢？我们萨尔贡的根源是什么？我们共同的目标，我们的向往又在哪里？你要是问我这个问题，我现在恐怕答不上来。
“但总有一天，只要我积累了足够的知识，或者，假如我能够踏入那座有着千年历史堆积的古老城市……我想我终究可以找到问题的答案。”

text.en: Pepe, a renowned historian from Sargon with many tales of derring-do, is also the eldest daughter of a respected padishah. Now aiding Rhodes Island on a series of archaeological surveys in Sargon as a field operator.
text.zh: 佩佩，萨尔贡知名的历史学者，身世显赫，是萨尔贡一位尊贵帕夏的长女。现作为外勤干员协助罗德岛在萨尔贡当地进行一系列考古勘察。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Pepe shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.012u/L
Operator Pepe rarely comes into contact with Originium.

'Hard to believe, but while I was doing her medical exam, there was an etiquette officer by her side watching my every move.'
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员佩佩没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.012u/L
干员佩佩甚少接触源石。

“难以置信，为她体检时居然有专门的礼仪官在一旁盯着我的动作。”

text.en:
Once operators aboard the landship heard there was a padishah's daughter about to visit Rhodes Island, there was no stemming their curiosity. They eagerly awaited her formal arrival, all so that they could take a peek behind the veil, so to speak. But she did not arrive at Rhodes Island with her caravan and retinue of servants until six months later. She came aboard in extravagant fashion, starting with a gold-embroidered carpet rolled out from the ship's hatch down to the reception room, followed by rows of servant girls bearing flowers and feather fans, then a sedan chair covered in layer upon layer of muslin curtains carried by four strapping young men in golden robes. Finally, a near-endless procession of porters, each carrying a rare treasure or ancient text from Sargon.
It's a shame this distinguished guest was hidden behind so many layers of servants, fans, and curtains that nobody was able to catch even a glimpse of her. Only her voice came through, one that felt slightly familiar to some.
As the gaggle of operators began to lose all hope, a clumsy servant accidentally tripped over their own robes, causing the line of servants to collapse like dominoes while also pulling away the curtains on the sedan chair, exposing the girl within. She was certainly not like how they imagined. A baggy T-shirt, carelessly tied-up hair, thick tomes in hand and ink smudged all over her face. Nobody could recognize her.
Upon seeing the dumbfounded operators, she merely scratched her head and laughed awkwardly, quietly saying:
'Thought I could wear whatever I wanted considering the curtains, haha...'

It was at this point an operator handling registration remembered why the padishah's daughter has a voice sounded so familiar.
Three months ago, a girl came along with some field operators returning from Sargon, her body completely covered in mud and dust. Everyone thought she was a patient who had been rescued at first, but she cheerfully told the operator in charge to get registration done ASAP, since she had a caravan to another excavation site to catch.
Another operator working in the library also heard her voice often, as there was a collaborating operator with the Sargon office who would always come with a giant pile of books to return, then leave with another equally giant pile of materials.
But when asked about her appearance, none were able to answer.

'Didn't see, her face was caked in mud.'
'I didn't get a good look either, books always got in the way.'
'...If she's been registered, surely there's a photo in the system, right? Can you look it up?'
'Lemme see...'
'...'
'Dammit, who the hell swapped the photo out for some wacky selfie? There's a giant mustache scribbled all over it; you can't see what she looks like at all!'
text.zh:
舰船上的干员们知道有一位帕夏的女儿即将造访罗德岛，都不免怀着好奇心，急切地等待她正式到来的那天，想要一睹真容。但直到半年后，她才带着自己的车队与侍从抵达罗德岛。而她登上舰船的派头震撼了在场的每一个人，一条绣着金线的地毯从舱门一直铺设到会客厅，捧着鲜花与羽扇的侍女排成长长的队伍，在她们身后是一架垂着层层纱幔的轿子，由四位身着黄金礼服的力士抬着，而在轿子后，是长长的队列，携带了从萨尔贡远道而来的罕见珍宝与古老文本。
可惜的是，这位尊贵的客人始终被藏在重重侍从、一把把羽毛扇，还有一层层不曾摘下的纱幔后，没人能一睹真容。只有她的声音，让人隐约觉得有些熟悉。
就在干员们暗自失落时，一位粗心的侍从不小心踩到衣角跌了一跤，导致长长的队伍像骨牌一样依次倒下，而轿子上的纱幔也被扯下，露出了里面坐着的女孩。与干员们的想象不同，她套了一件肥大的短袖，头发也只是胡乱扎起来，手里拿着厚厚的文件，黑色的墨水沾了一脸，没人能辨认她到底长什么模样。
见到呆愣的干员们，她只是挠头尴尬地笑笑，小声说了一句：
“我想有帘子挡着，就随便穿穿了……”

此时，一位报到处的干员想起了自己为何会觉得这位帕夏之女的声音耳熟。
三个月前，一个女孩跟着外勤干员从萨尔贡回来，身上没有一处干净的地方，全都是泥巴与尘土。在场所有人都以为她是被救助回来的病患，但她却神采奕奕地告诉报到处的干员，希望能尽快结束报到，她还要跟着下一支车队去另一个发掘现场。
而另一位图书室的干员也记起了这个自己常常听到的声音，有位萨尔贡办事处的合作干员每次回到舰上都会抱着厚厚的一摞书来还，而后又会带着厚厚的一沓资料离开。
但问到女孩的样貌时，几位干员却都支支吾吾答不上来。

“没看到哇……泥巴糊了一脸，什么也看不清。”
“我、我也不清楚，都被书挡住了。”
“……既然有登记，肯定录入过照片吧，能找到吗？”
“让我找找。”
“……”
“可恶，到底是什么人会把档案里的照片换成搞怪自拍啊？这两撇又黑又浓的八字胡画在脸上，完全看不出长什么样子嘛！”

text.en:
Pepe is rather fond of lotus flowers. The things in her room all sport some sort of lotus design. She even added a lotus sticker to her badge. Of the gifts she bestowed upon Rhodes Island, the most precious were lotus seeds. They were planted in the Convalescent Garden, and ever since, all operators can have the opportunity to appreciate their fragrance.
Her giant hammer also has a lotus seal engraved into it. Once heated up by the flame jet, it can leave behind a painful lesson for any enemy—a great big lotus brand.
It's not hard to see why, considering the lotus is the symbol of Pepe's family, Sargon's most ancient line of historians. Her ancestor once followed Shahanshah Lugalszargus on all his campaigns, and with reed pen in hand, they recorded every epic scene of that heroic age.
Ever since, her family would pick the best of each generation to serve the Shahanshah. With the same ancient reed pen, they would record the entirety of the titan that was Sargon, experiencing all they could before finally compiling it all into an addendum to the famous endless tome, 'The Book of Sargon.'
As her family's eldest daughter, Pepe has shown an unusually strong interest in history, always seeking to inherit her ancestor's duty to enter the City of Gold and pen the newest chapter of Sargon's history. However, her father preferred her quieter younger brother Senid. This was hard for her to accept. Once an adult, she strove to do all she could to contribute to historical research, all to prove to her father that she was qualified to be the court historian. But his heart was set on the matter, and while Pepe was at an archaeological dig, he sent Senid to the City.
This development has not upset Pepe. Though she no longer constantly mentions 'a historian's duty' like she used to, she still pursues historical research with zeal. Not only does she fund, participate in and lead excavations, she also contributes heavily to the preservation of relics. In only half a year, tomb robbers have learned to cower in the face of that lotus pattern.

[Audio Log]
I always ask myself, why am I so into researching history? Back then, I would have said 'obviously my family's influence'...
But now, I'm starting to think you're a reason too. Ever since we were young, we'd study together, play together, scribble in the books together, recite texts as punishment from Father together... Safe to say that sitting at your desk and reading some dusty tome is super boring as a kid, but since you were there, time kinda just flew past while we bickered.
Historian... I'm not too interested in the position anymore. Now that you're in the City of Gold, I dunno when we can see each other again. I wonder... If I make some huge discovery... Maybe you'll read my paper on it, and that'll count as seeing each other...
Senid... It's been so long. I-If we see each other again, I'll... I'll give you a right trashing.
—Pepe babbling to herself after getting drunk
text.zh:
干员佩佩对莲花极为偏爱，她房间内的物品全都印有莲花图案，甚至她的工牌上也贴着莲花贴纸。而她带给罗德岛的礼物中，最为珍贵的便是几颗莲花种子，后来栽种在疗养庭院，每位干员都可以领略到它的特殊香味。
就连她常用的巨锤上，也镶着一枚莲花纹章，经底部的火焰喷射器加热后，可以给敌人留下深痛的教训——一个巨大的莲花烙印。
不难理解，因为莲花图案正代表着干员佩佩的家族——一个萨尔贡最古老的史官家族。她的祖先曾追随着万王之王路加萨尔古斯征战四方，用灯芯草笔记录下那段波澜壮阔的英雄岁月。
其后，她的家族都会选出一名最优秀的后代随侍在历代万王之王身侧，他们用那支古老的灯芯草笔记录下了这个巨人般的国家，在此后时光中所历经的种种，最后全部集录在了那本举世闻名的浩瀚典籍《萨尔贡史》中。
作为家中的长女，佩佩从小就对历史表现出了非凡的兴趣，一直期待着可以继承祖先的史官职责，进入黄金之城为王国的历史记录新的篇章，可是她的父亲却更加属意她性格文静的胞弟塞尼德。这让佩佩难以接受，成年后她便致力于在史学研究上有所建树，只为向父亲证明自己也能胜任史官的职务，但其父心意已决，在佩佩外出进行考古研究时，将塞尼德送入了黄金之城。
佩佩并未因此一蹶不振，虽然她不再像以往那般总将“史官职责”挂在嘴边，但她对历史研究依然充满热忱，不仅资助、参与并主导了多项考古发掘活动，还在文物保护方面作出了众多贡献，短短半年里，那枚莲花图案几乎让所有盗墓贼胆寒。

【语音记录】
我总问自己，为什么会对钻研历史感兴趣？以前理所当然地觉得是家族氛围的熏陶嘛……
但现在看来，你也是原因之一啦。从小到大，我们一起学习，一起玩耍，一起在书上乱涂乱画，然后一起被父亲罚背书……按理说，小小年纪坐在桌子前啃大部头是件很枯燥的事……但因为有你在，时间在打打闹闹中好像很快就过去了。
史官……那个位置对我的吸引力已经没有那么大了，你进入黄金之城，也不知道什么时候能再见，我想……要是我能有个大发现……说不定你可以看到我写下的东西，这也算是见上一面了……
塞尼德……这么久没见，再、再见你的时候我可得好好……好好揍你一顿。
——喝醉酒后对着空气碎碎念的干员佩佩

text.en:
Don't mention anything to do with Shahanshah Lugalszargus while talking to Pepe. This was something everyone on the landship quickly learned. There was once an unlucky operator who barely even hinted at this king and his tales during a pre-dinner chat. Pepe then shoved them into a chair and proceed to talk about his glorious deeds for the entire night. From his birth to his ascension to the throne, up until his disappearance alongside Kharanduu Khagan in the foehn hotlands... The piteous soul was trapped until the light of dawn peeked over the horizon, unable to get a word in edgewise, reduced to staring blankly at Pepe's lips as they flapped about in excitement. That operator remembered it as such:
'My mind was completely blank. She kept saying things like 'this is a portrait of the Shah, very handsome I'd say, here, have a look—', then she'd take out a photo album with hundreds of pages and make sure I looked at each and every page real close.
'When she was talking about that shah's life, it was like her eyes were glowing. All I wanted to know is where the Shahanshah actually went in the end... I didn't need to know about how he and Kharanduu Khagan drank, then fought, then drank after they fought...'
It's hard to blame Pepe for her adoration of Lugalszargus. The king holds an exalted position in the hearts of Sargonians. Every child falls asleep to his tales, many cities have statues of him, and countless texts cite his words. There is an unending stream of scholars looking into the riddles he left behind, and Pepe is one of the foremost among them. Her research not only portrays Lugalszargus as a great conqueror and military genius, but also him as a son, husband, and father, aspects often overshadowed by his radiant deeds as king.
These past few years have seen Pepe wander all over Sargon, reconstructing those who stood by the king's side from time-worn carvings and phrases—loyal retainers, concubines who died tragically young, as well as a prince who stood vigil by his grave in the wake of his departure and a princess who wrote a full account of his life. They were forgotten by history, but thanks to Pepe's efforts, they have seen renewed attention in academia.

[Audio Log]
True, compared to the Shah's military brilliance, they're basically nobodies when it comes to historical influence. But they all had a deep emotional connection with him. It's these private, moving feelings that round out the Shah, and allow the past to resonate with us now. I believe that no matter the era, genuine bonds will survive history's forward march, shining for all eternity.
—A summary of one of Pepe's reports
text.zh:
不要和佩佩聊起有关万王之王路加萨尔古斯的事迹，这是舰船上所有人的共识。曾有干员只是在吃饭前和她提了一句有关这位君王的逸闻，便被佩佩按在椅子上听了一整晚他的光辉事迹，从出生到即位，再到与哈兰杜汗一同消失在焚风热土……一直到窗外天际泛白，可怜的干员都没能插上一句话来打断她，只能眼睁睁地看着佩佩的嘴唇翕动不停。对此，那位干员这样回忆道：
“我的大脑当时一片空白，她口中不停说着‘这是沙阿留下的肖像画，非常帅气，你快看……’，然后拿出一本画册，几百多页，每一页都一定要我仔细观看。
“当她讲到那位沙阿的一生时，眼睛简直就是在放光，我只想知道万王之王最后到底去了哪里……我不想知道他和哈兰杜汗到底是怎么喝完酒打架，打完架又喝酒的……”
不怪佩佩对路加萨尔古斯如此崇拜，在萨尔贡，这位君王的地位非比寻常。每个孩子伴着他的传说进入梦乡，众多城市竖立着他的雕像，无数典籍引用过他的言辞，更有源源不断的学者研究他留下的一个个谜团，而佩佩，正是他们中极为优秀的存在。她的研究不仅展示了路加萨尔古斯身为伟大征服者与军事天才的光辉形象，还发掘了被掩盖在王者光芒下他作为儿子、丈夫与父亲的另一面。
这些年，佩佩走访萨尔贡各处，从被时间剥蚀过的只言片语中，她还原出一些王者身旁的人物——忠心耿耿的侍从、早逝的妃子，以及在他离去后为他守灵的王子和一位将他的生平记述在史书中的公主……他们都曾被历史遗忘，又经佩佩的研究重新进入现今学界的视野。

【语音记录】
诚然，比起沙阿的赫赫威名，他们在历史中的形象无限接近于小人物，但他们每个人都与沙阿有着深厚的情感连接，正是这些私密的、动人的情愫，让沙阿的形象更加丰满，也让那个时代同如今遥相辉映。我相信，无论时代如何更迭，历史如何前进，真挚的情谊都会世代相传，永不磨灭。
——佩佩在某次报告中做出的总结

text.en:
As the one in charge of guiding Hatshepsut Hanim, I made my way down to the excavation site in the south of Sargon. Though dusk was about to set, the ruins were abuzz with workers scurrying about, laying down rain tarps above the excavation pits. It seems a rare rainstorm was about to hit.
When night fell, the storm arrived as expected. While others were falling sleep to the sound of raindrops pattering against the tarps, Hatshepsut Hanim put on her raincoat and set out, checking every part of the site to make sure not a single corner was overlooked during the covering. A sharp piece of rubble had torn her coat, and it was not until I offered her a new one that she realized she was soaked to the bone. After thanking me, she did not return to her quarters, but instead enthusiastically offered to show me around the site. I accepted, and we entered the ruins together.
There were only stumps of walls and pillars within, but they were enough for a peek into the past. The scene below the tarp showed a master of a garden enjoying a drink, the deep red within their cup proving the maturity of the wine industry at the time. The ruts in the stone pavement beneath my feet reminded me that this was once a thriving hub with carts passing back and forth incessantly. On the way back, Hatshepsut Hanim explained the discoveries found within the ruins while leading me to their edge. There, she revealed her most astonishing find yet.
At the end of a path, she lifted up a tarp close to the ground. I expected to see some priceless treasure, but within the pit all I saw were two even footprints embedded in the soil, one large, one small.
Noticing my confusion, she began to explain the principles behind the formation of these footprints. As she spoke, I began to imagine the distant past, walking alongside the footprints' makers as they wandered the city and enjoyed the fresh air and greenery, at least until some natural disaster or the other sealed their footprints in the mud for all eternity.
I still remember the last part of her speech:
'Preserving these footprints means preserving a beautiful, fleeting moment, in which these people will live on forever more. They will pass through the desert, walking into the distance...
'Far, far away...'

[News Clipping]
On the fourteenth of this month, the Padishah's wife Hati passed away after giving birth to her child in the hospital. She was mourned by all her people.
The funeral was held in the Padishah's residence on the twentieth, and she was buried in the garden she so loved in a private ceremony. She once mentioned during an interview that she was happiest when running barefoot through the garden with her daughter. Sadly, we can now only witness the tragic sight of her daughter carrying her baby brother while they mourn.
That day, countless citizens gathered in the streets to offer lotus flowers outside the Padishah's residence, enough to form small mountains of blossoms...

[Garden Closure Notice]
From this day forth, the garden will be forever closed. Do not enter without permission. Trespassers will be punished.
Date: ■■■ 21st ■■■■
text.zh:
在负责人哈特谢普苏特女士的带领下，我来到了她在萨尔贡南部的考古发掘现场，虽然黄昏将至，但古城遗址中仍是一派忙碌的气象——在场所有人正迅速但有序地扯开雨布，铺设在发掘坑的上方，以应对当地难得一遇的降雨天气。
夜晚，暴雨如期而至，其他人都伴着雨滴掉在篷布上的噼啪声入睡，但哈特谢普苏特女士还是穿着雨披，在遗址中检查是否有遗漏的地方。尖利的残石将她的雨披刮破，但她浑然不觉，直到我送上新的雨披，她才发现自己的衣服与头发早已湿透。表达过感激后，哈特谢普苏特女士没有离开，反而饶有兴趣地问我想不想参观发掘现场，我接受了邀请，与她一起深入遗址。
遗址内只剩下低矮的残桩，但依旧能够窥见它昔日的风光。雨布下的镶嵌画展示了花园主人的畅饮时光，杯中浓烈的紫红色表明了当时葡萄酒的酿制工艺已经臻于成熟，而脚下石板路上的车辙印提醒我，这里曾有车辆川流不息。路上，哈特谢普苏特女士边为我讲解遗址内的发现，边带着我往遗址外部走去，在那里，她将展示自己最惊人的成果。
在小路的尽头，哈特谢普苏特女士揭开地面上的雨布，我期待底下藏着价值非凡的文物，但只有两串均匀的脚印被时光拓印在土地上，一大一小。
看我不解，她解释起了脚印形成的原理。伴着她的讲解，我仿佛回到了那已不可考的过去，陪同脚印的主人漫步在城郊，享受清新的植物气息，直到一场自然灾害将这一刻永恒地封存在泥土中。
我还记得她最后和我说的话：
“保存下这两串脚印，就好像能保存下注定会流逝的一个美好瞬间，而脚印的主人，他们会活在这永恒的瞬间，穿过沙漠，走得远远的……
“远远的……”

【新闻摘选】
本月十四日，帕夏的妻子哈蒂在医院产下一子后不幸去世，她的离世引起了所有人的悲伤。
葬礼于本月二十日在帕夏的宫殿中举行，她在私人的仪式中被葬入生前最爱的花园。她曾在采访中透露，自己最惬意的时光就是与女儿光着脚在草坪嬉戏，但如今我们只能看到她的女儿抱着刚出生不久的弟弟为她哀悼。
当天，无数民众走上街道，为她献上的莲花在宫殿外堆成小山……

【花园封闭通知】
从今日起，花园将永久封闭，未经许可不得擅闯，违者重罚。
■■■■年■■月二十一日

text.en:
'Ahahaha, oh man, it hurts to laugh this much. Are these guys serious? A secret cabal of Savra in the jungles of Sargon, manipulating the governments of every country from the shadows... Haha, does this hack historian even know what he's writing?'
You look at the girl giddy with glee in front of you and don't know why. You look once more at the stack of books on the table and pull out a few at random, wanting to know what she's even laughing at. Upon seeing their titles, you become even more perplexed.
'Exploring the Foehn Hotlands: Eternal Soldiers of the Sands'
'Undying Immortal Sages'
'A Romantic History of Lugalszargus: The Secret Passions of the Once and Future Shah'
...
You help pull the girl up from the ground, her face contorted in a mixture of howling laughter and pain. The pain is echoed on your face as she grabs your arm tightly, twisting it as she rises. As you wonder what to do, Kal'tsit comes to both your rescues, supporting the girl laughing so hard she can barely breathe while freeing your arm from her vice grip.
Relieved, you throw the books you're holding into the trash can.
'The Shahanshah's secret passions? They couldn't even get the years right. Definitely not trustworthy.'
What you don't notice, though, is that some of these ridiculous texts seem to have gone missing from the pile.
text.zh:
“啊哈哈哈哈，真的笑死我了，这群人到底是怎么想的？起源于萨尔贡雨林的秘密萨弗拉社团，组成了影子政府暗中操控各国政府……哈哈，这野史作家知道自己到底在写什么吗？”
你看着眼前乐不可支的少女，觉得疑惑，再看看桌上的那一沓资料，从中随机抽了几份，想知道她到底因何发笑。当看到上面的标题时，你变得更加疑惑。
《探秘焚风热土：永不消逝的战士鬼影》
《长生不死的贤者》
《路加萨尔古斯艳史：揭秘伟大君王的情感道路》
……
你扶起趴在地上的少女，她因为无法停下狂笑面露痛苦，而你的表情也因为她抓着你胳膊的力道而扭曲起来。就在你不知该如何是好时，凯尔希的出现解救了你们二人，她扶走了笑得上气不接下气的女孩，也让你的胳膊逃离了被捏断的危险。
松了一口气的你随手将手中的资料丢进垃圾桶。
“万王之王的情史？这份资料连年份都是错的，完全不可信。”
但你并没有注意到，充斥着荒诞言论的资料其实少了那么几份。
