infectionStatus.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为非感染者。

text.en: Delphine, formerly an active intelligence officer in Norport for many years, later participating in a series of military campaigns near Londinium as a member of the Exemplars. After the Victoria incident, she worked out a number of cooperative strategic agreements with Rhodes Island to assist the Victorian branch office.
text.zh: 戴菲恩，曾作为情报人员在诺伯特区活动多年，后以典范军成员的身份参与了伦蒂尼姆周边的一系列战役。在维多利亚事件结束后，同罗德岛达成了一系列战略合作条款，为罗德岛驻维多利亚办事处提供协助。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, the operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Delphine shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.14u/L
Operator Delphine's BOCD is on the high side, and the fighting in Londinium must have affected her health to some degree. She needs to be extra careful to lower her risk of contracting Oripathy.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员戴菲恩没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.14u/L
干员戴菲恩血液源石结晶密度偏高，在伦蒂尼姆的作战一定程度上影响了她的健康，需额外注意矿石病感染风险的控制。

text.en:
Delphine is the daughter of Victoria's famous Duke of Windermere, and first in line to the title. This is practically an open secret in Rhodes Island. 
We have plenty of operators with status and power, but even among them, the authority Delphine wields—or perhaps we should say 'could wield'—is still an extraordinary case. No matter how Victoria is perceived today, being the heir to a truly powerful dukedom implies being able to command an entire fleet of high-speed battleships, having full control over the territory, and access to a considerable amount of wealth. However, Delphine seems to have voluntarily given up all of these enviable resources. The only things she has kept for herself appear to be the coat embroidered with the Windermere name and the saber left by her mother. 
Nowadays, other than the training room, she spends most of her time on Rhodes Island consulting a variety of travel guides and well-traveled operators. She carefully notes down valuable information and researches the best routes, just like a seasoned backpacker. However, she does not seem to have any passion for sightseeing, as neither the natural nor cultural tourist attractions that ordinary travelers flock to are ever a priority in her plans. She has not divulged much detail about her itinerary, but one thing we are sure of is that she seems to prefer visiting more chaotic regions that most prefer to avoid. 

Delphine and I talked a bunch about fun places and delicious shops near my place! But most people don't pay special attention to places like metallurgical factories and mines when they're plannin' a travel route, aye? ——Bagpipe 
Mm-hmm, the habits of a workaholic. Understandable. ——Harmonie
text.zh:
戴菲恩是维多利亚那位著名的温德米尔公爵之女，也是其爵位的第一顺位继承人，这在罗德岛上几乎是一个公开的秘密。
罗德岛的干员中并不缺乏地位显赫、身世富贵之人，但戴菲恩的权势，或者说，本可获得的权势仍是其中顶尖的。不论世人如何看待如今的维多利亚，一位实权公爵的继承人往往意味着能指挥数量庞大的高速军舰、在领地内说一不二的威权以及相当可观的财富。但据我们观察，戴菲恩似乎自愿放弃了这一切让人艳羡的资源。那件绣有姓氏“温德米尔”的大衣和她母亲留下的佩剑，似乎是她唯一留给自己与过去有关的东西。
如今，戴菲恩在罗德岛上的时间，除了花在训练室里，大部分都用在了查阅各种旅行指南以及与那些惯于在路上跋涉的干员闲聊上。她细心地记录下每条值得注意的信息，研究最好的旅行路线，简直和一个资深背包客没什么区别。不过，她似乎对自然风景与人文景观的兴趣都不算强烈，这些一般旅行者趋之若鹜的景点，反而不是戴菲恩行程规划里的第一选择。至于她自己的行程规划，戴菲恩并没有向我们透露很多，唯一可以确定的是，她似乎更愿意造访那些多数人选择绕开的混乱区域。

我和戴菲恩说了不少我家附近好玩的地方和好吃的小店！不过，一般做旅行攻略的时候，会格外留意冶金厂和矿场之类的在什么位置吗？——风笛
哼哼，职业病嘛，可以理解。——和弦

text.en:
Delphine rarely talks about her past, but sometimes she tells her friends from the Glasgow gang about the summers she spent as a child at Lynncardine. 
Lynncardine is located on Victoria's northeastern border with Leithanien. It is Victoria's military stronghold and the most important nomadic city in the Duke of Windermere's demesne—these descriptions often conjure an image of a stark and daunting nomadic fortress, but Delphine describes the place is completely differently. 
Naturally, since it is her hometown. 
She will speak of a small lake that shows up on the road to the city. Only during the summer do the city's denizens have the privilege to catch a glimpse of its always-clear waters. She will also mention a strange tree by the lake, and the seven or eight insect species one can find in June. Sometimes the city comes close to a woodland in summer, and she will always enthusiastically list off every type of tree one can find whenever she mentions it. Also, when Lynncardine sails into the shadow of a mountain, or when it heads toward a huge raincloud... 
There is no doubt that Delphine spent the best moments of her childhood there. But no fragment of these memories matches what we'd expect from 'a Duke's successor.' The Duke of Windermere was known in Victorian aristocratic circles for her strictness, and many speculated that even her heirs would be spared no quarter. Delphine's adeptness at combat and the calluses on her hands are proof her mother did indeed have high expectations of her. But on the other hand, her mother also wished to protect her daughter's smile more than she wanted to prepare her successor to become the next Duke by shuttling her between banquets and military camps as the Duke of Windermere. 
Perhaps precisely because she knew that her child would find it difficult to earnestly raise the corners of her lips again, upon inheriting her responsibilities.
text.zh:
戴菲恩极少谈起自己过去的经历。但她有时会和格拉斯哥帮的朋友们聊起她小时候在丽茵卡登度过的那些夏天。
丽茵卡登位于维多利亚的东北部边境，紧邻莱塔尼亚，是维多利亚的军事重镇，也是温德米尔公爵领地内最重要的移动城市——当有关丽茵卡登的这些说明摆放出来的时候，人们的脑海中往往会浮现出的是一座森严的、让人望而却步的移动堡垒，但在戴菲恩的描述中，却截然不同。
当然，那里是她的故乡。
戴菲恩会说起丽茵卡登航线上的那片小湖，一年中只有夏天的那几个月，城市中的人们才能有幸窥见永远澄澈的湖水。她也会说起湖边那棵古怪的树，说起六月才能找到的那七八种昆虫。有时候，夏天的丽茵卡登也会接近林地，戴菲恩谈起那片林地时总是兴致勃勃，一一将树的种类数过。还有丽茵卡登驶进群山阴影中的时刻，丽茵卡登航向一片巨大的雨云的时刻……
毫无疑问，戴菲恩在那里度过了自己童年中最美好的那些时光。但这些回忆中，却似乎并没有什么与“公爵继承人”相衬的片段。在维多利亚的贵族圈子里，温德米尔公爵以严厉著称，许多人猜测她对自己的继承者也同样苛刻。戴菲恩手上的老茧与娴熟的战斗技巧证明了她母亲确实没有放松对她的要求，但另一方面，相比于以公爵的身份让自己的继承者来往于宴会与军营，为“成为下一个公爵”早早做好准备，戴菲恩的母亲更希望自己的女儿能尽可能长久地露出笑容。
也许，这正是因为温德米尔公爵知道，当责任真正落下，一位公爵的孩子就很难再度发自内心地扬起嘴角了。

text.en:
[Classified Log] 
The chaos erupting in several counties under Windermere came as no surprise to us. 
After the Duke was KIA, all her troops retreated from Londinium's frontlines, effectively withdrawing from the war. The nomadic fortresses sent to the frontlines were also called back. According to several statements from Lynncardine, Duke Amphelise Windermere and her heir, Delphine Windermere, died on the battlefields near Londinium. Several factions with succession rights have begun competing for control over Windermere's demesne, and one can see the various supporters behind their backs: traditional military corporations, other Victorian dukes, and even Leithanien's Kurfürsten. 
But Delphine shows a rather negative attitude toward the situation in Windermere, reluctant to return to Lynncardine or to use her identity to regain any faction's support. She told us she would not use any connections or assets available to her as Windermere's successor, and that Lynncardine has nothing to do with what she plans to do next. 

This archive includes a recorded conversation approved by the concerned parties: 
Enough asking, Hannah. I'm not going back. I know you mean well, but I won't change my mind. It's not because I think I'm not up for it, or that I'm afraid of giving myself all that trouble. I know all too well how to play those political games, win over a few people, suppress a few more, and promise another few some benefits... Don't forget, I've spent a considerable number of years doing intelligence work. 
The question is: Do I want to continue playing these games? 
Of course I love my mother and father who dedicated their lives to the demesne, and I don't want to deny their efforts, but we've seen how everything ended. Lynncardine's savior won't be me, or any one person, that's just not possible. I'd rather do more concrete work, to kill the specific culprits instead of continuing to get myself hopelessly entangled with those conspirators as a 'Duke's daughter' or a 'Duke.' 
That's how I feel about Lynncardine, and Victoria too. Don't underestimate the people living there, they can make their own choices. What they need are not leaders, but companions. 
I'm one of you guys, part of the Exemplars. We help everyone we meet with practical work, and it'd be no different even if I took on some kind of position. 
We praise those who 'take up responsibility,' but whoever said that responsibility requires entering the palace?
text.zh:
【权限记录】
温德米尔公爵领所辖数个郡的混乱并没有出乎我们的意料。
在温德米尔公爵战死后，她的所有部队都撤出了伦蒂尼姆的前线，从事实上退出了这场战争，曾开赴前线的移动要塞也被撤回。在数条来自丽茵卡登的声明中，公爵安费莉丝·温德米尔以及她的继承人戴菲恩·温德米尔都死在了伦蒂尼姆周边的战场上。数个拥有爵位继承权的势力已经开始争夺对于温德米尔领的控制权，能从他们的背后看到不少支持者的影子，包括传统军事集团、其他维多利亚大公爵，乃至莱塔尼亚的选帝侯们。
但戴菲恩却对温德米尔领的局势表露出了比较消极的一面，她并没有急于重回丽茵卡登，也无意于利用自己的身份重新获得任何势力的支持。她告诉我们，她不会动用任何温德米尔公爵继承人这个身份带给她的人脉和财产，她接下来的计划也与丽茵卡登无关。

在获得本人的允许之后，档案收录了一段戴菲恩的谈话：
汉娜，别再问了，我不会回去的，我知道这是你的好意，但我不会改变主意的。这并不是因为我自认能力不足，或者害怕惹上那些麻烦事。我很清楚怎么去玩那些政治把戏，拉拢几个人，打压几个人，再给几个人许诺些好处……别忘了，我可是做了不少年情报工作的。
问题是，我还要继续这种游戏吗？
我爱戴我的母亲和父亲，他们为领地奉献了一生，我一点也不想否定他们的努力，但我们已经看到这一切的结果了。拯救丽茵卡登的不会是我，也不会是任何一个具体的人，没有人能做到这一点。我更愿意去做那些具体的事情，去杀死那些具体的罪恶，而不是继续以“公爵之女”或者“公爵”的身份，同那些阴谋家纠缠不清。
对丽茵卡登是这样，对维多利亚也是这样。别小瞧生活在那里的人们，他们会自己做出选择，他们需要的不是领导者，而是同伴。
我是你们的一员，我是典范军的一员，我们在用实际行动帮助每个我们遇到的人，这和承担什么职务相比，其实并没有区别。
我们称颂那些“担起责任”的人，但这种责任，未必就是进入宫殿之中。

text.en:
An unsent letter: 
Don't worry, Mum. I'm doing fine here. 
I'll be heading out again soon, to Castshire County this time. I still have no plans to return to Lynncardine just yet, and there's no way I can see you in person, so all I can do is to write you a letter about my current situation. 
I'm still in Norport, and the reconstruction work here is going pretty smoothly. The 'Slobberknocker' has reopened, and Hannah made a vow to make it the best in Victoria. I have no doubts about that. We paid Baird a visit too, and Morgan wanted to bring her some new tapes. I know she liked going over to the video shop just to sleep, and not for a love of movies, but as long as they're happy, I'm fine with that. Baird would definitely be glad to know that we plan to reopen the place in a while after saving up enough money, and we'll always leave a chair out for her. 
I've seen so many things these days, so much more than I ever saw on my trips with Papa. I'm starting to realize that I don't really know the country I grew up in. I learned how crude ale is brewed, and that people go door-to-door buying burdenbeast dung to use as fuel. I learned too little from you and Papa, but it's also because of this that I feel I've made the right choice. 
Two days ago, I dug out an old photo that I must have used as a bookmark and brought all the way to Londinium. I already forget how old I was back then, but Papa was holding up a huge fin with both hands while you were holding onto my shoulders with a scowl on my face—probably because that was yet another vacation that ended early. It was only then that we were nobodies, and nothing happened. 
I really miss you, Mum.
text.zh:
一封尚未寄出的信：
妈妈，不用担心，我的生活很好。
我很快就又会出发，这次的目标是开夏郡。我还是不打算马上就回丽茵卡登，也就没办法当面去见你，所以，我只能写信给你，说说我的近况。
我还是在诺伯特区落了脚，这里的重建进行得很不错。“揍歪下巴”拳馆重新开业了，汉娜发誓要把这里变成维多利亚最好的拳馆，我对此倒是毫不怀疑。我们也去看了贝尔德，摩根想给她带点新的录像带。我知道贝尔德喜欢去录像厅并不是喜欢看电影，她每次去那里只是为了睡觉，但她们乐意就好。过段时间，等我们攒了足够的钱，我们打算让那家录像厅重新开业，贝尔德一定会为我们这个计划高兴，我们永远会给她留一个座位。
我这些日子里见过了很多东西，比以往我和爸爸旅行时见的还要多得多。我开始发现，我并不那么了解这个我生长的国家，我第一次知道粗麦酒是怎么酿的，也第一次知道会有人挨家挨户收购驮兽粪便当燃料。我曾经在你和爸爸身边学到的东西，还是太少。但也正因为如此，我也越发确定我的选择是正确的。
前两天，我翻出了一张照片，大概是被我当作书签夹在了书里，一路带到了伦蒂尼姆。我已经忘记了那是我几岁的时候，照片里爸爸捧着一条大鳞，你搂着我的肩膀，我却一副闹别扭的表情——大概因为那又是一个提前结束的假期。只有在那个时候，我们谁也不是，一切也都没有发生。
妈妈，我真的很想你。

text.en:
The doctor's seen your mum. She told me she's injured, but she'll wake up in no time. 
'I know how you feel. You're thinking: if only you were stronger, less hesitant, if you hadn't been slacking on your training, if you'd walked a different path... would your mum be fine now? 
'But... there's no way to change what's already happened. Your mum put herself out there to protect you, so if you want to repay her for that, then you have to become stronger, strong enough to stand in front of her the next time she's in danger. 
'So, don't cry anymore. She's waiting for you to grow up and protect her too, you know!' 
After the Londinium incident concluded, Delphine rescued a mother and daughter duo at the Victorian border who survived a bandit raid. She handed the seriously injured and comatose woman over to the doctor, and held the incessantly crying girl in her arms, spending the entire night calming her down until she finally fell asleep at dawn.
text.zh:
“那个医生姐姐已经来看过你的妈妈了，她说，你妈妈虽然受了伤，但很快就能醒过来了。
“我明白你的感觉，你觉得，如果那时自己再强大一些，再稳重一些，如果不在以前的训练里悄悄偷懒，如果当时换了条路……是不是妈妈就会没事了呢？
“但……已经发生的事情就没有办法改变了。你妈妈为了保护你挺身而出，如果你想回报她，那么，你就在以后变得足够厉害，厉害到再遇到危险的时候，能挡在妈妈的身前。
“所以，一定不要哭了哦，你妈妈也等着你长大之后去保护她呢！”
伦蒂尼姆事件结束之后，戴菲恩在维多利亚的边境解救了一对在劫匪袭击中幸存的母女，在把重伤昏迷的母亲交给医生后，她抱着那个啼哭不止的女孩，从半夜哄到了黎明，女孩才终于安稳睡去。

value.en: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.
value.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为非感染者。

infectionStatus.en: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.
infectionStatus.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为非感染者。

text.en:
A Victorian viscount belonging to a branch of House Caster. His house holds territory in the northern parts of Victoria and is known for their martial prowess. A veteran soldier, having led troops against the remnants of Gaul and answered the Duke of Caster's call to war, he is also an experienced field medic.
Harold joined Rhodes Island of his own volition following the disclosure of the above information. At his own request, he currently serves as a medic in various operations.
text.zh:
维多利亚的子爵，属开斯特家族旁支。领地位于维多利亚中北部，在开斯特一系中颇负武名。本人常年率领领地中的征召军对抗高卢残党，且时常响应开斯特公爵的号召出征，拥有极为丰富的战争经验，以及在这个过程中磨练而来的临床医疗经验。
——在公示了以上身份信息后，哈洛德以个人身份志愿加入罗德岛。并且，出于本人的坚持，现作为医疗干员活跃于各类任务中。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Harold shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L
Operator Harold rarely comes into contact with Originium.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员哈洛德没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.12u/L
干员哈洛德甚少接触源石。

text.en: Regardless of what impression Harold's background left on Rhodes Island leadership, his arrival certainly left an impression on many operators. The sight of a well-dressed Victorian noble who had just elegantly introduced himself in impeccable King's Victorian bringing out a burdenbeast foal and introducing it with a completely different level of passion is bound to leave an indelible mark on the memory. The first thing he did after that was request a burdenbeast pen. While there was some befuddlement over him claiming to be a veterinarian, it soon became clear that he was serious about being a vet here, given how much time he spends in the pen and the number of veterinary and ecology-related papers he has published in Rhodes Island's internal newsgroup. Today, his name is widely known amongst Rhodes Island's pet owners, who have seen their beloved pets become happier and healthier under Harold's care, and learned more about animals under his tutelage. Not everything has been smooth sailing for him at Rhodes Island, however. It was a sunny afternoon, and Harold was explaining burdenbeast facts to operators visiting the pen. He asked for a volunteer to demonstrate milking, and he got one: Siege, who happened to be at Rhodes Island that day. For the first time since he arrived, Harold looked uncomfortable. Though he quickly recovered and began instructing her on milking, it was obvious to everyone that his movements were stiffer than usual. Very well, I admit it, I was startled at first. But then I realized I was just an old man who came here to get his men's illnesses treated and enjoy some peace and quiet. What Her Royal Highness gets up to and where is none of my business, is it? Oh, Her Royal Hi—I mean, Siege said she was interested in the habits of burdenbeasts. I should get the materials together now. Ta-ta!
text.zh:
不论哈洛德的背景给罗德岛上层带来的印象，他本人的到来，对许多罗德岛干员来说也是颇具冲击性的。
毕竟，一个衣冠楚楚的维多利亚贵族在用一串标准到不能再标准的维多利亚语进行自我介绍后，再牵出一头幼年驮兽并一改刚才的优雅，以一种热情的态度进行介绍时，那种强烈的反差，任谁都难以忘记。
在那之后，他立即申请了一间中型的养殖间，用于养殖驮兽，虽然一开始大部分人对于他自称是兽医感到有些茫然，但是看到他每日频繁地进出养殖间，并且一篇又一篇与动物医疗以及生态相关的论文在罗德岛内部的论坛上发表，越来越多的人开始意识到，哈洛德似乎是真的想要在这里发展兽医业务。
如今，哈洛德已经成了饲养宠物的干员们之中的名人，他们的宠物不仅在哈洛德的照料下焕发了比以往更旺盛的活力，而且，在哈洛德的教导下，这些干员本身对于动物的理解也在不断提升。
不过，他在罗德岛的生活也并不总是顺风顺水。
那是个阳光明媚的午后，哈洛德像往常一样，在养殖间中对着那些来见习或者凑热闹的干员滔滔不绝地讲述着有关驮兽的知识。
在讲到挤奶的时候，他询问干员们之中是否有志愿者，而走出人群的那一个，是恰好在那天返回罗德岛的推进之王。
接下来的场面显得有些滑稽，哈洛德第一次在干员们面前表现得有些狼狈。虽然他很快反应了过来并开始指导推进之王挤奶，但在场的所有人都看得出来，他的动作和平时相比有些僵硬。

好吧，我承认，一开始我确实有点愣住了。不过，转念一想，我只是个来给部下治病顺便疗养的小老头，高贵的殿下出现在哪里和我又有什么关系？哦，推进之王殿——呃，推进之王小姐还说对驮兽的习性挺感兴趣的，我要去准备准备我的课件了，再会！

text.en:
[Operation Log]
May 23
Doctor told me that Harold's family asked us to keep a close eye on his sleep and diet, and especially to limit his alcohol intake. I was therefore asked to have a look at his room at night.
I had said hi to him earlier in the evening, when I saw him heading into his room from the corridor, so I thought he'd gone to bed when I saw a bump under the blanket, only to realize that it was a pillow and that he had snuck out.
I frantically searched everywhere, only to find him in the cafeteria, where he was drinking with the soldiers he brought with him to Rhodes Island. I was fuming, of course, but he didn't seem the slightest bit agitated when he saw me, instead calling me over.
They explained that one of the soldiers had been having nightmares of the war. Harold told me that he put the pillow there so I wouldn't worry. They'd gotten up in the middle of the night to comfort their comrade by having a drink with him.
I sat down with them and listened to their war stories, and how their comrade came down with his condition. It was moving.
Harold said they didn't drink because they wanted to; they drank to drown their sorrows. I can't help but feel sorry for them. Maybe I can talk to the Doctor, see if we can relax things a little...

Come to the control room and check out the security footage, when you can. They were very much enjoying themselves until they noticed you, at which point they exchanged a look and put on that pity play. Then they started partying again as soon as you left.
Can't have been the first time they put on that act either, given how smooth the whole thing was. No wonder the Doctor gave me a heads-up.
- Closure

[Operation Log]
May 24
Thanks for the heads-up, Closure! I won't be fooled again.
Nothing happened today.

You might've fooled me too, if there weren't a few more hidden cameras Harold didn't know about.
You got so touched by their stories that you ended up drinking with them all night!
We need a different person on this job, Doctor. The kids don't stand a chance against these old slicksters.
- Closure
text.zh:
【执勤记录】
5月23日
博士告诉我，哈洛德先生的家人请我们多多关注他的饮食和作息，尤其是不能让他过量饮酒，特地请我们在夜晚检查他的宿舍，我就去看了一眼。
傍晚的时候我还在走廊和他打了个招呼，看他是往自己的宿舍去，所以我以为他已经睡下了。看到被子鼓起来时，我原本要走了，结果仔细看看，发现那竟然只是一个枕头，他不知道在什么时候溜出去了！
我赶紧去找他，找到一半，听到食堂那边有动静，过去一看，发现他正在和他带上罗德岛治病的士兵兄弟喝酒，我本来有点生气，但他见到我之后也没有很慌张，反而向我招手，让我过去。
我凑过去才发现气氛不是很对，听他们解释，原来其中一位士兵兄弟精神上有些紧张，做了和战场有关的噩梦。哈洛德告诉我说，枕头的事只是因为不想让我操心，他们几个半夜起来就是为了安慰这个兄弟。而他们兄弟之间互相安慰的方式，就是喝点小酒。
他们拉着我坐下，给我讲了一些他们战场上的往事，也讲了这位士兵兄弟为什么会得病，听得我也挺感动的。
而且，听到哈洛德说，他们喝酒有的时候也不是自己想喝，只是需要找点东西麻痹自己，我也挺难受的，我打算和博士聊一聊，我们或许可以对他宽容一点……

来主控室，我可以给你看看当时的监控录像。他们一开始喝得可开心了，注意到你靠近以后，互相递了个眼神就开始摆出那副愁云惨淡的架势。把你骗走之后，他们又大喝特喝了起来。
一整套操作的流畅程度和演技之高超证明他们拿这套东西骗过不止一个人。难怪博士还给我提了个醒。
——可露希尔

【执勤记录】
5月24日
多亏了可露希尔小姐的提醒，今天要是再发生这种事，我一定不会上当的！
今日无事发生。

啧，如果不是哈洛德对罗德岛还不够了解，有几个隐蔽的机位他还没摸清楚，说不定还真被你们混过去了。
你小子根本就是被他们拉着听故事听感动了，然后陪他们喝了一宿！
博士，换人执勤吧，年轻人根本玩不过这群老油条的。
——可露希尔

text.en: 'General, I heard you plan to assault the pass from the front. May I offer my opinion?' 'You're that medic they were talking about? Are you questioning my strategy?' 'No, of course not, just making a few observations. See, this is the lay of the land, with one pass through the middle, and three tiny trails providing access from the side. 'If I were the enemy, and I was facing a commander known for her frontal assaults, I would strengthen my defense down the middle, while sending people down the trails to flank the enemy.' 'Makes sense. Are you suggesting I split the squad and send people to attack down the trails?' 'No, no, only third-rate tacticians think that variety is the ultimate goal of tactics. But only the most cunning can fool everyone, because you can't help but leave traces of their own work.' 'I don't get it.' 'It's simple. Would you be willing to split your squad if I suggested it?' 'No, that would be boring.' 'Exactly. I just wanted to remind you of the potential risks. As a leader, you should be aware of all the dangers you face, and face them together with those by your side.' 'How should I continue the assault from the front, then?' 'It's simple. Have some people lie in wait atop the cliffs, and throw down roadblocks from above when the enemy comes around to attack you from behind. That would both cut them off from their main force and protect your rear. 'Naturally, your retreat will be cut off too, but the fact that the enemy has split their troops simply makes them more vulnerable to a frontal assault by your main force. Victory is yours as long as you can defeat them before their troops can return to reinforce.' 'Sounds like a great idea! Let's go with that. I thought you were just a doctor, Harold. Where did you learn all this?' 'To tell the truth, I've led troops into battle before, but I found medicine to be far more interesting.' 'That so? Well, I love battles, and so do the other kids.' 'I would love war too, if all wars were as adorable. In any case, good luck, General Myrtle.' Why is Harold getting along so well with Myrtle and her group of wargaming children?
text.zh:
“将军，我刚才听您说，您打算从正面进攻对方的关口，所以想要说两句。”
“你是……那个军医？你觉得我的决策有问题？”
“不不，将军威名远播，我只是提出一些我的看法。您请看，这是战场的地形，一个正面的隘口，以及三条可以从侧面进出的小道。
“如果我是敌方，我知道以正面进攻而闻名的将军是自己的对手，必定会在加强隘口守备的同时，派人分别通过小道，绕到将军背后，形成前后夹击的态势。”
“唔，你说的确实有点道理。所以你的意思是，我应该分散队伍，分出人手从小道进攻？”
“不不不，只有三流的战术家才会认为，追求多变，让敌人无迹可寻是战术的极致。殊不知，唯有多智近妖者能做到欺骗所有人，实际上，一个人做事必然会留下属于他的痕迹。”
“听不懂。”
“很简单，就算我建议您分散队伍进攻，您愿意吗？”
“不愿意，太无聊了。”
“正是如此。我的提醒只是希望您能注意到可能存在的危机，身为一名领袖，您应当知道自己面临的所有危险，然后，与身边的人共同面对。”
“告诉我，哈洛德军医，有什么办法能让我继续正面突破？”
“很简单，您只需要分出一些人马埋伏在山崖上，在对方的队伍已经抵达您的背后想要进行偷袭时，从山崖上投下障碍物，切断他们与您大部队的联系，到那时，对方的夹击之势自然就化解了。
“虽然您的退路也会因此受阻，但是，因为对方分派出了人手进行伏击，他们的正面力量必定是不如您的大部队的，只要您能在对方的偷袭队伍赶回来以前消灭对方，那么胜利就是您的囊中之物。”
“听起来好像确实是这么一回事，那就听你的！哈洛德，你不是医生吗，这些你是从哪里学来的？”
“将军，不瞒您说，我以前也带过一些人打过一些仗，但是对我来说，考虑这些东西远不如当个医生有意思。”
“是吗？我觉得打仗很好玩啊，其他孩子也都很喜欢。”
“哈哈哈，如果这片大地上都是这样可爱的战争，我也会喜欢的。无论如何，祝您旗开得胜，桃金娘大将军。”

哈洛德为啥和桃金娘带起来的那群喜欢玩战争游戏的孩子混得那么好啊？！

text.en:
Oh, it's my turn?
What were we talking about again?
Ah, yes, each of us tells a story about ourselves. Spare me the look of anticipation, please. They say I've seen a lot, but it's nothing compared to what you've seen.
Wait, what's that vintage you just took out? Alright, very well, here's one I save for special occasions.
When I was young, I didn't have the slightest doubt about my duty. I believed I was fighting for Victoria, for the greater good, until I lost my leg.
There's really nothing remarkable about the story. I stepped on a mine, lost a leg, spent a few months in bed, then went back to the frontlines after getting a prosthetic limb. It's a rare soldier who isn't missing a piece here or there, but I rarely tell people what I was thinking at the time.
While I was lying in the doctor's tent like a mannikin, I saw for the first time my comrades being brought in, moaning in pain. Some of them recovered, others were taken away still moaning in pain, and yet others ended up with a white cloth draped over their face.
For the first time, I realized that when you stripped away the glamorous exterior of glory, all that's left is the pained cries of the soldiers, and hands dropping weakly off the sides of beds.
That was when I started to feel exhausted by war.
...We've come this far, Doctor. Let me say a little more.
I still remember the puzzled gazes upon me when I stepped into the world of high society for the first time. They were sharper than any sword and threatened to impale me, but I took it on the chin and kept walking.
To give your life for your country is an honor, but it should be by choice. No one was born to be sent to their death.
The reason I'm still working so hard at this age is to find a place for the poor bastards who've stuck it out with me all these years with so little to show for it, and to set my own mind at ease.
Now, don't give me that look, I'm thankful that Rhodes Island is willing to accept a bunch of old invalids like us, with all the limbs we don't have. Besides, your burden's hardly any lighter than mine. Who's pitying who here?
As someone who's been there, though, the only advice I can give you is this: There's no greater happiness than being able to eat, drink, walk, and sleep. To have a few true friends, and a couple stiff drinks.
A toast to your health, that we may see the sun rise again tomorrow.
text.zh:
嗯？轮到我说了吗？
等等，要说些什么来着？
噢，对了，每人讲一个自己的故事。哎，博士，别用那种期待的眼神看我，他们都说我见多识广，但和你波澜壮阔的经历相比，我实在是汗颜啊。
什么，你居然把这样的好酒拿出来了？唉，好吧，只能把这个压箱底的活计拿出来了！
年轻的时候，我曾对自己的使命坚信不疑，我相信我是在为了维多利亚而战，我是在为了一个崇高的目标而战，直到我失去了这条腿。
这个故事没有什么出奇的地方，我在战场上不慎被绊雷炸断了一条腿，在病床上躺了几个月后，换上假肢重回前线。对于一个士兵来说，身上不少点什么才是少见的事，但我很少给人讲那几个月中我想了什么。
当我像一个傀儡一样躺在医疗帐篷里时，我第一次看到我的战友一个个呻吟着被送了进来。他们有的康复了，有的又呻吟着被抬了出去，有的则被盖上了白布。
我第一次意识到，所谓的荣耀褪下那一层光鲜的外衣之后，剩下的竟然只是士兵们的哀嚎，和一双双无力垂下的手。
那是我人生中第一次对战争产生了一点厌倦。
……都说到这里了，就让我多说一点吧，博士。
直到今天，我依然记得，我第一次踏进社交场时，那一双双投向我的讶异视线。它们比任何刀剑都要锐利，简直要洞穿我的身体。但我还是硬着头皮，走了进去。
为国捐躯确实是一种荣耀，但这应该是一种选择，没有人生来就是为了被撵着去送死。
到了这个年纪我还在东奔西走，无非是想给这帮跟了我一辈子没怎么享过福的倒霉蛋们找一条退路，也好给我自己一个交代。
哈哈，别露出那副表情，罗德岛愿意接纳这群缺胳膊少腿的老病号，我已经十分感激了。况且，你肩上的东西，可一点不比我少，咱们谁同情谁可不好说啊，哈哈。
不过啊，博士，说来说去，说到最后，我作为过来人，能给你的建议只有一个：能吃能喝，能走能睡。有亲朋几个，有好酒两杯，其实就没有比这更幸福的事了。
来，干杯，敬我们还能看到明天的太阳。

text.en:
Come now, Doctor, it's not as if we only met yesterday. Do you truly believe that I'm a noble at heart? Just the thought of it is more chilling than a bottle of the stiff stuff straight out of the fridge.
These cans and bottles? Well, you know, you need the right perfumes and mouthwash for when you've drunk so much that you don't dare go home and face your wife's wrath. And you need the right cosmetics for when you're down with a hangover, but have a banquet to get to that you can't miss.
I learned this from the other nobles, of course. It's only when I became part of high society that I realized that being dressed in the finest livery doesn't make you any nobler than my foul-mouthed men.
Come, have a seat, and let me tell you what these are for. First, this bottle of perfume. Oh, I remember how it practically saved my life from my wife...
text.zh:
天哪，博士，我们已经认识有段时间了，难道你还相信我骨子里是一个贵族吗？这简直比刚从冰箱里取出来的酒还让人寒心。
你说这些瓶瓶罐罐？呃，是这样的，博士，当你因为喝多了而不敢回家面对夫人的怒火时，你也会需要一些合适的香水和漱口水。而当你宿醉醒来脸色苍白，脑子也不太清醒，却要去参加一个相当重要的宴会时，化妆就是必不可少的了。
当然，这些也是其他贵族传授给我的，真的步入社交场后我才发现，那些衣着光鲜的人私底下未必比我那些满口脏话的手下高贵。
好了，博士，坐吧，我来向你详细介绍一下这些东西各自有什么用途。首先是这瓶香水，啊，它可以说是在我夫人那里救过我的命……

text.en:
Former three-time champion of the Kazimierz Major and personal bodyguard to Enciodes, the president of Karlan Trade. Joined Rhodes Island indefinitely as an operator, as per a contract between the Doctor and Enciodes. 
Currently active in various missions as a Guard, clearing paths for her team with her incomparable battle prowess. 

I've received some feedback that most missions with her feel more like camping trips. This is not the Doctor's fault—she does this on her own, and seems to quite enjoy it, too. Then there's no reason I should stop her, yes? 
——■■■
text.zh:
前卡西米尔骑士竞赛三届冠军，喀兰贸易总裁恩希欧迪斯的贴身保镖。基于博士与恩希欧迪斯签订的合同，无限期作为干员加入罗德岛。
现作为近卫干员活跃于各种任务之中，以其强大无比的战斗力为其他干员开辟道路。

我收到一些反馈，说大部分任务有她在的话，和野营没什么区别。这确实不怪博士，她主动去的，而且看起来她还挺乐在其中的。呃，那我也没什么理由反对，不是吗？
——■■■

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected. 

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 
0% Operator Degenbrecher shows no signs of Originium infection. 

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L 
Operator Degenbrecher rarely comes into contact with Originium. 

 I know many who are highly curious about her unusual constitution: she can't use Originium Arts at all. At first, you might think research on her could reveal some hidden truths about Originium, which could perhaps be applied to our current tech, or even weapon development in the worst case. But if so, we almost certainly wouldn't have ever seen her in Kazimierz's arenas. 
The reality is that people with such physiques are simply completely unable to use Arts. Such cases are exceedingly rare, and if you run into her, you can just pat her shoulder and say 'Don't worry about it, there are others even unluckier than you.' That's it, really. Oh, but don't actually pat her shoulder. My hand still hurts. 
——Warfarin
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员锏没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.12u/L
干员锏甚少接触源石。

我知道很多人对于她的体质挺好奇的——无法使用源石技艺。你乍一听可能觉得通过研究可以发现一些和源石有关的秘密，或者说，可以作为技术应用，再不济，也可以拿来研究武器，但实际上，要真是这么回事，那你们大概是见不到她走上卡西米尔的竞技场的。
现实就是，拥有这种体质的人只是无法使用源石技艺。这种体质很稀有，你见到的时候可以拍拍他的肩膀说“别太在意，有比你更倒霉的”，但也就这么回事了——当然，别去拍她的肩膀，我的手现在还疼。
——华法琳

text.en: If someone wants to know more about the Kazimierz Major, you definitely can't leave out the Black Knight. To most competition knights, a championship trophy is a dream come true, but to the Black Knight, they are but an insignificant footnote in her life. And only those who know what happened behind the scenes realize just how extraordinary winning the championship thrice really was. Because they would know that the General Chamber of Commerce did not want Degenbrecher's third victory—for fear of the competition becoming too predictable—so having her fumble and fall with her third victory within arms' reach was their most commercially viable script. The GCC arrogantly believe that everything is under their control, and thought she would act as they wished, but she gave her reply with her actions: No. 'The assassination plot had already begun the moment the Black Knight stepped off the podium.' My predecessor was there, that's how I heard about it. As for what happened in the end... She probably only had a few minor injuries by the time she made it to the city gates. 'It was basically spitting in the faces of those big shots, so naturally, they couldn't just let her go. So they ended up bringing the Darksteels into the fray. Of course, all they could manage was getting her to leave her trophy in the city. 'As for what came next, you know as much as I do. She met a noble from Kjerag who bought her, and from then on she had nothing to do with Kazimierz. I used to envy her when I first heard the story, but not anymore. 'I'm serious, Doctor. When I found out you had connections with the president of Karlan Trade, I was already expecting this day to come, but— 'Um, could you ask if she has any... issues with the Armorless Union for me? If so, I'll think I'll be hiding in the rafters when I see her going forward—though I doubt that'd help much.' —Excerpt from a conversation between Platinum and the Doctor
text.zh:
如果一个人要了解卡西米尔骑士竞技，那他就一定无法越过“黑骑士”这个名号。
对大部分竞技骑士来说，一座冠军奖杯是他们梦寐以求的奖励，但对黑骑士而言，却好像只是她人生中最微不足道的一个注脚。
而对了解内情的人来说，骑士竞赛三届冠军的意义更加非凡。
因为他们知道，商业联合会并不希望锏获得第三个冠军，因为第三个冠军会让未来相当长一段时间内的比赛失去悬念——黑骑士在第三个冠军奖杯唾手可得之际饮恨倒下，这才是最富有商业价值的剧本。
商业联合会总是自负于所有的事情都在他们的掌控之内，他们认为黑骑士也应该按照他们的意志行动，但黑骑士用实际行动告诉他们——
不。

“在黑骑士走下领奖台的瞬间，针对她的刺杀就已经开始了，我的上一任也去了，我就是从他那里听来的。结果嘛……等黑骑士快要走到城市关口的时候，大概也就受了点轻伤吧。
“这基本上和狠狠地扇那些大人物的巴掌没有区别，他们当然不可能就那么让她走，所以最后，把‘玄铁’请了出来。但是，就算是‘玄铁’，最后也只是做到让她把奖杯给留在了那座城市里。
“后来我知道的就和你也差不多了。遇到来自谢拉格的贵人，被买下，从此和卡西米尔撇清关系。以前听的时候我还挺羡慕的，现在就不会了。
“说真的，博士，在得知你和那位喀兰的总裁扯上关系时，我就想过这一天，但是——
“呃，你能不能帮我问问，她对无胄盟还有没有意见，如果有的话，我以后见到她就躲天花板——虽然大概也没用就是了。”
——白金与博士某次闲谈的内容

text.en:
A report from our correspondent: There are many mysteries surrounding the president of Karlan Trade, Enciodes, and the most intriguing of them all is of course his bodyguard, the former three-time winner of the Kazimierz Major—Miss Degenbrecher. 
...
With her permission, we have shadowed her for a day— 
When she wakes up in the morning, the first thing she does is to head downstairs to buy breakfast. After her meal, she will go out if Master Enciodes has work for her, or if there is Tschäggättä training to conduct. Otherwise, she will exercise in the yard for about two hours, then copy scriptures or read in her study until noon. She then goes to the nearby commercial district for lunch. 
During her lunch break, villagers will often approach her, asking for help with farm work or to settle some trouble (there is a consensus among the locals that her help is first-come-first-served), and what's most astonishing is that she will agree to help them after eating. You could say she spends most of her afternoon helping the villagers, and on the rare occasion she has free time, she will head to the snowy mountains in search of something more exciting. 
Usually, her dinner is willingly provided by the villagers who borrowed her assistance, or she'll simply have something on the road. Then, she goes for a stroll by Lake Silberneherze before returning to her residence and calling it a day. 
Yes, Miss Degenbrecher, the living legend who left an unbroken record in Kazimierz is now living the simple life here in Kjerag. This only whets our curiosity about her attitude toward life, but she was unwilling to share her opinion. After the writer was hung by a wooden pole on the wall outside her residence, we were forced to take a different approach. After interviewing some random neighboring villagers, we have selected a few valuable comments from them. Hopefully, our readers can get to know her better this way. 

 'Degenbrecher? She's a good person! Just ask around, there's no one here who hasn't received her help! You definitely have to write that down. No clue what this Kazimierz thing everyone keeps mentioning is, but she's definitely a good Kjerag girl!' 
——An old man enjoying the shade under a tree 
'Miss Degenbrecher? Oh, she's an honorary member of our Anglers Association. At first, we thought someone like her wouldn't be interested, but one day she spent the entire afternoon with us by an ice hole, and it was then I knew she was one of us. Go ask the fellas who're always at Lake Silberneherze. Everyone knows her, she's our idol.' 
——A young angler 
'Degenbrecher? To be honest, I was wary when she first joined us. After all, she pretty much took my position. But afterwards I stopped caring, yeah? Spend long enough with her, and you'll realize that despite how she looks, she really does care, deep down. There's no doubt she's an indispensable member of the Silverash family.' 
——An Itra with a strange scent 
'Can Kjerag can satisfy her? That is but the preliminary question. You will soon discover that what gives her cause to leave or stay is not the satisfaction she feels, but whether her environment makes sense to her. I am pleased to note that Kjerag does indeed, and I believe her attitude towards it represents a sort of simple, yet sharp, perspective on this place. I can only hope that she finds the future Kjerag just as coherent.' 
——A Feline who asked to conceal his identity 
.....
——Excerpt from the March 1098 issue of 'Kjerag Newsletter' second edition
text.zh:
本报讯 喀兰贸易的总裁恩希欧迪斯的身上有许多谜团，而其中，最令人好奇的，必然是他的保镖，前卡西米尔骑士竞赛三届冠军——锏小姐。
……
在本人的允许下，我们对锏小姐的生活进行了追踪——
早上起来，她会先去楼下购买早饭。早饭结束后，如果恩希欧迪斯老爷有工作上的安排或者这一天有山雪鬼的训练，她会出门。而如果没有的话，她会先在院子里锻炼两个小时左右，接着在书房里抄写经书或者读书直到中午，而后，前往不远处的商业街吃午饭。
吃午饭时，经常会有一些乡亲来找她，请她帮忙做一些农活或者解决一些棘手的麻烦（这似乎是这一带的一个共识——你中午可以在商业街找到锏，并请她帮忙，先到先得），而令人惊讶的是，锏小姐会一一应允，并在午饭结束后前去帮忙。可以说，锏小姐的大部分午后，都花在为乡亲们提供帮助上，而难得空闲的时候，她会进入雪山，寻找一些能够为她带来刺激的事物。
晚饭大部分时候都是请求帮助的乡亲们自愿提供的，或者也无非是在路边解决，然后，在银心湖畔散步一会儿，就会回到自己的住所，结束这一天。
是的，锏小姐，她曾在卡西米尔缔造了至今无人超越的战绩，这样活生生的传奇，如今却在谢拉格过着如此朴素的生活，这不禁让我们对她的生活态度更加好奇，但她始终不愿意就此发表看法。在笔者被一根木棍挂在她住所外的墙面上之后，不得已只得另辟蹊径，在她的住所附近随机采访了一些乡亲，并筛选出了有价值的一些评价，希望能通过这种方式让读者更加了解锏小姐。

“锏啊？她是个大好人啊！你去四邻八方问一问，谁家没受过她的恩惠！这句话你一定要给我写进去，什么卡西米尔不卡西米尔的我不知道，但她绝对是我们谢拉格的好姑娘！”
——在树下纳凉的老者
“锏小姐？哦，她是我们钓客协会的名誉会员啊。一开始我们都以为她这样的人物对这种事没兴趣的，但是那天，她和我们一起在一个冰洞边坐了一下午，那时候我就知道，她是我们这边的人。你去问问在银心湖边活动的家伙们，他们都认识锏小姐，她是我们所有人的偶像。”
——年轻的钓客
“锏姐？老实说，一开始，我对于她的到来是有些戒备的。毕竟她也算是抢走了我的位置。但后来我就不太在乎这事了，嗯？其实相处久了你就会知道，她表面上什么都不在乎，实际上心里清楚着呢。她是希瓦艾什家不可或缺的一员，毫无疑问。”
——身带异香的依特拉
“谢拉格能否让她满意这一点，只在一开始是个问题，很快你会发现，决定她去留的并不是一个环境能否满足她，而是这个环境是否形成了一种她能接受的自洽。我很高兴谢拉格做到了这一点。我认为，她对谢拉格的态度代表了一种朴素而又尖锐的视角，我希望未来的谢拉格也能尽量令她接受。”
——要求隐去身份的菲林
……
——摘自《谢拉格通讯报》1098年3月第二版

text.en:
Degenbrecher stands halfway up the mountain, turning around to view the scenery she has grown a little tired of, and recalls the first time she faced an avalanche. 
She had no choice but to face Kjeragandr's 'turnover'—the local parlance for an avalanche—to save a couple who could not escape in time. It was an interesting experience for her, and she realized for the first time how she could simultaneously wrestle with nature and have fun. 
Since then, you could always find her in the rescue team whenever an avalanche occurred in Kjerag, and as such she has become a hero to many of the locals. 
Honestly, I'm only trying to entertain myself, she thinks. 
These days, Kjerag's avalanche warning system is more than sufficient. The day before one occurs, the monitoring center sounds an alarm to warn the residents and pedestrians at the foot of the mountain to evacuate, and the mountain is closed to everyone and anyone—with her as the sole exception. 
When she sees the locals watching her walk into the snowy mounts with surprise in their eyes, she thinks she did not come here to win or lose. 
For her, there is no victory or defeat against an avalanche. After all, what even counts as a win? To survive? If so, then naturally she's on a winning streak. But if requires her to cut down her foe, then she has never once succeeded. 
But this does not dishearten her, for she finds it quite enjoyable to challenge something she cannot defeat. Besides, as long as she lives, she can try again and again. And perhaps one day, she might just succeed? 
Even so, the Kazimierz knights had regarded her as an insurmountable wall, and not just that. Once they concluded she was unbeatable, they gave up entirely on trying to score a victory, with their bouts somehow ending up about testing their skills against hers by the number of blows they could take before falling. 
A wave of white snow rises from the mountaintop and rolls downward. 
She looks up, thinking of Enciodes and his hooded friend. 
She thinks that what they face is just like the avalanche in front of her, or what those knights saw her as. 
She pulls out the swordbreakers stuck in the snow, and launches herself towards the wave. 
They always seem to make the same choice as her.
text.zh:
锏站在半山腰处转身看向已经有些看腻了的谢拉格风光，想起第一次面对雪崩时的光景。
为了营救一对来不及逃难的夫妻，她不得不直面耶拉冈德的“翻身”——在谢拉格，他们是这样称呼雪崩的——那是一次很有趣的体验，她第一次意识到，她可以与自然角力，从中获得一些乐趣。
从那以后，每次谢拉格发生雪崩，救援队中总是会有她的身影。因此，她也成了许多谢拉格人心中的英雄。
实际上，我只是想要从对抗雪崩之中寻找一些乐趣而已，她想。
时至今日，谢拉格的雪崩预警系统已经变得有模有样了。在雪崩发生的前一天，监测中心就会发出警报，对山脚下的住民和行人进行警告和疏散，并组织封山，不允许任何人进入雪山——当然，她是唯一的例外。
当她看到那些用讶异的眼光看着她走进雪山的谢拉格人时，她想的是，她并不是为了输赢而来。
对她而言，对抗雪崩并没有输赢之分，毕竟，怎样算赢呢？直面雪崩而活下来就算吗？如果是这样，那她的战绩自然是全胜。可如果她至少要切开雪崩才算胜利，那么，她还没有成功过。
但她并不会为此感到沮丧，毕竟，挑战自己尚无法战胜的事物对她而言是相当有乐趣的。况且，只要她没有死，她就可以一直挑战下去，或许有一天，她真的能做到呢？
然而，在卡西米尔时，那些骑士们将她看作一道无法逾越的高墙，他们的想法却并非如此，他们在认定她无法战胜后，就放弃了战胜她的想法，与她进行的比较不知何时变成了能在她手下撑过几招。
雪白的波浪自山巅而起，向着山下滚滚而来。
她抬起头，想起了恩希欧迪斯和他那个戴兜帽的朋友。
她想，他们面对的东西，恰如她所面对的雪崩，又或者那些骑士眼中的她。
拔起插在雪中的锏，她向着雪浪激射而去。
他们似乎总是会和自己做出一样的选择。

text.en:
Aspirations. 
For the orphan living out on the streets, it was survival and having a good meal. 
To achieve this goal, she wielded her worn-out swordbreakers and killed her way from Leithanien to Kazimierz, turning herself from an obscure competition knight into a champion. 
Everyone she met on the way told her that survival doesn't count as an aspiration, that one's desires should be more complex than that. So many were so insistent that she became a little curious. 
As a result, the Leithanian dark horse tried out many of their aspirations—their corrupt, intoxicating, infeasible lifestyles—she has tried it all. 
She has also met those with so-called nobler inclinations. 
But in doing so, she carefully realized that all their desires ultimately boil down to keeping themselves or the people around them alive, and to have a good meal afterward. It was then that she decided that Kazimierz did not hold the answer she was looking for. 
And so the nation's champion chose to be exiled. By the way, the GCC probably still doesn't realize that if they hadn't sought her out, she'd never actually planned on winning a third time. 
The conflict with Darksteel did indeed introduce unprecedented danger to her, and at the time she had two thoughts. One was to ask Darksteel what kind of aspirations someone as strong as them might have, and the second was that if her skills were lacking, then there really wasn't anything wrong with dying on the spot. Kazimierz was just that boring. 
In the end, neither happened, and instead she met a young noble who claimed to hail from Kjerag. 
You seem to be curious about how Enciodes convinced me to go with him at first. It was nothing special, he was just the first person I couldn't fully comprehend. And now, there are many more like him around me. 
I don't understand you, Enciodes, or some of the others on this landship any more than you understand me. 
You may find it hard to comprehend that I lack any aspirations, but do you people really have something you're striving for? All you do is to piece together the wishes of others into a huge fortress, then convince yourself that building it is a dream of your own. 
Let's say I ask you now, what do you want to do? Can you think of anything that isn't just realizing the desires of someone else? 
If you could trade your life to realize your dream, people like you probably wouldn't hesitate for a second, as if you were born just for that. 
I've seen too many avaricious people drown in their own desires, as well as too many tragic deaths of those who did no wrong and only wanted to live. I've also seen many who managed to realize their desires and obtain the life they aspired to. But people like you, I've yet to see how your lives end. 
And that's why I chose to go with him, and why I stand before you. 
Just do whatever you want, and I'll make sure you live.
text.zh:
理想。
对那个流落街头的孤儿而言，活下去，吃上一口好吃的，就是她最大的理想。
为了这个目标，她提着一双破烂的锏从莱塔尼亚一路杀到了卡西米尔，从一个默默无闻的竞技骑士一路变成了冠军。
这一路上的所有人都在告诉她，活下去并不是一个理想，我们是人，我们应该拥有更复杂的欲望。所有人都对此信誓旦旦，她于是也有些好奇。
因此，那个莱塔尼亚的黑马尝试了许多他人所谓的理想，那些糜烂的、醉狂的、迷梦般的生活，她都尝试过。
她也见过所谓志趣高尚的人。
但是，她仔细辨认过，他们的欲望，归根结底，依然是让自己或者身边的人活下去，然后吃上一口好吃的。那时她就断定，这个国家没有她要的答案。
于是，那个名满全国的冠军选择主动被卡西米尔放逐。对了，商业联合会大概至今都不知道，如果他们没去找她，她其实是不打算拿第三个冠军的。
和“玄铁”的周旋确实给她带来了前所未有的威胁，她当时有两个想法，一是想问一问“玄铁”，他这样的强者，有着怎样的理想，二是如果最后技不如人，死在这里也没什么不好，卡西米尔实在是无聊了点。
结果，这两个想法都没有实现，她就遇到了一个自称来自谢拉格的青年贵族。
你似乎一直很好奇，恩希欧迪斯当初是用什么说服我的——没什么特别的，只是他是第一个让我觉得有些无法理解的人。现在，这样的人又多了一些。
我并不理解你、恩希欧迪斯，还有这艘船里的部分人，正如你们不理解我。
你们觉得我没有理想难以理解，但你们真的拥有理想吗？你们只是将他人的愿望拼凑成一座巨大的堡垒，然后说服自己，搭建这座堡垒就是自己的理想。
假如我现在问你们，你们想要做什么，你们能想出实现某个人的愿望以外的回答吗？
如果能够用生命来换取理想的实现，你们这样的人恐怕会毫不犹豫地选择交换，仿佛你们就是为此而生的。
我见过太多怀抱欲望溺死的贪心者，我也见过无数仅仅为了活下去却惨死的正直者，实现自己欲望而获得了理想生活的幸福者也不在少数，但是，你们这样的人的结局，我还没有见过。
所以，我选择了跟在他身边，所以，我会站在你的面前。
尽管去做你们想做的事吧，我会让你们活下去的。

text.en:
Degenbrecher is almost done packing her luggage. She stands up in the originally unremarkable living room, and looks around to confirm she didn't miss anything. 
Going to Rhodes Island is just a relatively long vacation, so there shouldn't be a need to bring anything special, she thinks as she plans to take a final look at Lake Silberneherze from the window. 
As she walks across the floor in the middle of the room, her footsteps make a different sound than they do elsewhere. Hollow echoes remind her there is something beneath the floorboards. She pauses for a moment. Of course she knows what lies underneath—the hilt of a greatsword, the very same one she used in Kazimierz. This also brings back a few memories of the past. 
During her escape, the weapon was actually broken in two after blocking a Darksteel arrow. Back then, she threw the blade in reciprocation and took the hilt with her—after all, she had no other weapons then. Until she arrived at Kjerag and got her swordbreakers crafted by the Karlan Trade artisans. Naturally, she stopped using her greatsword. 
And as for why, she once told Sharp that it was because Kjerag was too cramped for it. She often repeats this to others while imagining a future where she might need it. Which is why she decided to stash it under the floorboards in the first place. 
However, she realizes now that even on the night she knew she was about to face Kjerag's biggest crisis yet, it never once came to mind. She had completely forgotten it existed until today. If not for her coincidental footsteps, she might not have realized it even after arriving at Rhodes Island. 
'I suppose if Kjerag was too cramped, then Rhodes Island might not have space for it either.' 
She thinks for a moment, then suddenly chuckles for some reason before walking towards the window. 
She will probably never need to use that greatsword ever again.
text.zh:
行李差不多收拾完了，锏站在原本就十分朴素的客厅里，环视了一圈，想要确认一下自己还有什么东西没带。
去罗德岛只是一次比较长的休假，应该没什么特别需要带的东西。她这么想着，打算去窗边最后看一眼银心湖的景色。
走过客厅中央的地板时，脚下传来了和踩在其他地板上不同的声响，有些空荡的回声提醒着她，下面有别的东西。她的脚步瞬间停顿，她当然知道下面有什么——一把巨剑的剑柄，还在卡西米尔时用的那把。这也让她回忆起了一点往事。
实际上，那把巨剑在逃亡过程中，因为抵挡“玄铁”的箭而碎成了两半，她当时把剑身给掷了出去作为回敬，而剑柄则顺手带在身边——毕竟那时候，她没有别的称手武器。直到来到谢拉格，有了喀兰贸易的工匠们为她制造的锏，也就自然地放下了这把巨剑。
对于放下这把巨剑的理由，她曾经对Sharp说，因为谢拉格太狭窄了。她对别人也是这么说的，在这么说的时候，她其实想过，或许未来有一天，会有需要重铸这柄巨剑的时候，正因如此，她当初才会把它放在地板之下。
但是，此时，她忽然意识到，即使在明知即将面对谢拉格有史以来最大危机的那个夜晚，她也没有想起这件事情，这把剑柄就这样被她遗忘到了今天，如果不是此时的偶然，或许直到抵达罗德岛她都不会记起来。
“……看来，谢拉格是有点太窄了，而罗德岛，或许也不太宽敞。”
她想了想，不知为何笑了一声，然后继续走向窗边。
大概不会有用到这柄巨剑的时候了。

value.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为感染者。

infectionStatus.en: Confirmed Infected by medical examination.
infectionStatus.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为感染者。

text.en: Ray, a Rim Billitonian without stable employment who often works in mine safety and security, or as a 'pitsinker' in the local parlance. After running into Amiya, the Doctor, and Savage while they were revisiting old memories, she took the initiative to apply to Rhodes Island. As an operator aboard the landship, she participates in a variety of security, combat, and exploration missions.
text.zh: 莱伊，雷姆必拓人，无稳定职业，较常从事在雷姆必拓被称为“探井人”的矿井安保工作。偶遇故地重游的阿米娅、博士与暴行后，主动申请加入罗德岛。现作为罗德岛驻舰干员参与各类安保、战斗及勘探任务。

text.en:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 4%
Operator Ray has no obvious crystals on the surface of her body.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.25u/L
Operator Ray frequently enters dangerous environments, and her condition is much graver than she reports.
In other words, Miss Ray has incredibly high pain tolerance. Being able to endure such pain means that it is very easy for the patient to neglect their condition. We will need to monitor her closely.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓模糊，可见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测异常，有矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】4%
干员莱伊体表暂未出现明显源石结晶。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.25u/L
干员莱伊常出入危险环境，其感染状况比患者自己所反馈的要严峻得多。
换言之，莱伊小姐对疼痛的忍受能力实在是过强了。这种耐痛性很可能使患者忽视自己的身体状况，我们需要密切关注。

text.en:
In the well-developed mining industry of Rim Billiton, 'pitsinker' was once a common occupation. Traditionally, every day before a mine opens for work, a lone pitsinker is dispatched down the shaft to inspect for hazardous conditions: water seepage, leaks both gaseous and liquid, areas at risk of cave-in, etc, all alongside suppressing any Infected creatures that thrive in mines. To ensure smooth operation, pitsinkers would also need to constantly patrol the tunnels and protect the miners from surprise attacks from said creatures. On paper, they are similar to modern security staff—with a greater focus on specialized knowledge and combat skills—but in practice there are practically zero requirements to become one. For the many vagrant children who lack the strength for long hours of mining work, it is the perfect job to make their way up in the world. At its core, pitsinking really is just going down a mine to check it for poison gas and cave-ins. At times, they will risk their bodies, even their very lives, to seek these answers. 
That said, Rim Billiton's mining industry has long since moved on, with much of the work now being performed by machines. The technologies used to monitor and decontaminate the mineshafts are constantly being refined, with the safety of the workers increasing day by day. However, small-scale private mines can still be found all over the country, and some mine owners continue to use the old ways passed down for generations. Operator Ray seems to be of like mind. She doesn't think too much about it or herself, and hasn't given her future much thought either. Once, long ago, someone told her that she could make a living as a pitsinker, and she's been doing it ever since. As a fellow Rim Billitonian who's worked in mine security, Savage has given Ray a number of tests, confirming that she has qualifications to hold a security post at a modern large-scale mine. Ray had simply never considered the possibility.
Thankfully, she seems to have luck on her side, having managed to make it through life without major injury. However, perhaps she will be stuck with a pitsinker's mindset for a while yet: isolated, always on high alert, always raising her head to gaze up from the bottom of the shaft at the light from the entrance, not knowing whether she's alive or dead until she's hauled back to the surface and leaves the dark behind her.

[A note jotted down after a test report]
Her reflexes are ridiculous! Maybe even too good! She managed to completely avoid my hammer and the following lightning strikes, then evaded every last fragment of shattered roadblocks too! She even dodged my pat on the shoulder after the test was over! While she may not have any real experience, I think she's perfectly capable of participating in milder combat as she is. 
By the way, don't leave this note in the copy of the report she gets. I praised her for her talent in combat, and how it took a lot more than luck to make it as far as she has, but she seemed... a little melancholy hearing that, crouching down to give her sandbeast a quick pat.
text.zh:
在矿业发达的雷姆必拓，“探井人”曾是一个十分常见的职业。传统矿井每天开工之前，会派遣一名探井人独自下矿，确认井下的安全状况，排查渗水、泄漏、塌方等事故的风险，此外还需清剿矿井中滋生的感染生物。若矿井顺利开工，探井人则需要继续在矿道间巡逻，保护矿工们不被感染生物袭击。乍看之下，探井人似乎与现代矿场中的安保人员类似，甚至比安保人员更需要充足的专业知识和优秀的战斗能力，但实际上，这一职业几乎没有门槛，甚至许多力量不足以负荷长时间挖矿劳作的流浪儿童，会优先以此为自己的出路，因为探井人工作最核心的部分，其实只是进入状况未知的矿井，确认内部是否有毒气泄漏与塌方的征兆。有些时候，探井人会用自己的身体乃至生命换回这个答案。
雷姆必拓的采矿业早已发生改变，现代矿井中这一部分工作已经被机械设备取代，应用于矿井环境的监控和净化技术在不断升级，工人们的生命安全所得到的保障也日益牢靠。然而，小型的私人矿井依然遍布雷姆必拓，一些矿场主也依然沿用着大家族里口口相传了不知道多少年的运作方式。干员莱伊似乎也是如此。她没有想太多，没有反思过自身，也不曾考虑长远的未来，仅仅是很久以前有人告诉她可以做探井人换口饭吃，她就一直做了下来。作为同样出身雷姆必拓且在矿场任职过的安保人员，暴行对莱伊进行了不少测试，最后确认，她的专业素质已经足够担任一个现代大型矿场的安保人员，只是莱伊自己从来没有想过这种可能。
值得庆幸的是，莱伊似乎运气很好，她活到了现在，而且大体称得上是安然无恙。但是，她或许还会长时间地维持一个探井人的生活状态：孤立，时刻保持高度警惕，在竖井下仰头望着井口的光，直到人们把她拉回地面，黑暗再也追不上她，她才能知道，自己活了下来。

【一份测试报告后的附注】
……她的反应速度真是太了不起了！可能有点过头了！我的锤子她躲开了，锤子击发的雷电束她也躲开了，远处被击碎的障碍物溅开的碎片她也躲开了，测试结束后我拍她肩膀的手她也躲开了！虽然她没有正经的战斗经验，但我认为她现在完全能够参与轻度实战。
对了，这条附注还是不要留在给干员本人的报告书里了。我夸她战斗方面很有天赋，活到现在果然不止是靠运气的时候，她显得……有点惆怅，然后蹲下去摸了一会儿自己的沙地兽。

text.en:
For quite a while after joining Rhodes Island, nobody paid much attention to Ray. There's no shortage of operators who are very welcoming to newcomers, but neither the movie club, the tea club, nor the culinary club ever sent her an invitation. After all, she's never asked for directions, or even stopped to get her bearings on the landship. This made it very hard for anyone to tell that she was indeed a newcomer, even as she was calmly making her fifth loop on the same route.
They might also not draw the connection between her and that one sandbeast that showed up recently. Sandbeasts are notoriously hard to tame, with many preferring to starve to death than eat in captivity. Thus, most believed that the sandbeast popping up in the corridors had merely crawled in via a ventilation duct, and that in a day or two it would find its way back to the great outdoors. In time, everyone simply got used to it hiding away in comfy corners. It might occasionally chew through a cable beneath a pre-fab board, but they were always fixed in a jiffy, with no one the wiser as to its owner.
One day, thanks to a particular dish on the menu, several operators were discussing the migratory fowlbeasts of Terra in the cafeteria, and eventually reached a confusion as to whether the fowlbeasts that arrived in two different locations were the same species or not. At that point, Ray—who had never spoken a single word to them—slipped into their conversation as though she had known them their whole life and started asking each of the operators where they were from. Upon learning their hometowns, she would explain which species were typical of each region in easy-to-understand terms. This was how they got to know her, with many amazed at her knowledge in this area, as well as her incredible curiosity that she never showed at any other topic. She was the type of child who would flip through a picture book again and again, repeatedly devouring all the animal almanacs in her local library and unintentionally memorizing every last page.
Naturally, everyone quickly realized that the mystery sandbeast was simply hanging out near Ray, and that she was the one fixing the wires it chewed through. Also, half of her single-occupancy dorm room was occupied by a giant sandbox. Not only did she make it herself, but when the landship made a stop in the wastelands, she took the chance to gather sack after sack of sandy soil to fill it.
Nobody knows how long she spent on the task, and she never mentioned it in the room renovation application form she handed in after-the-fact, but at least everyone is now aware that, of the many jobs she claims to have done, she wasn't lying about the heavy labor.
We should be glad that Ray is the only one aboard raising a sandbeast, because she never gave it a name. Most who raise a pet will try to condition them to respond to a specific word or phrase, but Ray simply whistles like a sandbeast to call hers. Perhaps she is simply not great at naming things. After all, the only reason her name was shortened to Ray—from Rayella—was because of a lazily-made temporary ID tag given to her by a worker who couldn't spell. Or perhaps she just thinks that 'sandbeast' has a nice ring to it. A special name, just like the 'Ray' she is so fond of.
text.zh:
莱伊来到罗德岛后，在很长一段时间里没有引起任何人注意。罗德岛并不缺乏对新人极其热情的干员，但各种观影会、茶会和美食品鉴会的邀请一直没有送到她手上。毕竟，她既没有问过路，也没有在罗德岛的任何一处停下来好奇地东张西望，这让其他干员很难发现她其实是初来乍到，以及，她可能正平静地第五次绕进同一条通道。
干员们也没有把近期出现在舰内的一只沙地兽与莱伊联系起来。沙地兽是很难驯服的野生动物，被捕获后往往拒绝进食，直至死亡。因此，一开始看到罗德岛走廊上出现沙地兽的干员甚至认为它是顺着某个排气口爬进来的，过两天就会自己找到路爬回大自然；一段时间后，大家习惯了这只喜好暗处的沙地兽偶尔咬坏埋在预制板下的电线而线路又很快就会被修好，却依然没发现沙地兽的饲养人是谁。
直到某天，几名干员在食堂里从一道菜谈论到泰拉各地的羽兽迁徙，正当他们为抵达某两地的是否是同一种羽兽而困惑时，从没和他们说过话的莱伊突然无比自然地接过了话题，一一问过在场干员的出身地，用十分浅显易懂的方式讲解了许多地区具有代表性的羽兽种类。干员们这才开始认识莱伊，惊讶于她在这方面的知识量，以及她平时在其他地方完全没有表现过的强烈好奇心：她以一种小孩子翻来覆去看画册的劲头，反复翻阅图书馆里诸多的生物图鉴，自然而然地记住了这些内容。
当然，大家也很快发现了沙地兽其实是在莱伊附近活动，每次电线被咬坏，都是莱伊自己修好的。以及，莱伊独居的宿舍房间里，有一半的空间都被一个巨大的沙箱占据。莱伊不仅自己做好了它，还趁着舰船停在荒地上，一麻袋一麻袋地搬来了填满沙箱的沙土。
没人知道她花了多长时间干完这件事，她自己在补交宿舍改造申请书的时候也没有提及；但是现在大家至少可以知道，她说自己做过很多种散工，这一点是真的。
以及，应该庆幸罗德岛上只有莱伊一个人养了沙地兽，因为她没有给沙地兽起名。大部分饲养宠物的人会尝试让宠物对特定的词语或音节产生条件反射，但莱伊呼唤沙地兽的方式，是吹响一只模拟沙地兽叫声的哨子。她或许真的很不擅长起名，就像她自己取自本名“莱叶菈”的这个昵称，“莱伊”，原本也只是一个不太会拼写的雷姆必拓工人随便给她贴的临时身份牌；又或许她真的觉得“沙地兽”这个词本身很好听，很特别，就像“莱伊”这个词她很喜欢一样。

text.en:
When other operators went to support Ray on her first solo field mission as scheduled, they found a small shed out in the wastes. It was built into a natural cave in the cliffside, made from lightweight discarded construction materials efficiently fitted together with simple joints, and lit night and day by a portable Originium generator. The Rhodes Island-issued tent she was provided with laid in the corner, still in its packaging.
Ray's way of doing things is pretty much the stereotype of a Rim Billitonian Cautus, but those traditions are as old as the first explorers from the nations of the centrum, who began showing an interest in Rim Billiton's Originium deposits decades ago. Before Rim Billitonians started building nomadic cities, they would combine easy-to-take-down buildings with solidly-constructed pits, using them to hide from the Catastrophes that plague the region especially frequently. After nearly a century though, the old ways have begun to fade. Cautuses these days still love their makeshift sheds, but will choose to build them away from the vicious wilds. Those who still make them out in the countryside like Ray are a dying breed.
Her way of life stems from her childhood. She was born into a family of hunters, in particular a group that stayed away from civilized cities for years on end, wandering about the country and staying self-sufficient. She does not clearly remember what she learnt of hunting back then. The only clear memory she has is of a time when the group took heavy losses from a bout of severe weather. Several of her family members went missing in that sandstorm. After surviving that, she decided to follow a distant relative to seek a living in a nomadic city, engrossed in seeing just how far she could go on her own.
Inside the shed, which felt rather cramped with four people, the operators considerately asked her if she had built a traditional Cautus shed like from her youth because she was homesick.
Ray first shook her head, saying that she wasn't sure what that even meant. 'The comforts of home?' But after a while, when they were finishing up their check of the supplies and getting ready to tear down the shed and leave, she looked about at the operators all squeezed together and suddenly blurted out: 'Now isn't this nice and cozy?'

'Those old Rim Billiton hunter stories she told us that day, like the Rim Billy Gloompincer with claws longer than a man is tall and so on... I don't think her love for animals comes from her childhood environment. I can tell that those memories are very, very far from mind.
But I can also tell that she really does recall something. Do you remember? When were getting ready to shut down the generator and turn off the lights, she looked so reluctant. Afterwards she said that she was saved by 'a ray of light'.'
'Eh? Was she the sort of person to use metaphors like that?'
——An excerpt from the post-mission chatter of two participating operators
text.zh:
当其他罗德岛干员按照计划去接应第一次独自执行外勤任务的莱伊时，他们在荒地上看到了一间小小的棚屋。棚屋倚靠一处天然岩窟而建，轻薄的建筑废料通过简易接合件高效地拼合在一起，一台便携源石发电机提供的能源将岩窟照得日夜通明。而罗德岛发给莱伊的帐篷就躺在墙角，似乎从来没有被打开过。
莱伊的做法的确很符合许多人对雷姆必拓卡特斯的刻板印象，事实上，这种传统也和使核心圈国家开始对雷姆必拓地区产生浓厚兴趣的源石勘探运动一样年代久远。雷姆必拓人在尚未建起移动城市时，正是靠着结合易于拆卸的地表建筑与牢固的地穴，来躲避这片土地上格外频繁的天灾，但近百年来，这种生活方式已经慢慢被淘汰了。卡特斯们依旧热衷于搭建棚屋，只是会选择避开凶恶的荒野，像莱伊一样在野外还保有这种习惯的人，则已经十分少见。
莱伊的生活方式源自她的童年记忆。她出身于一个猎人家庭，而那支猎人队伍显然常年游离在城市文明之外，四处游荡，停停走走，自给自足。自己作为猎人学到了什么，莱伊已经记不清楚，在她脑海中唯一清晰的，是某一次使队伍受到重创的恶劣天气。在那场长时间的沙尘天气中，一部分家庭成员失散，莱伊自己幸存了下来，之后选择了跟随一名远亲前往移动城市谋生，一个人埋头走得越来越远。
在这间挤入四人后立刻显得有些狭小的屋子里，罗德岛干员体贴地问莱伊，她是否是因为想家，才像小时候一样搭起传统的卡特斯棚屋。
对此，莱伊先是摇了摇头，表示并不理解干员所说的“家的温馨气氛”。但过了一会儿，在完成物资清点，准备拆除棚屋离开的时候，她看了看挤在一起的罗德岛干员们，突然没头没脑地说：“现在这样是挺好的。”

“我们那天听她讲了雷姆必拓猎人的几个小故事，比如雷姆必拓的钳兽一只钳子比人还长之类的……不过，我不觉得她对动物的热情来自童年的家庭环境。我能感觉到，那段记忆对她来说特别特别遥远。
“但我也能感觉到，她确实一直记着那时的什么事。你还记得吗？我们准备关闭发电机熄灭灯光的时候，她好像非常不舍得，后来她提到，自己被‘一束光’救过。”
“呃，她是那种说话会用比喻修辞的人吗？”
——两名参与任务的干员事后的聊天摘录

text.en:
[Ray's accounts]
Today's expenses:
Sandbeast feed
Sandbeast electrolyte supplement (mix with water)
Sandbeast fur cream (Spare. Blended by Dr. Honeyberry. She's not 100% sure if it works, so remember to give feedback after using)
Meal card recharge (Need more protein, doctor's orders)
Compensation for Lanns's truck (Still got eleven months to pay her back in full)
Oripathy suppressants (Gray-ears has been eating hers on time every day this week, so I'd better too)
Today's income:
A bag of snacks
One notebook, two ballpoint pens (girl from HR said that if I needed new ones, I could find her and she'll give me more. Nice lady. Thanks)
'True Accounts of Supernatural Phenomena' cassettes 17-20 (Rented, need to be returned. The librarian suggested that I swap it out for a more credible documentary series next time)

'Look, I was just worried if you could keep your schedule straight, not if you could afford stuff—I've said it before, this payment deadline was your idea, and as close as we are, I wouldn't mind even if you delayed it indefinitely. Basically, no need to show me your tidy little accounts book. If anyone else ever asks you about this kind of thing, don't give them this little book, and definitely don't make them read it the whole way through. Got it?'
'Mhm.'
'Hmph, I never would've expected that behind my back, you'd manage to tidy up your room all spick and span, learn to cook alright, and got even better at mending clothes than me! I also hear your field mission went smooth as butter. They were going on about how you had all these plans and were super-reliable... You sure they're talking about the same Ray? Really?'
'Mhm.'
'Alright, I guess I better change my tune then. Can't keep calling you 'Truckjacker.' After all, what you did back then is our little secret. Best to let the Rhodes Islanders keep their impression of you as a friendly, reliable, occasionally smiling young lady.'
'Mhm.'
'Oh, right, considering that you've been keeping your accounts so nice and tidy, what are you actually planning to do with the money you save up?'
'I'm thinking of looking for a type of big burdenbeast in the Columbian barrenlands, let them start to dance after the moon again.'
'...Eh? You still on about that kind of thing?'
text.zh:
【莱伊的记账本】
本日支出：
沙地兽饲料
沙地兽用电解质冲剂
沙地兽护毛膏（备用。蜜莓医生调配的，她不确定是否有效，试用之后要给她反馈）
饭卡充值（遵循医生要求，多吃蛋白质）
兰娜的运载车赔偿金（还有十一个月付清）
矿石病抑制药（灰耳朵这个星期每天都按时吃了药，我也是）
本日收入：
零食一袋
笔记本一个，圆珠笔两支（人事部干员说如果需要新的可以再去找她，她会继续送我，她真好，谢谢）
《超自然现象亲历者口述》录像带17-20（租借，需还。图书管理员建议我下次换个可信度更高的系列纪录片看）

“我就是关心一下你能不能自己把日子过清楚，不是怀疑你还不上钱——赔偿金的事是你自己提的，我也说了，我们这关系，你想拖延就可以无限期拖延——总之，没必要这么客气把记账本都拿给我看。要是再有人问起类似的话题，你也别把这个本子给他们看，更不要催他们看完，明白吗？”
“嗯。”
“啧，不过我之前真没看出来，你居然能把房间收拾得有模有样，饭也做得不赖，缝补衣服的手艺更是比我还强上那么一点！听说你的外勤任务也干得不错，他们都夸你有计划、特别靠谱……你以前也这样吗？真的？”
“嗯。”
“好吧，我也该改口了，不能再叫你‘劫车的’了。毕竟你干的那些事，现在算是我们之间的秘密，罗德岛这里的人对你的印象，就维持在现在这个友善、可靠、时不时笑一笑的样子就好。”
“嗯。”
“对了，你账本记得这么认真，有没有什么攒够钱之后的计划？”
“我想找到哥伦比亚荒野上的一种大驮兽，让它们重新开始跟着月亮跳舞。”
“……啊？怎么又是这种东西？”

text.en:
[Classified Log]
Alright, Doctor. I won't mention what I know about Feranmuts to anyone else. Thanks for explaining more about what I experienced in that cave.
Memories? My story helped you recall more from the past? ...I'm glad I could help you out.
I know the feeling, having your past locked so very far away, and so indistinct, to the point where you can't even be sure it really happened to you or not. Maybe that's why I thought about seeing it one more time.
Regrets? No, not for now.
Fear? No way.
All I'm thinking of is... illuminating the present. On careful consideration, I don't think it really matters whether or not that light was the ray of light from my memories.
I'll cheer you on, Doctor, and I hope you'll be able to get your memories back without a hitch. Although I will say, being by you and Amiya is bright enough already.
text.zh:
【权限记录】
好的，博士，这些巨兽相关的知识，我不会和其他人说起。谢谢你，很详细地解释了我在那个洞窟里的经历。
回忆？这段故事有助于你回忆以前的事情吗？……很高兴能帮到你。
我知道那种感觉，过去的一些事情，很远又很模糊，让人弄不清楚究竟是不是自己经历过的。也许我就是因为这个，才想再看见它一次。
遗憾？现在还好。
害怕？不会。
我只是想……照亮现在。亮起来的是不是记忆里的那束光，我仔细想了想，好像都没关系。
我会给你加油的，博士，祝你能顺利地找到自己的记忆，虽然，你和阿米娅的身边已经很亮了。

text.en: Wanqing, real name He Sheng, an Agricultural Tianshi apprentice of the Yanese Tianshi Bureaus. Produced significant research results in many Dahuang planting projects. Introduced to Rhodes Island by Shu, he is now on the landship as an exchange student and Logistics Operator.
text.zh: 万顷，本名禾生，炎国天师府学徒，担任农业天师一职。在大荒城多项育种实验中取得了重要的成果。经黍介绍，来到罗德岛访学交流，兼任后勤干员。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Wanqing shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L
Operator Wanqing is very meticulous about following protection procedures when handling Originium.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员万顷没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.12u/L
干员万顷在接触源石时做的防护工作非常到位。

text.en:
While many operators on Rhodes Island are familiar with the farming life, a scholar specialized in agricultural research is still rare enough to turn heads.
'Is it true that you'd need to be hunched over plowing a field every day, all year round?'
'I heard that during the harvest season, everyone from little kids to grannies get their sickles out to reap wheat as far as the eye can see, from dawn until dusk.'
Under the sympathetic yet admiring gazes of everyone around him, Wanqing shyly scratches his head before earnestly introducing himself. Dahuang is Yan's foremost center for agricultural research. There, the entire process is mechanized. From sowing seeds to harvesting crops, from spreading fertilizer to spraying pesticides, every step is handled by Originium machinery. It is said that there are even plates that not a single person need set foot on all year. As Wanqing speaks, he takes out all sorts of Tianshi apparatuses, displaying high-precision agricultural Originium devices we have never seen before. He also decides to show off a painstakingly-choreographed performance by his 'Sky Pole' drones...
Since time immemorial, Yan has always found it incredibly important to track agricultural yield. Countless lives are built upon that foundation of tiny seeds. Which is why an entire group of Tianshis like Wanqing dedicate themselves to agricultural research, unceasingly developing more efficient planting methods and higher quality grains. Despite their sophisticated equipment though, their research is hardly a walk in the park. Whether carefully selecting which plants in their fields meet their requirements, or imitating remote environments without access to Originium machinery, toil cannot be avoided. It is a tough life, as can be seen in Wanqing's young but toned arms and the calluses poking through his gloves. It is this sort of work that the Nongye Tianshis of Dahuang perform year after year, after which the finest seeds from their programs are sent to every corner of the country, carrying with them the wishes of their creators for a successful germination.
When asked whether he is proud of his work, Wanqing finds it hard to hide his embarrassment.
'It's hard to think about anything but farming when you're out in the field... I'm pleased whenever we get a bumper crop, and getting to see everyone eating their fill, well, that makes me happy too.'
text.zh:
虽说罗德岛上有不少干员都接触过农活，但是真正从事农业研究的学者还是令大家感到好奇。
“是不是一年到头，每天都要弯着腰在田里耕地？”
“听说在农忙的时候，从小孩到老人，都要拿起镰刀在一望无际的麦田里从早割到晚？”
面对大家投来的同情又敬佩的目光，万顷有些害羞地挠着头，认真向我们介绍道——大荒城作为炎国最重要也是最先进的农业研究基地，农业生产的整套流程基本已经全面机械化，播种收割、施肥撒药全部都由源石机械代劳，甚至有部分地块，或许一年到头都不用人走到地里。万顷一边说着，还拿出了携带的各种天师仪，展示了我们见所未见的高精度农业源石装置，以及他自己编排的“天桩”无人机的高难度编队表演……
长久以来，炎国始终对农业生产高度重视。小小的一粒种子，关系着千万人生活的根基。所以才有一众像万顷这样专门从事农业研究的天师，不断研究更高效的种植方法、更优质的谷种。虽然有先进设备的加持，但这并不意味着农业研究是件轻松的事。在地里一株株仔细挑选性状符合需求的植株，或是模拟更偏远地区没有源石机械的耕种环境，都免不了繁重的体力劳动。工作的辛苦，从万顷年轻但结实的臂膀、手上隔着手套磨出的厚茧都可见一斑。大荒城的农业天师就是这样年复一年地重复着这些工作，然后将培育出的最优质的种子送往全国各地，并在心里期待这些种子能好好生根发芽。
当被问及是否会以自己的工作为荣时，万顷也总是赧然。
“种地的时候很难想什么别的……只是看到庄稼丰收的时候会很开心，看到大家能好好吃饱饭，也会很开心。”

text.en:
In Yan, a Tianshi is an occupation that commands respect, but demands great responsibility in turn. To become part of this elite group, one needs to pass the Tianshi Bureaus' grueling exams.
They require not only outstanding talent in Arts, but also a deep pool of specialized knowledge. Thanks to Wanqing's exceptional exam results at the young age of fifteen, an exception was made for him, and he was placed under the tutelage of a senior Nongye Tianshi, Shu. Only a handful of test-takers in all of Yan meet that standard. Some suspected cheating at first, but suspicions were quickly dispelled once his performance at the Tianshi Bureaus became clear. Not only were his academic scores once-in-a-generation, his first crop breeding experiment yielded promising results. Only three years after entering the Bureaus, he'd already taken on several fellow Tianshis as students.
However, Wanqing was by no means a child prodigy. Even now, he is somewhat slow to pick up new techniques, a fact reflected in the courses he takes while on Rhodes Island. His tutor, Shu, who is just as kind as he is, says: 'using your mind always means being a touch slower than those around you, and your limbs will always be a touch slower than your mind.' Instead, he was able to achieve such amazing scores thanks to his unusual concentration and focus. As he himself puts it, if he runs into an issue while on the job, he'll simply think of a way to solve it. Thoughts such as 'maybe I could take a shortcut?' or 'what happens if I can't fix this?' never even cross his mind. While that sounds simple, it is actually quite difficult for most people to work without mulling over the consequences. 'For every step, plan three further' is an ancient Yanese saying for a reason, and its people are naturally disposed towards caution and forward planning, while always keeping an escape route in mind. This, too, can be considered a form of instinctive wisdom. However, only those who able to completely immerse themselves in the act of moving forward are able to arrive at their chosen destination.
'In earlier eras, crops still needed to be harvested by hand. More experienced farmers would tell younger ones, in all seriousness, that they must never raise their heads as they worked. Seeing the full fields stretching out to the horizon would demotivate even the hardest worker. But if you only see the stalk in your hand, then, well, you need only cut a single stalk.' Wanqing is rather serious when sharing his experiences with others, without a hint of arrogance or pride in his voice.
'While being able to focus like that is a rather rare trait, it's not always an appropriate one. Once, Wanqing accidentally broke an automatic door by bumping into it, and he silently took it on himself to fix it. By the time someone found him, he'd been at it for a full twenty-four hours... Can someone make sure to help him out the next time this happens? I'm scared that he'll starve to death.'
text.zh:
在炎国，“天师”是一种地位尊崇，并且责任重大的职业。想要跻身这一精英阶层，就要通过天师府选拔严苛的考校。
考校不仅要求考生源石技艺天赋过人，还要在专业知识上有充分的储备。而万顷在十五岁就以优秀的成绩通过了天师府考校，被破格录取为资深农业天师黍的学徒——这样的成绩放眼整个炎国也是寥寥可数。曾经也有人怀疑过这样的录取有不公之处，但是很快，万顷在天师府的表现就让所有人打消了怀疑。不仅多项科目的成绩名列前茅，而且第一次参与育种实验就做出了突出的成果。在进入天师府学习三年后，他甚至担任起部分授业天师的工作来。
万顷并不是那种少年天才的学徒，甚至许多时候，他对新事物的学习速度还要稍慢一些，这些在他学习罗德岛的课程时也有所体现。温柔如他的导师黍，也给出过“动起脑子永远比周围人慢一拍，手脚跟上脑子又要慢一拍”的评语。而万顷之所以能取得那些亮眼的成绩，还要归功于他异于常人的专注力。对于万顷来说，开始做一件事，遇到问题就去想办法解决问题，至于有没有捷径、解决不了的话会有怎样的后果，这些统统不在考虑范畴之内。道理说起来简单，但实际上人们很难不计后果地去做事。“走一步看三步”也是一句炎国老话，人们会习惯性地瞻前顾后，谋求退路，这同样是种智慧的本能。但往往只有那些埋头向前的人，才能到达最初的目的地。
“在更早的时候，人们还要亲手收割庄稼，有经验的职农会很认真地告诉年轻人，千万不要抬头。看到那连到天边的庄稼地谁都会害怕。可是如果专注在手里要割的那一株庄稼上，要割的就只有那一株。”万顷很认真地分享着自己的经验，没有一点骄傲。
“虽然专注确实是种难得的品质，但也要分场合才行吧。上次万顷不小心撞坏了一扇自动门，他就一声不吭地在那修了起来，被发现的时候他已经在那耗了一天一夜了……下次遇到这种事能不能帮帮他，我真的害怕他会饿死自己……”

text.en:
When Wanqing was registering as an operator, he came up with his codename in almost no time at all.
Dahuang focuses on several distinct problems plaguing the farmers of Yan, and is host to multiple experimental crops, each with their own name. For example, a crop bred for colder climates is named 'Kangdong', or 'Frost Resister'. If a descendant of this crop shows marked improvement during further experimentation, it would be named 'Kangdong #2'. In addition, there is also 'Zaoyou' ('Early Excellence'), 'Fanglao' ('Flood Defender'), 'Chuibudao' ('Unblowable'), 'Esichong' ('Pest Starver'), etc etc. These simple names entrust a simple hope into each and every variant. Of special note is 'Wanqing', or 'Vast Expanse'.
Since time immemorial, people have been fighting with Catastrophes for land. Catastrophes destroy buildings and farmland alike, and soil contaminated with Originium is extremely difficult to grow crops in. As such, in ancient times, Catastrophes were usually followed by famine. Since the invention of the nomadic city, most scholars of agriculture have focused on increasing the yields of food grown on nomadic plates. However, the Tianshis of the Dahuang persist in trying to breed crops resistant to Originium. But despite their long efforts, countless academics have deemed it futile.
The Dahuang Tianshis believe that limited space is a fundamental flaw of nomadic plates, and that though their research has been slow, it is only by exploiting the vast unused tracts of land that all the people of the lands can eat their fill. Generation upon generation of Tianshis have contributed, breeding crops that could tolerate more and more Originium activity. Five percent grew to fifteen percent, which blossomed further into twenty-five percent. Now though, progress is made only in fractions of a percent, with the rate of improvement inversely proportional to the time put into the experiments. Great leaps in tolerance seem to be a thing of the past. According to the Tianshis participating in the research, one could dedicate their entire life with no results to show for it, denied a place in the annals of history.
Wanqing is just one such nameless Tianshi.
'People have asked if I'm afraid I'll never see my experiments bear fruit. I used to be... because I felt that anything I did needed a result, any result, so I could face myself in the end. But I think I see the bigger picture now. A man's life may be all too short, but the road he walks is long. It isn't the destination that's the result. It's the path you follow, and the footsteps that you leave behind.'
text.zh:
万顷在罗德岛登记成为干员时，几乎没怎么犹豫就想好了自己的代号。
大荒城针对不同的农业问题，有多项育种实验。这些实验培育出的庄稼都有自己的名字，如培育出的适宜种在寒冷地区的庄稼代号就叫“抗冻”，之后的研究中，庄稼的性状如有明显的突破，则会被命名为“抗冻二号”，除此之外，还有“早优”“防涝”“吹不倒”“饿死虫”……这些质朴的名字寄托着一个个质朴的愿望。在这其中，“万顷”是尤为特殊的一项研究。
自古以来，人们始终在与天灾争夺着生存的土地。天灾会摧毁房屋与耕地，源石污染过的土地也极难再种植庄稼。所以在更古老的时候，天灾的发生也往往伴随着严重的饥荒。移动城市被发明后，多数农业学者将研究的重心放在了提高移动地块上粮食的产量上，但是大荒城天师府的部分天师，始终在坚持着培育源石耐受性高的庄稼。尽管长久以来，这被无数学者认为是不可能的事。
大荒城的天师们相信，移动地块的面积始终有限，而这项研究虽然困难，却是唯一能利用起更多土地，让生活在这片大地上的所有人都能填饱肚子的办法。经过一代又一代天师的努力，培育出的庄稼能耐受的源石活性率，从百分之五提高到百分之十五，再到百分之二十五。实验数据小数点后的数字缓慢爬升，速度与实验耗费的时间似乎完全不成正比，这项研究离真正得以推广依旧十分遥远。对于参与研究的天师来说，或许毕其一生也无法得出什么结果，也无法在书中留下自己的名字……
万顷，正是这许多无名天师中的一个。
“有人问过我，会不会害怕看不到实验得出成果的那一天。我曾经是害怕的……因为觉得既然做了一件事，总要做出什么结果，才算对自己有个交代……后来，我也想明白了。人一辈子太短，要走的路又长。不是非要走到哪里才算结果，走过的路，踩出的脚印，都是结果。”

text.en:
In modern times, 'starvation' is a rather foreign concept to most of us.
It is more than simply having to endure until the cafeteria opens for dinner because you missed lunch, or skipping a few meals for two or three days straight during a tough mission. Rather, it is the inability to obtain sufficient nutrition for a long period of time, and the pain, suffering, and despair that comes along with it. Such an experience is beyond our imagination, and the same can be said for Wanqing. However, the records of withered crops and the photos of famished crowds in his textbooks have stamped themselves into his mind's eye.
He returned to the village ruins up the large river outside the city. The ruins could very well have been his 'hometown', and he knew that his biological parents, and possibly others in his family, could easily have been in one of those starving crowds in the books. They, too, had experienced suffering unlike anything he could imagine.
Wanqing was a fortunate child, being set adrift in a basket along the river at the tender age of two, sent by the wind and the flowing waters to Dahuang, like a seed blown by the breeze and coming to rest in a rice paddy. Thankfully, he survived the experience. As the farmers would tell him, after several years of poor harvests, the year he floated in saw Dahuang a bumper crop. And that is the story of how Wanqing came to the city, where he spent his childhood after being taken in by the kind-hearted farmers. One day he would eat at a house on the east side of the village, the next he would eat on the west side. He would run madly on the ridges between rice paddies, pulling along his kite. He would clamber up the greenhouses and back down again. All in all, he was just like any other child born in Dahuang. He might not be great with words, but he remembers their kindness, deep in his heart. Ever since then, he's treated the day summer began that year as his birthday. And as if by divine providence, ten years since his fateful landing, he was back in that very same paddy, gathering the rice fortunate enough to break through to a new level of Originium tolerance.
He brings the seeds, bred with his own hands, alongside him as he sets off once more on the endless road, sending them to every corner of Yan. Wherever the wind takes these seeds, hope sprouts.
text.zh:
时至今日，“饥饿”对于我们来说或许已经是一个有些遥远的词。
并不是因为错过了食堂的饭点只能忍到下一次开饭，或是在艰难的任务中两三天无法按时进食。而是一种长时间的，难以获得足量的食物而感受到的痛苦，还有绝望。我们无从想象那是一种怎样的感觉，万顷也是如此。但是当他看到教科书上对于饥荒场面的记载，还有几张实地拍摄的受灾人群的照片，他的心被狠狠地揪住了。
他回到过城外大河上游的村庄废墟——那座最有可能是他的“故乡”的村庄，他知道，自己的生身父母，还有可能存在的其他家人，都是受灾人群中的一员，他们也经历过自己无法想象的痛苦。
万顷是幸运的，一个装在木盆里不到两岁的孩子，被风和河流送到了大荒城，像一颗被风吹起的种子，不偏不倚地落在了那片稻田里——然后幸运地存活下来。职农们告诉他，在经历了几年收成不佳的年景后，万顷漂流到大荒城的那一年，庄稼长得格外好。万顷就这样留在了大荒城，被一个个好心的职农照顾着长大。今天在东家吃饭，明天在西家过夜。在田垄间牵着风筝疯跑，在种植大棚里爬上爬下——就像生在大荒城的每一个孩子一样。万顷不善言辞，但是将这一份份善意牢牢记在了心底。后来，万顷也将那一年立夏的日子当做了自己的生日……就像是某种天意，十几年后，万顷同样在那片稻田里，捡到了一株幸运存活下来的，在源石耐受性上有突破的水稻。
现在，他带上了自己亲手培育出的种子，再一次踏上了漫长的路，他要将种子送去炎国各个地方。风吹起，种子飘落的地方，都总有希望。

text.en:
The Tianshi Bureaus have a tradition of conducting apprenticeship ceremonies whenever a young student passes their exams. They are formally placed under the care of a senior Tianshi, and the ceremonies they hold, large or small, will give some insight into their mentor's character. During Wanqing's apprenticeship ceremony, Shu gave him only a single verdant seedling.
'In the past, these ceremonies would require three bows and nine kowtows, but that's rather out of fashion these days. Take this rice seedling and plant it beneath you. We can consider it your mark of respect. I cannot teach you much myself, for all the knowledge that you wish to learn ultimately springs forth from the soil.'
Wanqing did not fully understand this, but respectfully stooped to plant the seedling in the soil beneath him. When he raised his head, he saw the endless, fertile fields, and the calming greenery that grew within them.
From that moment on, he began to put down his roots.
text.zh:
天师府有行拜师礼的传统，当一名年轻学徒通过考校，正式拜入一名前辈天师门下的时候，都会举办一些仪式，或大或小，要看前辈天师的性格。当万顷拜师时，黍只是给了他一束青翠的秧苗。
“过去拜师要三拜九叩，现在我们也不兴这么做了。这束稻苗给你，你自己种到地里去，就当你行过礼了。我能教你的不多，你要学的所有知识，最终还是要从这片土地里学来。”
万顷似懂非懂，恭恭敬敬地弯腰把稻苗插进了地里。当他抬起头，看到了望不到头的丰饶的田地，还有令人安心的绿意。
从这一刻开始，他就扎根在这儿了。
