感染已步入中期，矿石病有明显的扩散迹象，所幸及时前来罗德岛就医，目前已在一定程度上控制住了病情。

干员摆渡人的病情不容乐观，除此之外，他身上还留有大量伤痕，甚至面部也有被炮火燎烧的痕迹。据说这些疤痕，还有他的矿石病，都是他以游击队员的身份与萨尔贡人作战时留下的印记。我们不知细节，但可以想象那是多么惨烈的战斗。

text.en:
HR and Medical were on high alert following the arrival of Xanthos on Rhodes Island. While Rhodes Island has no shortage of operators who hail from countries in conflict with each other, no one calls the Sarkaz 'devils' here, nor do Kazimierzians go for the throats of every Ursine they see. But Xanthos's situation was different. Everyone had heard what happened in Athenius, and the atmosphere at the Medical Department was particularly tense whenever Xanthos came in.
He turned out to be surprisingly well-behaved, and the terrifying scene of Xanthos vs. Dr. Gavial that Lena was worried about enough to specifically warn us of never happened. People were relieved, and perhaps they began to let their guard down.
That was when the accident happened.
Dr. Warfarin had obtained a rare blood sample and was working overtime to study it, messing up the shifts and forgetting to make sure that Dr. Gavial was not on duty when Xanthos came in, resulting in the two of them coming into contact with one another. One was oblivious and the other seemingly unconcerned, but everyone else was quite panicking. Dr. Gavial read the latest checkup report, saw that Xanthos was taking his medication as instructed—bringing his condition under control—and patted his shoulder in approval, with considerable force. Everybody quite freaked out, but Xanthos said nothing. His face was hidden under his mask, but if he took it off, one would probably find a complicated expression on his face. No violence ensued, though, and Dr. Warfarin stopped worrying about staggering the shifts.
Rumors that Operator Narantuya had invited Xanthos to rob Sargonian caravans in the desert with her remain unsubstantiated, as Narantuya had promised us that she had left behind her life of banditry once and for all. All we know is that they did indeed leave the ship together once, but had returned by the time we found out, and refused to talk about what they went out to do, or what happened in the desert.
What we do know is that Xanthos has successfully integrated into Rhodes Island, and there is no concern that he will act aggressively toward operators from Sargon.

Xanthos is definitely cut from the same cloth as Aspasia alright! He's a solid survivor and a fighter—not as good as me of course, but good enough to survive in the desert. Too bad he doesn't want to become my subordinate, but I won't give up so easily!
—Narantuya
text.zh:
赞索斯来到罗德岛之后的很长一段时间里，人事部和医疗部都如临大敌。毕竟，罗德岛虽然不乏一些彼此有过冲突的国家来的干员，但至少没有人会在这里喊萨卡兹“魔族佬”，卡西米尔人也不会见到乌萨斯人就打。可是，赞索斯的情况不太一样，大家都听说了雅赛努斯发生的事，尤其是在医疗部，每当赞索斯前来就医，气氛就会变得有些紧张。
不过，赞索斯前来就医时意外地老实，让莱娜担忧到特地写信来预防的赞索斯大战嘉维尔医生的恐怖场面，也一直并未发生。虽然似乎还不能彻底放松警惕，但至少大家都松了一口气。
意外就是在松懈中产生的。
那天华法琳医生拿到了一份稀有的血液样本，一头扎进了研究中。她沉迷得忘乎所以，超时加班，打乱了换班的规划，也忘记了要将嘉维尔医生值班与赞索斯就医的时间错开，于是两人打上了照面。这两位当事人中，一人一无所知，另一人浑不在意，但除了他们自己，所有人都很担心。嘉维尔医生看完了新出的体检报告，发现赞索斯确实在遵医嘱按时服药，病情得到了控制，便也忘乎所以，猛拍他的肩膀表示嘉许——这一刻，大家的担忧达到了顶峰。不过，赞索斯一句话也没有说。虽然他的脸被面具挡住了看不到，但总感觉他当时应该表情复杂。这让人紧张的场面就这样平稳渡过，此后，华法琳医生也不再为排班的事而费心了。
至于干员娜仁图亚曾盛情邀请赞索斯同去沙漠抢劫萨尔贡商队的事，始终只是一则传闻，考虑到娜仁图亚向我们做过保证，说她已结束了自己的沙盗生涯，因此这个传言的真实性存疑。人事部只知道这两人确实曾经一同外出。但由于我们得知时两人已经回舰，且对此事的经过绝口不提，因此两人究竟是去做什么的，在沙漠中又发生了什么，这些细节也就不得而知了。
能够确定的是，如今的赞索斯已融入了罗德岛的生活，即使他遇到了萨尔贡来的干员，我们也不必担心他会做出什么过激的行为。

赞索斯不愧是阿斯帕齐娅的同胞，生存技巧和战斗水平都很不错，虽然比我还差点儿，但要在沙漠中讨生活应该不成问题！只可惜他不愿意做我手下，不过我不会放弃的！
——娜仁图亚

text.en: By Minoan standards, Xanthos is quite reserved—stiff even. We know that Minoans love drama, as citizen-organized performances are a frequent sight on the streets of Athenius, and Minoan villages often jointly hold small drama festivals during agricultural off-seasons. Xanthos, however, seems to have little interest in it. It is not that he does not know the stories of the heroes—he responds to citations of the legends in conversations—but his own words are always brief and succinct, never quoting proverbs or fables. His upbringing may have something to do with it: Xanthos was raised in a small village in southern Minos, near the border with Sargon. Life was hard even without Sargonian raids. His father died when he was very young, and he inherited his father's work as ferryman. He spent most of his time on the river, and his emotions flowed like the river, never rising or falling by too much. But the river was also fickle, and he had to be vigilant at all times, never letting his guard down. His taciturn and cautious manner is the result of such a life. This is not to imply that he has no hobbies: he has told us that reading poetry was his way of relaxing in those rare moments of leisure. The reasoning was that poems are relatively short, and do not make you forget the time or to monitor the condition of the river. Xanthos showed some interest when I invited him to join our Poetry Club, but began to hesitate upon learning that we get together and recite poems in front of other club members, apparently not used to group activities. My praise of his speech at the First Temple of Athenius seemed to have the opposite effect, as he looked visibly uncomfortable, though I was eventually able to convince him to come. That night, we read poems that we wrote ourselves, and engaged in some impromptu group poetry. Someone brought wine, which I had reservations about, though I must admit that good wine can indeed do wonders for the atmosphere. Once we got a little tipsy, we began to sing while someone played accompaniment, ending on a high note with the climax of the Kerespereia. Xanthos sat in a corner throughout, listening quietly and touching none of the wine (most admirably!), looking somewhat out of place. He continued to attend the meetings, sitting quietly in a corner as he did the first time, saying little except nodding on occasion upon hearing a particularly well-crafted verse. He seems to prefer sentimental odes to narrative epics, and takes a particular liking to the works of a certain female poet from Antisa. It seems that his appearance belies a much more delicate nature. —Erato, in Rhodes Island Poetry Club Report
text.zh:
以米诺斯人的标准来说，赞索斯算是相当拘谨，甚至称得上死板。
我们知道，米诺斯人热爱戏剧，公民自发组织的戏剧表演在雅赛努斯的街头随处可见，米诺斯乡间的大小村落在农闲时节也常会联合举办小型的戏剧节，但赞索斯似乎对此没有太多的兴趣。他并不是对各种英雄的故事一无所知，假如在与他对话时引用这些传说，他确实能够应和，但若是由他自己开启话题，那他所讲述的内容必然是简洁而务实的，不会有太多修饰，也不会引经据典。
这或许是他早年的生活造成的。赞索斯的故乡在米诺斯南部与萨尔贡边境交界之处，那是个很小的村落，即使没有萨尔贡人的侵扰，生活也很艰辛。他的父亲在他很小的时候就去世了，他接过了父亲的衣钵，成为河上的摆渡人。在故乡的绝大多数时间里，他都在河上独处，情绪随河水流淌，不会有太大的起伏。但河流的水情又是瞬息万变的，任何松懈都可能酿成惨剧，他必须全力应对，容不得一点疏忽。这一切的共同作用，让他渐渐成了现在这样寡言而谨慎的人。
但这并不代表他的生活没有丝毫的情趣。据赞索斯说，他在河上偶尔的闲暇时刻，最爱的放松活动是阅读诗集。对此，他给出的理由是诗歌的篇幅通常不会太长，不至于像小说故事一样让人沉迷到忘记时间，忘记关注河面的变化，更适合像他这样与河流相伴的人。

听说赞索斯喜欢诗歌，我就邀请他来加入我们的诗歌爱好者协会。一开始，他还有些兴趣，但得知我们会在定期活动时聚在一起，在其他爱好者们面前朗诵诗歌后，他变得迟疑起来，似乎并不太习惯这样的集体活动。于是我夸赞了他在雅赛努斯第一神殿广场上做的公开演讲，但这话好像起了反效果，他明显表现出了不自在的模样。好在最终我还是说服了他。
那天晚上，我们念了一些各自新写的诗，又彼此应和，做了一些即兴的创作。有人带来了酒——对此事我不太赞成，不过不得不承认，酒精在某些时刻，确实是调节气氛的绝好助力。分享了一些美酒之后，我们边弹琴边歌唱，气氛十分热烈，最后以《克瑞斯拉纪》中的高潮部分合颂愉快地结束了活动。在整个过程中，赞索斯都只是坐在角落里，静静地倾听，滴酒不沾——值得夸赞！——似乎有些格格不入。
在这之后，他又来了几次。每回都跟第一次一样，一个人静静地坐在角落，也不怎么说话，只在一些诗句流泻时轻轻点头，表示出欣赏之意。据我观察，相比于叙事的史诗，他似乎更偏好抒情的颂歌，尤其是那位安提萨的女诗人的作品，最能获得他的认同。这一点很有意思，他的内心似乎比他的外表要纤细许多。
——摘自《罗德岛诗歌爱好者协会定期报告》，埃拉托撰文

text.en:
The training of a priest is a serious matter in Minos. Children found to have the proper aptitude are sent to the temples to receive education and training at the age of ten, studying with a dozen other children of the same age. They are responsible for everyday cleaning and maintenance, while also studying the classics and learning about the heroes and their associated rituals. They also have to study scientific knowledge associated with the temple, as well as accumulate management and administrative experience, all in preparation for a career in the priesthood. The process can take more than a decade, until trainees pass their exams to become full-fledged acolytes. The priests of Minos are therefore among its most talented and educated people.
When we learned that Xanthos's apprentice in Athenius was a former trainee acolyte, we began to wonder—did this mean Xanthos possessed knowledge that rivaled the temples? There was, of course, an element of self-interest in our curiosity: there are patients of every age group at Rhodes Island, including young children who had to abandon their education because of their condition, and we wanted to give them an opportunity to continue learning.
Xanthos seemed to smile wryly behind his mask.
'Lykeion knew much more than I do, in terms of professional knowledge. I dealt with issues that occurred on the river through experience and instinct, accumulated through observation and memorization, while he understood the principles behind them, and could draw on such knowledge to understand things that he had never seen before. It was practical experience that he lacked... but the real reason I took him in as an apprentice was that he needed a reason to keep living after I saved... after he contracted Oripathy. I didn't need a caregiver or companion, but he needed something to fill his life, in order to find the strength to keep going. I'm glad that he's found a new goal.'
Xanthos was humble and did not immediately agree to take on apprentices at Rhodes Island, but we have noticed that he has a way with children, guiding them to fulfill their potential while showing remarkable patience. He tells stories of heroes to crying young patients, competes with Popukar to see who can cut planks faster using a chainsaw (and his oar), and steers Bubble and Ceobe to keep the corridor clear when they are playing in the hallways. Perhaps it comes from his experience observing the river—'one can only sail far and easy by going with the flow,' in his own words—or perhaps he is simply a natural educator.
text.zh:
如今在米诺斯，祭司的培养是一件非常严肃的事。通常一名被认为具备相关资质的孩童在十岁前后就会被送入神殿，与十来个年龄相仿的孩子一起成为学徒，接受教育。他们要承担一些日常的扫洒工作，维系神殿的圣洁与生机，也要诵读经典，了解英雄的故事和相关的仪式，更要广泛地学习该神殿相关领域的科学知识，甚至要积累管理和行政方面的经验，为将来的祭司工作做充足的准备。这个过程常常会持续十数年，直到学徒通过考核，成为助理祭司。也正因如此，米诺斯的祭司通常就是这个国家最有学问和才能的人。
听说赞索斯在雅赛努斯收的徒弟，曾经就是祭司学徒，我们不由得产生了好奇——这是否说明赞索斯掌握了不输于神殿的海量知识？当然，会有这样的疑问，主要也是因为我们有一些私心：如今在罗德岛就医的病人涵盖了各个年龄段，一些年纪很小的孩子因为病情不得不放弃学业，我们也希望能给他们提供各种途径来继续学习。
对此，面具后的赞索斯给出了类似苦笑的回应。
“在专业的知识上，吕刻伊昂所掌握的其实远甚于我，我只是一直在观察和记忆，靠经验与直觉来应对河上会出现的各种问题，而他知道其中的原理，也能够靠它们来理解他未曾见过的现象，他缺乏的是一些实际操作的机会。不过，在我救下他……在他感染矿石病后，他所缺乏的，就变成了一个继续活下去的目标。我是因为这一点，才收他做徒弟的。我并不需要他人的照顾与陪伴，但他需要通过这些来填充日常，让自己获得一些生活的动力。我很高兴他现在有了新的目标。”
赞索斯说得很谦虚，也并未立刻答应我们在罗德岛再收一些小孩做徒弟，不过我们确实观察到，他很擅长照顾孩子，能引导他们发掘自己的潜力，也会在这其中表现出无比的耐心。他会给哭闹的小病人讲英雄的故事，会与泡普卡比赛用电锯——以及他的桨——切割维护罗德岛需要使用的板材，泡泡和刻俄柏在走廊上打闹时，他也会将她们引导到更开阔的地方去。这可能是长期观察河流给他带来的经验——按照他自己的说法，是“只有顺着河流的水势，才能航行得更远更轻松”——也可能，他在教育一事上，本就有些过人之处。

text.en: You want to know about my life in the marshes? It wasn't like what you might find in pastoral poems. Ferrying in the marshes was not like ferrying in Athenius. It was not a simple matter of going from one side of the river to the other. Our village was surrounded by the river. Essentially, we lived in the river. The river was the most important part of life in the marshes; master the river, and you master the marshes. It was formed from rainfall and meltwater from the peaks of Mt. Hymnoi. Spring was the season for planting and irrigation, as the snow began to melt and rainfall declined. I ferried people back and forth between the village and nearby small plots of farmland, separated by the river, while keeping an eye on the snowline in the distant mountains, looking out for sudden floods. Summer was when meltwater was at its highest, the busiest season for irrigation. People guided water into the fields, and harvested young reeds which were used for weaving. Autumn was the season of harvest, with increased rainfall and reduced meltwater. The crops in the fields had to be harvested quickly, and reeds that had grown hard harvested for reserves. The river was calm in winter—villagers used harvested reeds to make handicrafts, and repaired farm tools and houses, while I ferried people between our village and neighboring villages. Reeds were a frequent sight on the river, growing along the river and marshes, forming narrow passages that only those who knew the river well could navigate successfully. Only those few could ferry the others to where fins and fowlbeasts were in abundance. Reeds were versatile materials that could be woven into baskets, mats, even houses and their foundations. We used reeds to mark out areas in the river, and filled them with reed stalks to make floating plates on which we built our homes. It may seem primitive to people used to the nomadic cities, but it was flexible and adaptable to any changes in the river. When Ithakos came, he taught us how to connect these reed plates to create large public areas, upon which we built a little temple and lit a fire that belonged to us... Life was hard, and far from affluent, but it holds a special place in my heart, not only because of the memories of home and my deceased friends and relatives, but also because it was a life that was within my grasp. All I needed to do every day was to understand the river beneath me. The river has since dried up, but it continues to flow in my heart. Having lost sight of my own heart from loss, I'm trying to understand it now, trying to tame it. Perhaps this will allow me to once again grasp my own life.
text.zh:
你想了解我过去在沼地的生活？不，它并不像你想象的那么诗意。
在沼地的摆渡工作与在雅赛努斯的不同，并不是从河的这一边到河的那一边那么简单。我们所在的地方被河流环绕，我们就居住在河流之中。河流是沼地生活最重要的部分，掌握了河流，也就掌握了沼地的生活。
在我们居住的地方，河水由荷谟伊山顶的积雪与降雨共同组成。每年春季，积雪开始融化，降雨减少，大家要开始播种灌溉，每天我会划船送村里的人到村子周围被河水划分成小块的土地上去劳作，也得留意观察远处高山的雪线，以防出现预料之外的春洪；到了夏天，融雪到达高峰，这是灌溉最繁忙的季节，需要将河水引入田地，也要收割初生的芦苇，留着做柔软的编织材料；秋天则是收获的季节，此时的降雨增多而融雪减少，田地里的作物需要尽快采收，已生长得坚硬的芦苇也得收割作为储备；而当时间来到冬天，一切安静下来，河水变得平缓，大家会用备好的芦苇做些手工，修补农具和屋子，我也会在我们的村子与邻村之间将大家接送。
芦苇是河上最常见的点缀，它们随河流和沼泽的走向生长，因此，河面会形成一条条狭小的通道，只有最了解河流的人才能在其中自由地穿行，也只有最了解河流的人，才能将大家带去鳞兽或羽兽聚集的地方捕猎。芦苇是实用的材料，可以编织篮子和筐，也可以编织垫席，甚至我们的住房，还有它的地基，都可以用芦苇来建造。我们会先用芦苇圈出足够的水域，然后一点点地将苇秆编织在里面形成漂浮的地块，再往上搭建小屋。这样的地块在见惯了移动城市的人看来或许有些简陋，但它能顺应河流的变化，在我们需要的时候，能迅速地对其进行调整。后来伊萨科斯来了，在他的设计之下，我们将这些用芦苇编织的地块拼接在一起，于是便有了大块的公共区域，可以建造属于我们沼地的小小神殿，在神殿里点燃属于我们的火焰……
那样的日子……自然是艰辛的，生活也远称不上富足，却最让我怀恋。不，不只是因为那里有我生长的家园，我故去的亲友，更重要的是，那是我能够掌控的生活。那时候的每一天，我需要做的，就只是了解我身下的河流。
是的，那条河已经干涸，可它还在我心中流淌着。在渡过了因为失去而无法看清自己内心的日子之后，如今的我也在尝试着了解它，驯服它，而后，或许，我就能再一次地，掌控我自己的生活。

text.en:
The wounds that Sargon left behind in Minos have yet to fully heal, even in the nomadic city of Athenius, far from the border. Scholars continue to piece together the cultural heritage of Minos prior to the Sargonian occupation, the priests relying on a mix of legend and imagination to recreate the ceremonies and rituals of the past. Ruins of classical buildings litter the streets; few remain intact.
We do not care about that, said the Athenians. We were free. We would build a new glory with our own hands, so long as the spirit of the heroes lived on in our hearts. Athenians smiled, put on plays on the streets, and sang at temple ceremonies, as though they had forgotten the suffering of the past—until Xanthos, the dockmaster, delivered his speech to the people of Athenius at the First Temple.
We do not care, say the Athenians now. We do not care how strong our foe is, nor the price we must pay for freedom, but we will remember the hardships along the way, and remain vigilant of our foe's cunning. And we will not forget to lay a white flower at the graves of our fallen kin.
text.zh:
萨尔贡人在米诺斯留下的伤痕，即使是在今天，在远离边境的移动城市雅赛努斯，也未能完全愈合。学者们还在艰难地拼凑着米诺斯被萨尔贡占领之前的文化遗产，祭司们只能靠想象与传说来复现旧日的祭典与仪式，街头只剩一些古典建筑的残垣断壁，几乎见不到完整的古老房屋。
但是我们不在乎，雅赛努斯人总是这么说，我们已经获得了自由，只要英雄的气概还在我们心中流淌，我们就能用自己的双手构建新的辉煌。欢笑已出现在雅赛努斯人的脸上，人们在街头表演戏剧，在神殿的仪式上放声歌唱，似乎已经忘记了曾经的苦难，直到——直到那位叫作赞索斯的渡口管理者在第一神殿的广场上发表了一场公开的演讲。
是的，我们不在乎，现在的雅赛努斯人会这么说，我们确实不在乎我们的敌人有多强大，我们也不在乎为了自由要付出多大的代价；但我们将始终铭记这一路的艰辛，警惕敌人的狡诈，而且，我们也不会忘记在战死同胞的墓前放上一束白色的花。

value.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为感染者。

infectionStatus.en: Confirmed Infected by medical examination.
infectionStatus.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为感染者。

text.en: Explorer, ore collector, and also a famous content creator on the video side of Columbia's intercity net. Contracted Oripathy due to inattentiveness on a geological excursion, and came to Rhodes Island seeking treatment. After some negotiation, she joined Rhodes Island as a specialist operator, using her ample geological knowledge and survival experience to support our teams on their many outdoor exploration missions.
text.zh: 探险家，矿石收藏家，同时也是哥伦比亚城际网络中颇为知名的社交媒体视频创作者。在地质考察过程中，不慎感染矿石病，来到罗德岛接受治疗。其后，经过交涉，作为特种干员加入罗德岛，以丰富的地质学知识和荒野求生经验，为罗德岛诸多队伍的野外探索任务提供支持。

text.en:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 5%
Thanks to noticing the symptoms early and receiving timely treatment, Operator Wulfenite's condition is relatively under control.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.15u/L
Due to the nature of her work, Operator Wulfenite must frequently enter areas with high concentrations of Originium. Even with her knowledge of protective measures, there is always the possibility her condition will worsen, and she will require close attention.
Hopefully understands her limits going forward.
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓模糊，可见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测异常，有矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】5%
由于发现较早，且治疗及时，干员钼铅的病情得到了较为有效的控制。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.15u/L
干员钼铅由于工作性质，需要经常进入高浓度源石环境，即使本人掌握充足的防护知识，病情仍存在恶化的可能，需要密切关注。
希望她未来能够量力而行。

text.en:
Operators involved in the field of geology such as Earthspirit, Eyjafjalla, and several of our other scholarly types occasionally come together for a seminar to share their research. Once Wulfenite found out about this, she applied to take part in it.
At first, the others assumed she wished to learn from them. She called herself an ore collector, after all, and many collectors were in touch with and worked alongside geologists—an arrangement all present were familiar with.
But they quickly realized that she was no ordinary collector.
She was an incredible font of geological knowledge. While she would awkwardly twiddle her thumbs when the researchers spoke about theory, whenever a piece of ore she was familiar with was put on the table, she would happily go on and on about all its properties. The ore that inspired her codename, wulfenite, is a topic she is especially well-versed in. She knows everything about it, having even visited every single source of the ore within Columbia's borders. It was then that the other operators realized she did actually have a solid grounding in theory. She simply wasn't systematically deriving and discussing it like an academic would.
She also turned out to have some extremely obscure knowledge. Some of it was related to questions the researchers had always wondered about but never had the time to look into, while other parts involved things they had heard of but wouldn't know how to begin researching. To their surprise, Wulfenite took the time to go through that list of topics and verify them one by one.
However, the greatest change her participation caused in these seminars was that, at her urging, some of the quieter operators who only really talked about research also started sharing amusing anecdotes from their surveys. Several seminars even had to be extended for an hour due to this.
Afterwards, the participating operators would say they originally considered these incidents to irrelevant, but Wulfenite showed them that these trifles, or rather, personal experiences, were also worth sharing.
'Not only is she a new friend, she also pushed us to get to know each other better. She's one hell of a girl, I tell you.'
text.zh:
作为同样对地质学有研究的干员，地灵、艾雅法拉还有其他一些学者干员偶尔会召开交流会，聚在一起分享各自的研究。钼铅得知后，主动申请参加了交流会。
一开始，干员们以为她是抱着学习的心态来的，毕竟，钼铅自称矿石收藏家，许多收藏家都跟地质学者有联络和合作，大家对此习以为常。
但是，很快干员们就发现，钼铅和普通的收藏家完全不同。
钼铅的地质学储备相当惊人，和普通的学者不同，如果只是围绕某种理论展开讨论，她会感到棘手。但是，由一块她熟知的矿石出发，她可以滔滔不绝地说出与这块矿石有关的各种地质知识。尤其是她的代号来源，钼铅矿，她能说出与这种矿石有关的一切，甚至去过哥伦比亚境内所有的钼铅矿产地。大家这才发现，她其实知道那些理论和知识，只是，她并没有像学者那样进行系统性的归纳与整理。
其次，她还同时掌握了一些十分冷僻的信息，其中有些是对学者们来说心痒却又不愿意耗费时间去证实的消息，有些是他们有所耳闻却不知该如何下手的秘辛，而钼铅居然都花费了时间一一证实。
不过，钼铅的到来带来的最大变化，还是在她的带动下，几位沉默寡言，只说学术性内容的干员，也试着分享了一些在地质考察中遇到的趣事，以至于有几次交流会的时间被生生拉长了一个小时。
与会的干员们会后纷纷表示，他们原本以为自己遇到的那些小事微不足道，但钼铅让他们知道，这些小事，或者说，个人的体验也有分享的价值。
“我们不仅仅是多了钼铅一个朋友，她还让我们彼此更加亲近，她真是个不可思议的女孩。”

text.en:
Wulfenite isn't shy about sharing her videos from when she first started recording her adventures.
Rather than records of her exploits, they would be more accurately described as recordings of her rambling to herself. A girl out in the wilds holding up a camera, recounting to the lens what happened to her that day.
They are very different from the videos she uploads onto the intercity net, in that they are much more personal, but through them, we catch a glimpse of the start of her recorded life of derring-do.
'At first, I recorded myself so I wouldn't get too... you know, lonely. I know there's not much you can do about it when you're searching for ore, but sometimes, the loneliness really gets to you.
'A friend once told me I didn't have the right personality for solo exploring. And I don't. I usually look for stuff in the middle of nowhere, and nobody wanted to be my survey partner. But I didn't want to give up because of that, so I came up with this instead.
'At first, I was just talking to myself, but soon, I started imagining my parents or my friends behind the lens. That they were right there with me, and I'd chat with them.
'Frankly, I wouldn't have even thought to upload my first video if a tech-savvy friend of mine hadn't done it for me. Who knew so many people would be into that stuff? But with her encouragement, I made my own account and started doing this sort of stuff with a bit more purpose.
'Right, that's the video. I'd been combing the wilds for days with nothing to show for it. I wasn't in the best mood, and was really homesick, so I recorded it. Man, all that crying I did to the camera was a real long time ago, now that I think about it.'
text.zh:
钼铅毫不避讳地向我们分享了一些她刚开始记录自己的冒险时拍摄的视频。
这些视频与其说是记录冒险，不如说是在记录她的自言自语——一个女孩，在荒野上，举着摄像机，对着镜头诉说当天发生的事情。
这些视频和她后来在城际网络上发布的视频截然不同，非常私人化，但是，通过这些视频，我们也足以窥见她用这种方式记录自己冒险生活的起点。
“一开始，我会拍视频，其实是因为——太寂寞了。虽然为了寻找矿石，我知道这也是没有办法的事，但是，有的时候，孤独是会击溃你的。
“有一个朋友说，我这种性格其实不适合独自探险，我也不否认啦，我要找的矿石一般都分布在很偏僻的地方，没有多少人会陪我一起去，但是，我也不想就这样放弃呀，所以，我想到了这个方法。
“最初，我只是在自言自语，但很快，我开始想象镜头的对面是我的父母或者朋友，想象他们在我的身边，我会和他们聊些什么。
“其实第一支视频，是我一个对网络比较熟悉的朋友帮我上传的，我也没想到，会有那么多人喜欢我分享的这些东西。在她的鼓励之下，我才开设了自己的账号，并且开始有意识地去做这些事情。
“对，就是这支视频。那时，我在荒野上探索了很多天都没有收获，心情很不好，又很想家，于是录下了这支视频。那天我对着镜头哭得稀里哗啦的，现在想起来，已经过去很久了。”

text.en: Rhodes Island is no stranger to sociable people who like participating in or organizing group activities, but Wulfenite has managed to make a name for herself even in that crowded space. She's had her share of memorable moments, but the one that left the deepest impression on others is the ore exhibition and exchange she held soon after she joined Rhodes Island. Generally, so long as a sensible plan is provided in writing, Rhodes Island is always willing to provide its operators space to hold events for whatever activities they are passionate about, as well as some support. However, when Wulfenite submitted her proposal to Logistics, the operator who received it felt a twinge of doubt. The proposal itself was extremely comprehensive, and she did indeed have enough samples to stock the exhibit, but the amount of space she requested was simply ridiculous. At first, the logistics operator simply assumed she was unaware of the scale she was asking for, but she repeatedly claimed to know what she was doing, and that she had proof: many patients and operators alike had already expressed through various means their desire to participate. After tallying up the responses, Logistics accepted her application, and after asking Amiya for further instructions, the exhibition finally got the green light. It was then that something happened, something that shocked all of Logistics. A week before the event, a padishah suddenly paid a visit to Rhodes Island. At the same time, a truck transporting a massive chunk of wulfenite ore, escorted by the padishah's men-at-arms, stopped a safe distance away from the landship. Wulfenite's proposal did mention that she would be displaying something related to her codename, which also happened to be what got her into ore collecting in the first place: a giant hunk of wulfenite ore. But everyone had assumed she would simply break off a piece of her special rock to display. Instead, the ore was going to be exhibited in its entirety. Not only that, but the padishah was greatly looking forward to perusing the exhibition, just like everyone else. 'Hmm? No, my granddad used to be one of the royal guards, sure, but that's all. He wasn't anyone special to the padishah. 'It was only after I went back to the city and helped the padishah find some ore that we became friends.' After her rather understated explanation, she turned back to the crowd and started managing the exhibition. As an ordinary person who could call a padishah friend and make so many more in such a short time aboard Rhodes Island, Wulfenite's social skills are apparent at a glance.
text.zh:
罗德岛上绝对不乏擅长社交、喜欢参与和组织集体活动的人，但钼铅依然算得上是其中的佼佼者。
她能被人记住的事迹有许多，不过其中最让人印象深刻的，恐怕是她刚加入罗德岛不久时举办的那场矿石展览交流会——
原则上，只要能够拿出合理的企划书，罗德岛总是愿意为干员们腾出场地举办他们热衷的活动，并且提供一定的支持。
当钼铅将矿石展览交流会的企划书递交给后勤部时，后勤部的干员感到了一丝疑惑，展会本身的企划内容非常完善，钼铅能够提供展览的矿石数量也十分充足，但是，她申请的场地规模却超乎想象。
后勤部干员一度以为她对于自己的申请没有清晰的认知，但钼铅一再表示，她知道自己在做什么，并且找来了相应的证明——许多病人和干员都通过各种渠道表示，他们希望能够参加这场展会。
经过人数统计，后勤部认可了她的申请，在请示过阿米娅后，这份企划终于还是得到了批准。
然后，令所有后勤部干员震惊的事发生了，展会的前一周，一名帕夏突然造访罗德岛本舰，同时，一辆运载着一块巨大的钼铅矿的卡车，在帕夏军队的护送下停在了罗德岛本舰的安全距离外。
钼铅的企划书上，确实写着会展览有关她代号的来源，同时也是她开始收藏矿石的起点——一块巨大的钼铅矿，但所有人都以为，她或许会从那块对她有特殊意义的钼铅矿上切下一点拿来展览。
然而，这块钼铅矿现在被原模原样地运送到了展会，不仅如此，帕夏本人也和其他观众一样，饶有兴趣地穿行在展柜之间。
“嗯？不，我的祖父曾经只担任过帕夏大人的卫兵，帕夏大人并不认识他。
“是我后来重新造访那座城市时，帮帕夏大人找到了一些矿石，然后和帕夏大人成了朋友。”
她轻描淡写地解释完，就转身回到人群中，开始了展会的主持工作。
能够以普通人的身份和一位帕夏结交，还能在加入罗德岛以来这么短的时间内结交这么多的朋友，钼铅的社交能力可见一斑。

text.en:
There is one thing Wulfenite's fans often talk about: she was a real pioneer in registering her account and uploading videos, and her videos are very high quality, but there are extreme gaps between her uploads, often months at a time. Due to her upload schedule, she was never very popular.
However, that all changed one day when she suddenly started uploading videos en masse, with even better content and presentation than ever before. This was usually a sure sign of a content creator going commercial, but she never showed any indication of going down that path, nor of wanting to chase more popularity. The fans were unsure what to make of the situation.
The answer was simple, and only requires a glance at her medical history: it was around that time when she contracted Oripathy. Her fans, and even the people she worked with, had no idea about her illness.
'Only after catching Oripathy did I realize that so many people on the intercity net were also fellow sufferers. We became friends, and I learned something: to people like us... the net's a place where we can have our former lives back, even if just for a little bit.'
Exploring the wilds, hauling your finds back to town, sharing your results... Once, she would have done the sharing on classroom podiums or even TV studios, but now, she chooses to record videos and use social media for communication. Most assume she's a net addict, unwilling to live in reality, but they never expect to hear that she simply has no other choice.
Wulfenite has many public social media accounts she actively uses to record and share her life. Observant fans have noticed that whenever these accounts begin to make a stir, it means she's back from a trip.
Her posts are just as passionate as her videos, which makes those watching her believe that she acts exactly the same way whether on the net or in real life. What they don't know is that behind the facade is someone racked with worry day in and day out. She had no choice but to bear the pressure of keeping her Oripathy hidden.
When she was out exploring, she lived in her videos. When she returned to the city, she lived on social media. Compared to most other net celebrities who were only aiming to boost their popularity, Wulfenite appeared to be a completely virtual being. For a while, her fans were obsessed with finding out where she lived in real life, but over time, they gradually stopped caring.
From the moment she arrived on Rhodes Island, her voracious desire for social interaction was apparent. One can even say her life and her personality were at complete odds.
However, despite it all, she has managed to stay optimistic and tenacious throughout.
'It's true that I didn't have a choice at first, but when I started to take the net seriously, I found that it's actually a real interesting place. It's no big deal if you're Infected online—nobody cares.'
text.zh:
钼铅的粉丝们常常会讨论一件事：钼铅开设账号及上传视频的时间很早，视频内容也颇为优质，但更新间隔很长，经常要等几个月甚至半年时间，这使得她的人气一直不高。
但是，从某天起，她忽然大量地上传视频，制作形式和内容也更加精良。这本该是一个视频创作者即将步入商业化道路的信号，她却并没有更进一步的举措，也没有展现出为自己继续积攒人气的欲望。粉丝们搞不明白，这个时间点究竟意味着什么。
答案很单纯，只要看过钼铅的病历单就知道了——那是她刚感染矿石病的时候。而她的粉丝们，甚至和她有工作交接的人们，并不知道她已经感染了矿石病。
“在感染矿石病后，我才通过一些途径了解到，有不少在城际网络上活跃的人都是矿石病患者。我和他们成为朋友，并且明白了一件事——对我们这样的人来说……城际网络能够让我们一定程度上，继续过去的生活。”
在荒野中探险，将成果带回城市之中，分享成果……曾经，她会走入教室，站上讲台，或者踏入电视台的影棚，但现在，她选择录制视频，使用社交软件实现交流。周围的大部分人只当她偏爱城际网络而疏离了现实，却没想到她是不得已而为之。
钼铅有不少公开的社交账号，她积极地通过这些社交平台记录和分享自己的生活。对关注她的人来说，这些账号开始活跃的时候，就是她探险回来了的时候。
她的文字与视频中的她一样热情，这让关注她的人相信，城际网络上的她与现实中的她别无二致。他们并不知道，这一切背后，是一个个充满忧虑的日与夜——她不得不承受对他人隐瞒矿石病的压力。
不仅如此，当她出门探险时，她活在那些她上传的视频中；当她回到城市时，她则活在社交平台上。和大部分只将网络当成宣传工具的城际网络红人相比，钼铅似乎更像是网络上的一个虚拟存在。某一时期，粉丝们热衷于找寻她所处的位置，但久而久之，大部分人逐渐不再关心现实的她居于何处。
从她来到罗德岛后表现出的强烈社交欲足以看出，这样的生活方式与她的性格甚至可以说是相悖的。
不过，关于这一点，钼铅展现出了一以贯之的乐观与坚强——
“一开始确实是不得已，但是随着我开始认真对待网络，我发现，网络其实很有趣。在网络上，矿石病患者的身份并不特殊，我们不会因此影响任何人。”

text.en:
Wulfenite carries a lot of specialized survey equipment with her: a compass, a scratch kit, a pickaxe, miniature explosives, even a portable rock crusher.
Having learned from dealing with other exploration-inclined operators, Engineering is always ready to help repair equipment whenever they return from a trip. However, with Wulfenite they noticed her tools were always near-pristine, with barely a mark on them, yet she clearly wasn't coming back empty-handed.
How does she do it? With this question eating away at them, a certain Engineering operator volunteered to come along on her next sojourn.
The operator was unsure whether to laugh or cry when the truth became clear.
It was not that Wulfenite did not want to use her tools. She simply had no need to.
Her tail was able to wind around strategic spots on rock faces to help her climb.
It could also easily crush solid rock into powder.
It could smash through cliff faces, allowing her to bypass difficult terrain.
Yes, it is her impressive tail that lets her solve most of the issues she runs into.
The fact of the matter is, at least according to that operator's observations, Wulfenite would have a much easier time if she simply stopped lugging around all that equipment. She herself is skeptical, though.
As long as she has her tools, she can feel at ease. If she ever lost them, she would become anxious, and her exploration would go much less smoothly.
If her tools had souls, and knew that their only purpose was to provide emotional support, they wouldn't know whether to laugh or to cry either.
Better to be prepared than unprepared, though. Perhaps they will actually come in handy one day.
text.zh:
钼铅随身携带着大量用于地质考察的专业设备——指南针、硬度笔、镐子、小型炸弹，甚至是一台便携的碎石机。
有其他探险家干员的前车之鉴，工程部已经习惯了每次在他们归来的时候，帮他们维修随身携带的各种道具，但是，到了钼铅这里，他们发现，她随身携带的那些工具几乎不会损坏，甚至没有多少使用痕迹，而她的成果又证明，她并没有半路就打道回府。
她是怎么做到的？带着这个疑问，一名工程干员主动提出，跟着她进行一次外出探险。
结果令这名干员哭笑不得。
并不是钼铅不想使用这些工具，而是她没有使用的必要。
她的尾巴可以缠住各种险要的地形帮助她进行攀爬。
她的尾巴可以轻易地令石头碎成粉末。
她的尾巴可以击穿岩壁，让她在困难的地形中穿行。
是的，她那条傲人的尾巴，足以解决大多数在探险中遇到的问题。
事实上，根据这名干员的观察，如果钼铅卸下随身携带的这些工具，她的探险恐怕会进行得更加顺利。但对于这一点，钼铅本人却并不相信。
她觉得有这些工具在，她才能够安心下来，如果失去了这些工具，她会变得心神不宁，自己的探险也将无法顺利进行。
如果工具们有自己的灵魂，得知自己存在的意义竟是为主人提供情感上的支持，恐怕也会哭笑不得吧。
不过，不怕一万就怕万一，说不定有一天，它们真的会派上用场呢？

value.en: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.
value.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为非感染者。

infectionStatus.en: Medical tests have confirmed that no infection is present.
infectionStatus.zh: 参照医学检测报告，确认为非感染者。

text.en: Historian of the Imperial Historical Cabinet, and author of the best-selling culinary essay collection 'Baizao Cuisine & Food Culture'. Currently a guest at Rhodes Island through the introduction of Operator Blaze.
text.zh: 行箸，就任于炎国太史阁的历史研究者，畅销美食类散记《百灶食珍录》作者。经干员煌介绍，以访客身份来到罗德岛。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Xingzhu shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.16u/L
Operator Xingzhu takes great care when coming into contact with Originium.

She shared a little tradition from her hometown, which is located upon an Originium deposit. She wears her jade ring with the patterns pointing to the fingertip, which is meant to ward against the poison of Originium and prevent it from entering the body. Children are taught such traditions by the elders of the family from a very young age.
—A Medic Operator
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员行箸没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.16u/L
干员行箸在接触源石时做的防护措施非常到位。

行箸干员分享了有趣的“习俗”——玉石戒指上的纹路要朝向指尖的方向，意思是源石污染不入体内。据说她住在一座坐落在源石矿脉上的城市，很多防护习惯都是从小跟家里老人学的。
——某医疗干员

text.en:
Blaze had been busy lately. She had been asking other operators about their hometowns' traditional delicacies, submitted multiple procurement requests, and was paying close attention to the arrival of Messengers. Picking my words carefully, I asked if someone she knew was visiting.
While she is normally cheerful and straightforward, I had never heard her talk about her family, so I thought it best to be tactful.
Indeed, even such a carefully worded question made her frown and mull over it. In the end, her hesitant answer surprised everyone in the room: 'I guess you could say... my little sister's coming. She finally finished what she's been doing, and she'll be coming back with me to Victoria.'
'Sister?! You have a sister?!'
'Hehe...'
'How old is she?'
'...We were born on the same day.'
Twins?! Looking at Blaze, clothes still soaked in sweat from a training session, I could only picture someone just like her: loud and cheerful, with the same black ears and eyes.
'Then all those snacks from different countries that you bought...'
'Yeah, she eats six meals a day.'
A big eater! But not too shocking, if she's Blaze's sister.
'So you cleaned up your desk because...'
'Nothing gets past her eyes! She'll know everything I don't want her to if I just leave my stuff lying around.'
An inquisitive spirit, too.
Seeing how busy Blaze was, I decided to help out and prepare a training room for them. Given that she was Blaze's sister, I expected them to have a friendly brawl first thing after meeting up.
'Hey, guys, er... this is my little sister.'
My brain froze for a moment. Blaze's 'twin sister' turned out to be a polite, mild-mannered young lady with spotless white ears and tail. The two of them were nothing alike. Indeed, one could say they were polar opposites.
'Who are you calling a little sister?' This 'sister' of Blaze's retorted with a smile. 'We don't know who was born first, do we?'
The woman by the name of Xingzhu was friendly and graceful, sharing snacks she brought from Yan with us. As she left the office with Blaze, we all had the same question in our hearts, but none of us felt comfortable asking it aloud—
Who actually is this 'sister', born on the same day but sharing not a single thing in common?
text.zh:
煌最近格外忙碌。她四处打听各位干员家乡的美食，跑了好几趟采购部提交订购申请，还十分关注信使的动向。我斟字酌句地问出了那个问题：“煌，有认识的人要来看你了吗？”
煌平时大大咧咧，待人真诚，这样的她却从未提过自己的家庭情况，谈话中自然避免提起比较好。
果然，即便是小心问出的问题，也让煌陷入了一时的烦恼。她思考一番，迟疑地说出了办公室里所有人都没想到的答案：“是……我妹吧。终于忙完了手头的事，准备跟我一起回一趟维多利亚。”
“你妹？你有妹妹？！”
“哈……”
“比你小几岁？”
“……和我同一天生的。”
双胞胎？！瞪着煌那刚刚操练完，一身热汗的样子，一个和煌一模一样的黑耳朵大眼睛常常爽朗大笑的热血姑娘形象已经出现在我的脑中。
“那你采购的各国小食……？”
“是，我妹一天能吃六顿的样子。”
是个超能吃的主！不过既然是煌的双胞胎妹妹，也没什么好意外的。
“那你收拾你的办公桌……”
“唉！什么都瞒不过她的眼睛。要是东西都放在外面，那我的所有‘家底’都被她看去了。”
哦，还是个爱八卦的机灵鬼。
看着煌那么忙忙碌碌的，我也试着给她出点力。她妹妹登舰的那天，我提前收拾好了一间训练室——既然是煌的双胞胎妹妹，两人见面，干一架交流感情也很正常吧？
“呃，大家……这个，我妹。”
我的思维有一瞬停滞了。站在煌身边的这位，“双胞胎妹妹”，竟是一位柔和文静、风度翩翩的淑女……纤尘不染的白耳朵白尾巴，浑身上下没有一点与煌相似，说是相反也不为过。
“谁先出生还说不定吧。”“妹妹”笑着反驳。
这位叫行箸的姑娘，礼数周到又大方，亲切地与我们打招呼，还将她从炎国带来的点心分给我们。她与煌并肩离开办公室后，我们面面相觑。大家心中有着相同的疑惑，却又感到不便深究——
这位与煌同一天出生却没有任何相似点的“妹妹”，与她到底是什么关系？

text.en:
I have gotten into the habit of reading Xingzhu's gourmet reports. There is a simplistic charm to her writing, true to her experience as a historian, and her accounts are filled with interesting anecdotes.
March 7th. Upon trying a fin dish, she recalls that one of her strengths when she was little was being good at getting small finbones out of her mouth.
May 8th. After an argument with her supervisor about whether to include a certain entry in the historical records, they awkwardly shared a table at a snack stand in front of the Imperial Historical Cabinet's office. After biting into some unripe green plums, she looked up to see her supervisor's face scrunched up from the sourness. They both looked at each other and laughed.
She attached delicate sentiments to food, and reading her gourmet reports is like reading a slice of life.
Interestingly, by searching her pen name I also found a number of side accounts. It did not take long to understand why she used them: Xingzhu's writing style is reserved but also straightforward, mincing no words if there are any deficiencies in the ingredients or the preparation of a dish, which unsurprisingly earned the ire of more than a few restaurants. Xingzhu herself seems entirely unconcerned though, occasionally poking fun at it in her books before continuing to write her blunt and honest reviews, perhaps under a different account.
Following the trail of pen names, I found another account by the name of 'SpringNightsBanquet' on a novel website, which had numerous novels published—and was getting far more Likes than her gourmet reports. Yet Xingzhu never once mentioned that she wrote novels, nor was there anything in her onboarding files.
I started browsing through one, expecting a historical novel or perhaps a food essay, only to be increasingly bewildered by what I was reading. Wait, is this a... I scrolled up and took a good look at the title. 'The Twin Moons Playing With a Flower'?! Wait, so the moons are...?! And the flower?! Oh dear. Last update... last night, right after Xingzhu submitted her work report.
I closed the webpage, took a deep breath, and decided not to search for her side accounts anymore.
—Anonymous HR Operator
text.zh:
我已经养成了读行箸小姐美食评论的习惯。本职历史研究使她的文风有种质朴的迷人，她所记录的内容也充满生活趣味，比如：
3月7日，她出门吃鳞，鳞肉入口，回想起儿时细数自己的优点，竟还有一条“善吐鳞刺”，不禁莞尔。
5月8日，与上司为某条史料收录与否发生了争执，后又在太史阁门口的小吃摊尴尬地坐了同一桌。尝到了没熟的青梅，抬眼发现上司的脸皱成了“囧”字，两人对视，抚掌大笑。
她将细腻的情感寄托在食物上，读她的美食评论时也会读到她的生活点滴，十分易于共情。
有趣的是，顺着她的笔名，我还搜到了她的一堆小号。稍加阅读后，我很快明白了小号的意义。行箸小姐的文字风格虽然恬淡，但她的评语却十分直白。一道菜无论是用料上的差池还是手法上的瑕疵，她都会直接指出，少不了得罪一些饭店老板，甚至好几个饭店公开表示不欢迎她来点评。不过，行箸小姐对此十分看得开，甚至还会在自己的书中调侃此事，下次换个号继续点评店里的其他菜，而她之后的点评依旧实事求是。这恐怕也是行箸小姐作为历史研究者的独特行事风格了。
顺着笔名继续搜索，我注意到了某个同样属于她的账号，叫“春夜宴”，出现的地点是一个小说平台，名下有大量的小说，其点赞量远超她的美食评论。原来行箸小姐还会写小说？可她不仅对此只字未提，入职资料里也没有写。
我猜测她的小说会是戏说历史之类，或者美食文。然而我越读正文内容，越觉得不可思议。等等，这是一本……！我返回重读小说标题——“双月戏花记”？！这个月，这个花，是、是那样的意思吗？啊啊啊，最近更新时间……是昨天晚上，行箸小姐提交工作报告后……
我关闭了网页，深吸一口气，决定不再擅自搜索她的小号。
——某位不愿意透露身份的人事干员

text.en:
What you did deserves to be recorded in the history books—these were the words of encouragement a worried Xingzhu had for Blaze after a particularly dangerous mission. For her part, Blaze did not think what she did was especially notable, but she was curious what kind of people tend to get their names in the history books. 'The Imperial Historical Records? People who have affected the livelihoods and thoughts of the masses. The greater their influence, the more people they affect, the bigger the mark they leave on history.' Since the people who left a mark in Xingzhu's eyes were massively influential, Blaze was sure she was just joking when she said that she deserved to be in the history books.
One day, they sat down together for a drink. With hazy eyes, Xingzhu spoke as if muttering to herself:
'The nanny who brought me up died when I was in school. On her deathbed, I told her I wanted to write her epitaph. She said it wasn't necessary, that she was just an ordinary person, after all. I begged and begged, and at long last she agreed.
'I sat by her side, and together we recalled the major events of her life. I filled an entire notebook, but even then I felt it wasn't enough. I didn't want to leave anything out. But the first thing I saw when I left her room was the tombstone her family had prepared for her.
'That's when I realized I could only fit a brief description on it, a few events from her entire life, and I couldn't hold back my tears anymore.
'Then... I started writing about the little people, the ones the history books leave out. I wanted my pen to remember you, all of you.'
Listening to this, Blaze remembered Xingzhu's words, and laughed. 'So it wasn't a joke after all.'
text.zh:
煌所做之事，应被载入史册——在一次煌执行了极其危险的任务回来后，行箸带着忧心的表情这样鼓励了她。然而煌并不觉得自己有那么了不起，反倒好奇在她的工作中，怎样的人会被记入史册。“你说太史阁？影响到百姓生计和民间思潮的人，影响越大，涉及的人越多，溪流汇成汪洋，自然就会在史书中留下汹涌而过的痕迹了。”煌认为入得行箸眼的都是些影响力巨大的人物，愈发觉得她那句“载入史册”只是个随口一说的玩笑话。
后来有一次，两人饮酒谈心，行箸醉眼朦胧，喃喃地、如同自言自语般地提起了一件事：
“我读书期间，照顾我长大的保姆去世了。她垂危时，我提出想为她写墓志，她说自己只是一介普通人，我苦苦央求她才同意。
“我与她一道回想她一生的大事，我记了整整一册，怎么也记不够，哪一件都不舍得丢。但是，走出她房间的时候，我看到了家里为她准备的墓碑。
“我突然意识到，墓碑只有这么大，我只能从她的一生中挑零星几件事放上去。于是忍了一天的眼泪怎么也止不住了。
“后来……我就开始记录。史书会落下许许多多小人物，但我想用我的笔记住你，记住你们。”
煌听完她的喃喃自语，回想了一番那时她的话，噗嗤笑出来：“原来不是玩笑话……”

text.en: The baby-delivering fowlbeast asked the black and white cats, born on the same day, which one to send to the family that had produced generations of government officials. The white cat knew her destiny did not lie there and shrank back, so the fowlbeast took the black cat. The black cat was confident and strong. The fact that she was the 'stray kin' of a distant clan did not make her timid, and her star shone bright even in a family full of such stars. She went into the Tianshi Bureau, found those she wanted to protect, found what she wanted to change, and never strayed from her path. The white cat drifted to a distant land. Timid and cautious, she did not know where to go when she got Oripathy, so she took a notebook and traveled the land. It turned out that this life was not so bad, and she began to write book after book about her travels... All was as it should have been, as they should be. —Excerpt from a draft of a novel, discarded by Xingzhu 'If we were never swapped—I can't even imagine it! Where would I be, if not here? You should keep writing! Now I'm curious.' Xingzhu shook her head. 'We've already embarked on a path that doesn't belong to us. No amount of words can make things right...' Blaze's eyes went wide. 'What do you mean, make things right?' 'I always felt like I owed you... ow!' Xingzhu covers her forehead with a hand, wincing in pain. She looks up to see Blaze with her hand raised, preparing to flick her forehead again. 'S-Stop, my eyes are already tearing up from the pain...' 'Then I owe you an apology. And now we're even.'
text.zh:
送子仙羽兽问同一日出生的黑猫与白猫，哪位应该送去那官宦世家？白猫知道自己的命运不在于此，向后缩了缩，仙羽兽便叼走了黑猫。
黑猫自信且强大，不会因为自己“远房遗孤”的身份就谨小慎微，即便在那群星闪耀的大家族中也毫不逊色。顺利地进入天师府，找到了自己想保护的人，想改变的事，从此一往无前。
白猫则飘摇到了异国他乡。她胆小且谨慎，身染矿石病，不知何去何从，便选择带着一本笔记浪迹天涯。在这片大地上四处游历，竟也自得其乐，写下一本又一本游记……
一切本该如此，本应如此。
——被行箸放弃的小说草稿

“如果我们当初没被交换——哈哈，我想不出来，我如果不是现在这样，会是什么样。写出来啊，我很感兴趣！”
行箸摇头：“我们到底已经走上了本不属于我们的路。无论怎么写，有些事都抚不平……”
煌莫名其妙地睁大了眼睛：“抚不平什么？”
“煌……我一直觉得，自己欠你一个道……哎哟！”行箸狼狈地捂住了自己的额头，看到煌举着手，还准备弹第二下。
“别别，疼，眼泪都疼出来了……”
“那我也欠你一个道歉。我们互不相欠了。”

text.en:
The leaves of wild shepherd's purse become too tough in tofu soup if they are picked too late, making it feel as though one is chewing on dried grass. So grandpa and I uprooted the roses in the garden, and tried our hand at planting them ourselves. But it seemed this vegetable would rather grow on the sides of the street than be cared for by us. The seeds would not sprout properly if not sown well, or if it was too warm, as was the case in our garden.
I stopped tending to the garden when grandpa moved out. I fell ill in the winter of that year, and was hardly able to eat anything. The cook brought a bowl of tofu and shepherd's purse soup, but the leaves were too tough, so I took it back to the kitchen.
The cook said the shepherd's purse in the garden had sprouted after it snowed, and she picked them from there. She said that grandpa had been in the kitchen, pondering over a piece of tofu: 'What to do with this tofu if there are no such leaves?' We both laughed, and I finished the bowl of soup. On my way back to my room, I stopped by the garden, and laughed again when I realized that grandpa's ways of coaxing me had never changed, even after all these years. The garden was filled with shepherd's purse, but not the type we planted.
—Excerpt from the Baizao Cuisine & Food Culture, Volume 3
text.zh:
豆腐羹里的荠菜若采用街边挖来的，收晚了叶就不够嫩，有嚼枯草之感。我便与爷爷铲了院子里的几棵月季，在地里自己种。不想这小小野菜，宁愿在街边蓬勃生长，也不屑受我与爷爷的照顾。荠菜的种细小，撒得不好，不出苗；喜寒，院子里太暖和也不出苗。
后来家中发生了许多事，爷爷不在家了，这一方田地我就没有再管了。到年末，卧病，连续两日粒米未进，厨房送来一碗荠菜豆腐羹。荠菜入口，老得嚼不动，我便端去还给了厨房。
厨娘说，那场雪后，院子里的荠菜就发芽了，她便是从那里摘的。她说，爷爷之前种不出菜，在厨房烦恼：“没有荠菜，这块豆腐做点什么好呢？”我与她都笑了出来。我于是把那碗荠菜豆腐羹重新端起来喝了。回房路上，我去看了那片地，不禁失笑——爷爷哄人的手法，从我小时候起就没变过。好一片郁郁葱葱的荠菜，却并不是我们当时栽下的那个品种。
——摘自《百灶食珍录·卷三》

text.en: Before his brief stint with Nine's new Reunion movement, the Victorian optician Nowell traveled across Terra in search of someone, making a living with his optician skills. After the Londinium incident, Nowell was reunited with a former customer who introduced him to Rhodes Island.
text.zh: 诺威尔，维多利亚配镜师。在与九及其领导的新整合运动短暂同行前，曾于泰拉多地游历寻人，同时以为当地人配镜维持生计。伦蒂尼姆事件结束后，诺威尔与往日的一位顾客重遇，经其引荐，开始与罗德岛接触。

text.en:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Operator Nowell shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.08u/L
Operator Nowell scored full marks on Medical's standard Oripathy prevention quiz, and demonstrates a degree of understanding of applied Arts theory. His cautious and logical approach towards knowledge is also to be commended.

'He can take over the Introduction to Oripathy seminar for new operators as far as I'm concerned.'
—Warfarin
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓清晰，未见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测未见异常，无矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为非矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】0%
干员诺威尔没有被源石感染的迹象。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.08u/L
干员诺威尔在医疗部的矿石病防护知识例行提问中对答如流，对源石技艺实用理论也表现出相当程度的了解。通晓某方面知识且始终对其保持谨慎严肃的态度，这种精神实在令人敬佩。

“给新干员开的矿石病科普系列讲座就让他去得了，我看他不是全答对了吗？”
——华法琳

text.en:
Operator Nowell was born in Victoria, though he does not remember exactly where. Based on his Gaulish accent, we speculate that it was somewhere in the northern regions.

Remarks:
This is merely a hypothesis, and has not been verified.
Remarks on remarks:
Forget the hypotheses and standard practice for background checks. Would anyone still use those brass glasses things with gradation marks he's got in his box? The only other place you'd find something like that is in a museum.
...That doesn't mean he's lying! No optician has used the Gaulish style ever since the fall of Lingones and the sacking of the Imperial Academy of Sciences. Besides, the Royal Victorian Academy of Sciences soon established new regulations that defined optometrists and opticians as separate professions. No matter where he was born, someone who mixes up the two definitely does NOT have an optometrist's license!

[Internal Medical Department Memo]
After discussions with Operator Nowell concerning his lack of an optometrist's license, we have arrived at the following solution:
1. Operator Nowell will go through training and receive formal education on modern optometry and lens fitting theory.
2. Operator Nowell will undergo formal optometry accreditation, pursuant to his progress in training.
3. Until he obtains optometrist accreditation, Operator Nowell will no longer conduct eye examinations, and focus solely on fitting and dispensing.

'I would say that Mr. Nowell is not so much an optometrist or optician as a craftsman. Even after learning how to use more convenient instruments, he still prefers to make the lenses and frames by hand.
'It may take more time, but every pair of glasses he makes is unique. The other patients say they envy my sister for the poem he engraved on her glasses frame: 'Under the blue sky the river flows / And by its banks sway the willows.' It's about what a bedridden child sees after walking out of the door for the first time in a long time.
—Family member of a patient
text.zh:
干员诺威尔出生于维多利亚，但具体地理位置已被当事人遗忘。不过，根据他明显受到高卢语发音习惯影响的口音，也许可以推测他出生于维多利亚北部地区。

批注：
以上仅为推测，不确保真实性。
批注的批注：
先忘了那些乱七八糟的推测和背景调查的惯例吧。我只说一点，你们有谁还在用他箱子里那种带刻度的黄铜眼镜？这东西，除了他箱子里那几副，你再要找一副一样的，就只能去博物馆里碰运气了。
……但这不代表他在撒谎！他肯定也不是什么术业有专攻的古董商。那东西是高卢制式，而自从林贡斯陨落、帝国科学院被洗劫一空之后，就没哪家配镜师还敢用了，更不用说没过多久维多利亚皇家科学院就制定了新的规范，把验光和配镜彻底区分开来，从此配镜的归配镜，验光的归验光。无论他出生在哪里，像他这样到现在还把两者混作一谈的……肯定没有验光师执照！

【医疗部内部公告】
关于干员诺威尔实际不具备验光师资格的问题，与当事人面谈后达成共识，现得出解决办法如下：
1.自即日起，干员诺威尔进行现代验光技术培训和实操演练，且系统性学习现代验光与配镜理论知识。
2.取得阶段性成果后，须参加验光医学资格证考试。
3.在干员诺威尔取得验光师资格前，不再安排其参与医疗部的眼科验光工作，仅提供配镜服务。

“诺威尔先生他，比起配镜师或者验光师，更像是一个呃……手艺人？意思是就算他学会了怎么用那些更方便的器械，也还是会倾向于在配镜环节由自己手工打磨镜片和镜框。
“虽然这样慢了点，可他做的每副眼镜都是不同的。这里的病人都羡慕我妹妹，因为她的眼镜框上有单独的刻字。诺威尔先生给她刻了一首诗，‘屋顶之上的蓝天，梧桐摇曳着，留下河畔棕榈的倒影’……这是在写一个长年卧病的孩子，终于走出家门时看到的景象。”
——某位患者家属

text.en:
Nowell was the first client who came to seek my assistance at the Londinium office after the war, not for himself, but for the child he was accompanying.
I was surprised to find him looking exactly the same as he did thirty years ago, when he passed through my village and made me a pair of glasses. I was around the same age as the child at the time. He didn't recognize me, and I didn't say anything. He was anxious at the boy's stubborn refusal to cooperate with medical personnel, but never lost his patience, just like how he listened to a farmer's child thirty years ago, before producing a pair of glasses like a magician and saying that he would collect payment once I graduated from university. Does he still remember those few pounds he has yet to collect?
We proceeded with the registration process. Nowell had brought the boy here at the request of his parents—whom he had assisted during the evacuation—in order to examine him for Oripathy. The boy had calmed down by then, and Nowell knelt down to speak to him in a low and serious tone. From what he said, I gathered that he understood quite well the tragedy that had occurred here in Londinium.
He was unsurprised by the results of the examination.
The child had finally stopped struggling and sat on the stool. As I was drawing his blood, I kept waiting for the words to come out of Nowell's mouth.
But he did not ask the question, even when all the tests had concluded. Had he stopped searching for that certain someone? The invisible shadow behind history, whose identity no one in town knew? Were they ever even a real person?
He never asked, so I could only guess. Perhaps he had already found them, or perhaps he had simply stopped obsessing over it. Regardless of the reason, he was there, standing, waiting in silence... As though he finally had unlimited time to spend at his leisure, without having to hurry to the next village, asking the question few knew the answer to.

[Addendum]
Operator Nowell entered Londinium and assisted the Self-Salvation Corps in evacuating the survivors. Reports about his agelessness and his search for the 'Unicorn' are to be archived with no immediate action at this time.
Expenses incurred by Operator Price of the Londinium office in purchasing corrective lenses have been reimbursed by the Medical Department as an employment benefit.
—HR Department Archive
text.zh:
诺威尔先生是我战后在伦蒂尼姆办事处接待的第一个求助者，然而他找到这里却并不为他自己，而是为他带来的孩子。
起初我惊讶于他的长相还与从前路过村庄为我制作眼镜时一模一样，而那已经是三十多年前的事情了，当时我还和他带来的这孩子差不多大。但他没有认出我，我也没有主动提起，只看着他站在一旁，因孩子固执、不肯配合医护人员而局促，但一直非常耐心。从前他也曾这样耐心地听完一个农人之子的困惑，接着像变戏法一样变出一副眼镜，约定好等对方上大学再收取相应的报酬。时间已经过去很久了，他还记得那几镑从未收到的货款吗？
我们决定先进行详细的信息登记。原来他带着孩子来到这里，只是因为在撤离中受到他帮助的一对父母，请他顺路将孩子送来进行矿石病排查。此时，男孩的反抗情绪已经开始消退，诺威尔先生蹲下来和他说话，声音低沉而严肃。从那些话中，我听出他对伦蒂尼姆、对这里早前发生的惨剧有着准确而清晰的认知。
他对排查的结果也早有预料。
之后那孩子终于不再固执，坐回圆凳上。我一边准备为他采血，一边等着诺威尔先生问出那句话——
但直到所有检查结束，他都没有问那句话。他不再寻找那个人了吗？那个他问遍了当时镇上所有人都毫无收获，无人得见的、历史背后的影子？说到底，那果真是一个人吗？
他没有问。于是我只能猜测，也许他早就找到了，也许这已经不是他心中的执着。无论如何，他如今仍然在那，沉默地伫立，等待，等待……好像他终于有无尽的时间可以消磨，不必着急赶往下一处，去继续追问那个绝大多数人都无从知晓答案的问题。

【补充记录】
干员诺威尔进入伦蒂尼姆之后，与自救军合作，为当地幸存市民的安全撤离做出了贡献。关于档案中指向他的长生者身份，以及持续寻找“独角兽”动向的部分内容，予以保留，档案封存。
另，罗德岛驻伦蒂尼姆办事处干员普莱斯采购个人用近视眼镜等医疗器械的费用已由医疗部综合福利支出报销。
——人事部留档

text.en:
Mr. Miltner admitted he had low expectations when he first reached out to Rhodes Island, particularly as we had already turned down several visitation requests for various reasons.
He did not give up, however, attributing the previous failures to bad timing, such as the landship being too far away, or the subject of his visit being away from the ship at the time. Far from being frustrated, he continued to submit his requests to meet with Operator Nowell.
When his eighth request finally went through, the rest of the process went surprisingly smoothly. Even though Norwell claimed not to know any middle-aged men by the name of Georgia Miltner, and showed clear reluctance regarding this 'family visit', and even though Mr. Miltner himself admitted having doubts about whether this Nowell of Rhodes Island was really the one he was looking for... the meeting came to pass, at long last.

[Audio Log]
'I've lost track of how many leads came out empty. Middle-aged Vulpo optician by the name of Nowell... there were three who fit all the criteria, in Victoria alone.
'But none were the one Grandma Madeline was looking for. None were... my great-grandfather.
'My father had already passed away, but I'd always hoped to tell Grandma Madeline that I found Great-Grandpa Nowell, while she could still see and hear.
'Do you know, she isn't even that concerned with being able to see him one last time. She just wanted to ask him a question, and hear the answer.
'That was the one thought keeping her going for a century. To me, she's always been a healthy, happy, and well-to-do old woman, which made me even more curious about this Great-Grandpa Nowell.
'And at long last, I'll get to see him with my own two eyes.
'I hope it's really him.'

After the meeting, Operator Nowell escorted Mr. Miltner all the way outside the ship. They bid each other farewell with a smile.
It seems Mr. Miltner had finally found his man.

[Addendum]
'Have you found peace?'
'I will. Someday.'
'Then...
'That's all Grandma Madeline wanted to ask, and all I need to know.'
text.zh:
米尔特内先生坦言，自己一开始通过医疗安置点联系上罗德岛本舰时，并未抱有太多真的能找到亲人的希望。加上我们出于种种原因曾多次拒绝他的访问申请，找到的希望大概更加渺茫。
但他并未因此放弃。他把前几次失败都归结为某种程度的时运不济，例如“本舰已经驶离，距申请者所在地太远，不建议个人在非必要情况下前来访问”，或“访问对象短时间内不在本舰，处于外派状态”等，总之，米尔特内先生仍然孜孜不倦地投递访问申请，大有不见到干员诺威尔就不罢休的势头——
好在他第八次投递的访问申请终于通过了，后续流程也很快滚动起来。于是，尽管诺威尔先生表示自己并不认识一位名叫乔治亚·米尔特内的中年男性，并对名为“探亲”的访问表现出下意识的排斥；尽管米尔特内先生本人也在申请中写明了内心的疑虑，直言不确定罗德岛的诺威尔是否真的是他所寻找的对象……这场会面终于还是姗姗而来。

【语音记录】
“说实在的，我找错过太多次了。配镜师、中年男性、沃尔珀、名字叫诺威尔……完全符合条件的人，光在维多利亚我就找到过三个。
“但没有一个是玛德琳祖母要找的人，没有一个是我的……曾祖父。
“父亲已经去世，我想，至少得让玛德琳祖母在彻底听不见也看不见之前，能得到诺威尔曾祖父确切的消息。
“你知道吗，她甚至不惦记再见一面，只是有问题想问，并且执着于得到答案。
“这念头支撑着她活过了百年，在我眼里她一直是个健康且幸福富足的老人，所以她越这样，我就越好奇，这位诺威尔曾祖父究竟是一个怎样的人？
“还好，我马上就要见到他了。
“……我希望，这次真的是他。”

会面之后，干员诺威尔陪同米尔特内先生一直走到本舰的出入口，他们平静地道别，分开时脸上都带着笑。
看来，这一次米尔特内先生没有找错。

【补充记录】
“您获得平静了吗？”
“总有一天，我会的。”
“那么……
“这就是玛德琳祖母想知道的，也是我想知道的所有了。”

text.en:
'The words I say often feel like they're coming out of somebody else's mouth.
'It's like a distorted voice coming from a telephone left on a table, asking if there's someone on the other end. That's the feeling some of the voices in the dream give me, a feeling that extends to reality, making it difficult to distinguish them.'
'Sounds like something out of a movie.'
'...I haven't watched many movies. I'm just describing what it feels like.'
'Sorry. The words just came out of my mouth...'
'It's alright. Do you like movies?'
'They briefly immerse me in somebody else's life and story, because my own is so easily forgotten against my will.'
'...I'm sorry.'
'It's okay, sir.'
'...Here, the coated non-corrective glasses you wanted. The lightweight frame should make them easy to wear for long periods. I suppose this is what young people want these days?'
'Wow, they're so light! Thank you.'
'Then I'll take my leave—'
'Do you want to come to this Friday's movie screening, Nowell?'
'What?'
'It's where we all get together watch a movie and talk about it.'
'Even if I won't have much to say?'
'But you described the voices in your dream so beautifully. We're showing an Ursine children's movie this week, and there'll be a lot of young operators there.'
'...Very well. Let me know the time and place.'

[A Prominent Memo]
Mon 9am, Eyewear Fitting Room, Medical Department. After work—Drink in moderation with Hellagur and Mountain at the bar.
Tue Morning—Repairing glasses. Totter comes for pickup at 3pm.
Wed 9am, Eyewear Fitting Room, Medical Department. 5pm—Training Room.
Thu—Day off. Pick up package. Check location on terminal.
Fri Morning—Prepare glasses. Afternoon—Prepare glasses. 7am—Movie screening (no doubleheaders if working the next day)
Sat/Sun—Off if no field assignment.
text.zh:
“很多时候我都会觉得从自己口中说出的话，声音倒像是从别人嘴里发出来的。
“就像是……电话听筒被搁置，里面不断确认对面是否有人时会发出的失真声音。有些梦里的声音给我这样的感觉，而梦里的感觉又一直蔓延到现实之中，很难把它们区分开来。”
“听上去真像电影。”
“……我没怎么看过电影，我只是在描述我的感受。”
“抱歉，我也只是下意识感叹……”
“没关系。你很喜欢看电影？”
“电影能让我短暂沉浸在别人的故事，别人的生活中。因为我会不受控制地遗忘自己的生活。”
“……抱歉。”
“没关系的，先生。”
“……给，你要的镀膜平光眼镜，镜架换了轻质的，戴起来不累。你们年轻人都喜欢这样的材质。”
“啊，真的好轻。谢谢您……”
“行，那我就先——”
“诺威尔先生，您要来参加周五的电影放映会吗？”
“什么？”
“就是，大家聚在一起，看看电影，聊聊感受的活动。”
“就算我没有那么多的感受可以分享？”
“我觉得，您刚才对梦中声音的感受，描述得就很美，而且，这周还有很多小干员也会来，我们一起看一部乌萨斯的儿童电影。”
“……好吧。告诉我地点和时间，我会准时过来的。”

【一份贴在显眼位置的日程提醒】
周一　上午9点到医疗部眼科配镜室轮班。下班后到舰上酒吧寻干员赫拉格与干员山，适量饮酒。
周二　上午修复眼镜。下午３点前完成，交给干员铅踝。
周三　上午9点到医疗部眼科配镜室轮班。下午5点到训练场参与训练。
周四　自由安排，记得找时间去取包裹，位置在终端上。
周五　上午制作眼镜。下午制作眼镜。晚上7点去参与观影活动。（下次不参与电影连映活动了，影响第二天工作）
周六至周日，若无外勤任务，可自由安排。

text.en:
Dear Doctor,
I am currently on a field mission. This letter is not urgent, and you may read it in your spare time.
As we returned to our vehicles, one of the other operators picked up a few white hairs from my shoulder. After I put them away, I heard that sound like joints creaking in my ear again, which I'd heard while boarding the vehicle.
It made me start searching for signs, tracing it back to my increasingly frequent dreams. Fragments of memory float to the surface even during the day, making it difficult to make up for the restless nights with a nap.
In my dreams, I sit in a workshop by the Lingones River, or walk through the marshes in southern Victoria. I see flashbacks of all my journeys across Terra. There is only one thing that I am sure of, no matter how blurred the fragments are: my heart is at peace. I am waiting.
But what am I waiting for? What CAN I wait for?
Perhaps I have saved enough lives. I have tasted happiness. Perhaps this ember will be scattered to the winds. Perhaps...
Perhaps that day is near.
If so, I ask for your blessings, friend.

There is no need to reply or hold on to this letter. Do with it as you please.
I will see you soon if all goes well with the mission. Take care.

(There is no signature)
text.zh:
致博士：
目前我正在执行一项外勤任务，这封信并不紧急，可等公务处理完毕后再行查看。
今日队伍回到载具上进行休整时，同行的干员从我肩上拾起几根白发，当我将它们尽数收好后，登上载具途中那种关节发出的喀嚓声又突然回荡在耳边。
这也致使我开始寻找更多迹象，并最终追溯到近来夜间越发严重的多梦少眠，白日里偶尔也会突然拾起一些琐碎的记忆片段，使休憩或补眠都难以实现。
好吧。更细节地说，在那些片段中，我大都坐在林贡斯河岸的工坊里，或徒步穿行在维多利亚中南部的沼泽中。于泰拉诸国游历的过往都以一种近乎闪烁的方式接连出现。唯有一件事是无论片段如何模糊也能判断的，那就是——我的内心已然安定，我在等待。
可我在等待什么？或者说，我能等待什么？
也许我已拯救足够多的生命，我已饱尝幸福的滋味，也许这捧余烬行将被风吹散，也许……
也许，那个日子真正近了。
如果是这样，那么我唯有希望得到你的祝福，我的朋友。

这封信无需回复，也无需保留，可自行处置。
若任务顺利，不日归来。珍重。

（无署名）

value.en: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.
value.zh: 体表有源石结晶分布，参照医学检测报告，确认为感染者。

infectionStatus.en: Originium crystals distributed across surface of body, confirmed Infected by medical examination.
infectionStatus.zh: 体表有源石结晶分布，参照医学检测报告，确认为感染者。

text.en: Brigid, a nomad. Said to be from one of Tara's ancient wandering tribes, who have lived on the plains and hills since time immemorial. They also serve as traditional couriers for Catastrophe warnings, mail, and other related tasks. At Operator Reed's recommendation, she has started working with Rhodes Island, receiving Oripathy treatment while taking part in battle as a sniper operator.
text.zh: 水灯心，本名布莉吉，游牧民。据称来自塔拉某支古老的游牧部族，其成员长久以来在平原、丘陵地区从事游牧活动，兼领天灾预警、传信相关职责。现经干员苇草推荐与罗德岛合作，在接受矿石病治疗的同时，作为狙击干员协助战斗。

text.en:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 3%
A few small Originium crystals can be seen on the back of Operator Brigid's waist.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.14u/L
'She's certainly very healthy. Even if she hadn't turned around, lifted up her shirt, and pointed out the crystals to me on her own, based on her blood test results, she's in better condition than most Catastrophe Messengers I've checked over before. Maybe those Taran nomadic tribes have some sort of special method to protect themselves? ...What's that? She just follows along whenever the burdenbeasts migrate? That works?'
text.zh:
造影检测结果显示，该干员体内脏器轮廓模糊，可见异常阴影，循环系统内源石颗粒检测异常，有矿石病感染迹象，现阶段可确认为矿石病感染者。

【体细胞与源石融合率】3%
干员水灯心腰部后侧可见少量源石结晶。

【血液源石结晶密度】0.14u/L
“她这身板真的很健康了。如果不是她自己转过身撩起衣服，把身上的结晶指给我看，光从血液检测结果来说，情况比我之前见过的多数天灾信使都要乐观。也许她那个塔拉的游牧部族有些什么特殊的防护手段？……什么？她说只是带着驮兽不停迁徙？这也有用？”

text.en:
Operator Brigid was born in the plains of southern Victoria. As a member of one of the few nomadic tribes there, she knows many legends and stories that modern Taran city-dwellers are unfamiliar with. Once she became an adult, she split from her tribe and became a solitary drifter until a series of localized conflicts broke out between Tara and its neighbors. During this period of unrest, she continued her nomadic lifestyle, taking on work that involved warning people about Catastrophes and delivering messages, relying on her plentiful experience with wilderness survival and long-distance travel to do so.
We are unsure how she balances all this traveling for work with her personal life. Maybe it's as she says: her life is an 'endless road'. This does match the first impression she usually gives: cheerful, uncomplicated, and hyperactive.

[Addendum]
As per protocol, we were required to sit down with her for a serious conversation, and to our surprise we learned another side of the Na Saoirsí incident, as seen through her eyes. When we asked for her personal understanding of the matter, she had this to say:
'Those who can see the flames in others' hearts can also share some of their own soul's fire.'
We had no idea what to make of this, especially as a response to our question, until she explained further.
According to her, in the tribes' distant past, this ability protected their people from the dangers of the wilds and the darkness, but such flames also burn away at their wielder's life. As such, those who disregard the cost and freely give away their flame often run into hardships, and never have happy endings of their own. Even so, the people still choose to place great expectations on those with this extraordinary ability, and hold them in the highest esteem. The authority and prestige held by the Red Dragon stem from this respect.
This clearly does not match our understanding of how political power takes shape in modern society, and we can only surmise that it is a folk tale passed down orally among Tara's nomadic tribes. However, if we consider that ability a form of Originium Arts, and compare it to a tradition from another obscure Taran community Brigid once mentioned—the 'wakemen' and their 'fire-returning ceremony'—it is not difficult to see the similarities. Because of this, we lean towards considering the legend an attempted explanation of the wakemen's Arts, rather than historical evidence of any kind of Victorian regime change.

That might be where it comes from, but it's not how the legend goes! The Red Dragon gave away her fire, and if she don't get it back, she'll die. Simple as.
—A recording Operator Brigid made at HR
text.zh:
干员水灯心出生于维多利亚南部平原地区。作为数量稀少的游牧部族一员，她知晓许多不为现代塔拉城镇居民所知的传说故事，在成长到足以独当一面的年纪后才从部族中离开，独自漂泊，直到塔拉与周边地区的局部冲突次第爆发。动荡期间，干员水灯心一直都保持着游牧的生活方式，长期从事天灾预警与信件传递的工作，有着丰富的野外生存与长途行动经验。
我们无从得知她如何平衡这样奔波的数份工作与自己的生活，或许，如她本人所说，她的生活就是“永远在路上”。这也符合她给人留下的第一印象：快乐、简单而匆忙。

【补充记录】
就遵守必要的秩序与流程一事，我们与干员水灯心进行了严肃的谈话，意外地从这名见证者口中了解到纳斯尔纱事件的另一面。谈及个人对此事件的理解，干员水灯心这样回答：
“那些能看见他者心火的人，也因此拥有将己身之火分享的能力。”
起初我们并不理解这句话的涵义，更不用说它与我们所询问事项的关联，直到干员水灯心向我们进一步解释。
据她所说，在更早的、尚属于游牧民的远古时代里，这种能力可以保护普通人不受荒野与黑暗的侵袭，却会燃烧使用者的生命。所以，那些选择不计回报地将火分出的人，常常命途多舛，不得善终。但即便如此，人们仍以这类人拥有非同寻常的能力为由，对其寄予不平凡的期望，推崇备至，红龙的权柄与威信也由此而生。
显然，这种说法与现代社会对此地政权如何形成的认知并不相符，我们只能认为这也是塔拉游牧民口口相传的“传说”之一。不过，如果将这种能力看作某种源石技艺，与干员水灯心曾提及的塔拉另一鲜为人知的群体——“守灵人”的“还火仪式”进行比对，则不难发现二者的共通之处。因此，我们更倾向于将这一传说理解为“守灵人”源石技艺的起源之一，而非将其作为维多利亚政权更迭历史的佐证。

这就是原因，不是传说！红龙分出了火，除非她收回那些火，否则她就会死。就这么简单。
——干员水灯心在人事部的录音

text.en:
According to our background checks, Brigid left the city and returned to the plains following the Na Saoirsí incident. While she is currently a Rhodes Island operator, she is often away on field work, and never stays on the landship for long. Thus, we recommend inquiring into her whereabouts when necessary, but there is no need to actively track her.

[Excerpt from a Rhodes Island Clubs bulletin board announcement]
'Topology Lovers Research Group third official roundtable and reception will be held at the mid-level activity room—specific details can be found on your personal terminal. At this roundtable, we are fortunate to welcome an expert in topology's more pragmatic side, here to demonstrate some special knot-tying techniques. Modern topological research grew out of Knot theory, and knots themselves possess a long history and cultural significance...'

'Notice of Suspension of Racing Club activities: the planned Saturday afternoon race in the living area corridors and the planned weekly Friday evening back-and-forth sprint on the deck have been canceled. We ask club members who see this notice to pass along the news. We are currently waiting on rescheduled dates to be decided.'

'Disciplinary Notice: several days ago, two members of the Racing Club, Brigid and Grani, held impromptu sprinting competitions in the mid-level corridors. As they did not give any advance notice or clear the corridors of personnel, they caused many passing operators to imitate them, creating a deleterious effect on pedestrian flow and safety in the corridors on that level. Similar activities are now suspended, and the involved operators have been fined.'

[Racing Club message board]
is brigid back yet
also how come she left in the first place
im gonna ask the radiant knight when we can start racing again
—Grani
1) No.
2) Don't know.
3) Don't bother her.
—Tequila
is brigid back yet
—Windflit
NO!!
—Wild Mane
text.zh:
根据背景调查，在纳斯尔纱事件结束之后，干员水灯心就回到了原野之上，不再于城市中逗留。即使现在以干员身份加入罗德岛，她本人也更倾向于参与外派工作，而非长期留驻本舰。因此，建议对干员水灯心的去向适时问询，但不必频繁追踪。

【罗德岛兴趣社团公告栏公示摘录】
“拓扑学爱好者研究协会第三次正式座谈会暨迎新会，将在中层甲板的活动室开展，具体信息可在个人终端查收。在本次座谈会上，我们有幸邀请到一位实用主义拓扑学学者，前来为与会者展示专业的绳结编织技巧。绳结研究，是现代拓扑学的学科前身之一，拥有悠久的历史与文化内涵……”

“赛跑俱乐部活动停办通知：原定于周六下午在生活区回廊进行的赛跑比赛，与原定于每周五晚上举办的甲板往返短跑比赛，现均已取消，请社团成员看到通知后相互转告。活动恢复时间待定。”

“通报批评：日前，水灯心、格拉尼两位赛跑俱乐部成员在中层甲板走廊进行了短途赛跑，因未提前报备和进行人员疏散，吸引了众多路过干员效仿，对该层的道路畅通及行人安全产生了极大的负面影响，现做出类似活动停办、涉事干员罚款等处置，特此通告。”

【赛跑俱乐部留言板】
水灯心回来了吗？她怎么又走了？我要去问问耀骑士，我们什么时候能恢复比赛！
——格拉尼
没有，不知道，以及别问。
——龙舌兰
水灯心回来了吗？
——掠风
没有！
——野鬃

text.en:
The Catastrophe Messengers Rhodes Island often works with have never met a 'colleague' quite like Brigid before.
First of all, it must be noted that, contrary to what you might think, Catastrophe Messengers generally do not engage in the routine letter and parcel deliveries that standard Messengers do. They are mainly dedicated to delivering Catastrophe warnings, and use unique methods of intel sharing and transmitting among themselves in order to be ready to handle any unexpected occurrences. In that sense, it is difficult to see Brigid working by herself in Tara as anything more than an ordinary Messenger handling mail or war orders.
It took a follow-up investigation for us to understand more. Traditional methods for forecasting Catastrophes have been passed down in Brigid's tribe for generations. When she set out on her own, it was these techniques that allowed her to aid isolated nomadic cities that actual Catastrophe Messengers were unable to help find shelter.
According to her, it was a friend's suggestion that prompted her to call herself a 'Catastrophe Messenger' when she registered with us. She does not seem too clear on what precisely that entails.

What's the big difference between helping deliver letters and warning people about Catastrophes? They're both just passing on info.
More importantly, what kinda arsehole would I have to be to see the signs of a Catastrophe and not go tell the people in the way?
Right, since I'm usually following the burdenbeasts to keep an eye on the Catastrophe, sometimes I'll have to make a run for the city to warn them in time, even if the beasts haven't made it to safety yet. But even if I run, I still don't always make it in time... That's why I try to run faster than ever, little by little, so I can make it more often.
—HR audio log

[Addendum]
After hearing about this, several experienced Catastrophe Messengers expressed a desire to introduce Brigid to modern Catastrophe warning systems so she could perform her duties better than ever. They were quick to put their ideas into practice. Aside from sharing information with her, they decided to use their own wages to put together a set of basic Catastrophe forecasting equipment, giving it to her in Rhodes Island's name.
Although Brigid did ultimately refuse it, saying she'd find a way to pay for it herself, she was happy to accept their gift of a comms terminal of the same model commonly used by Catastrophe Messengers, becoming a part of their everyday group chat.
text.zh:
经常与罗德岛往来的天灾信使全都未见过水灯心这样的“同行”。
需要先解释的一点是，尽管反直觉，但天灾信使一般来说并不从事常规意义上的信件、邮包传递这类信使活动。他们主要负责预警天灾，互相之间有一套独特的情报共享和传递机制，以便应对各种突发情况。因此，不管从哪个方面来看，干员水灯心独自在塔拉地区从事的工作，都更像一位传递信件和战时消息的普通信使。
而在后续的调查过程中，我们才了解到更多。干员水灯心出身的游牧部族传承着使用旧方法预测天灾的传统，等她出走独立之后，也正是使用这套方法，帮助一些真正的天灾信使无法关照的、落单的小型移动城市，躲避天灾的侵袭。
据她本人所说，在报到时自称“天灾信使”是朋友的建议，听上去她本人对此并无清晰的认知。

帮人送信和预警天灾是一样的，都是传递消息，没什么区别啊。
主要是，如果我能提前看到天灾来临的迹象，却不去通知那些可能不知道的人，不是很奇怪吗？
嗯，因为我一般是凭驮兽牧群的活动轨迹来观察天灾，有的时候，就算不等驮兽们到安全区域就跑去给移动城市预警，也会赶不上……所以我只能努力跑得快一点，再快一点，这种赶不上的时候总会越来越少。
——人事部语音记录

【补充记录】
在听说这件事之后，几位从业多年的天灾信使都表示希望能帮助水灯心熟悉现代天灾预警系统，以更好地履行天灾信使的职责。这一想法迅速落实：除了共享情报之外，他们决定用自己的工资凑齐一套基础的天灾预测装置，再以罗德岛的名义赠送给她。
尽管最后干员水灯心拒绝了天灾预测装置，表示会想办法自己购买，但她高兴地接受了同行们赠与的天灾信使常用款通讯终端，面对面加入了他们的日常群聊。

text.en: Operator: Brigid Time: three months ago Books borrowed: Local Maps of Tara (1098 edition) Wanted to borrow a map, seeing how I lost the one I drew. What map? Y'know, a map, just point 'em out and I'll go find it myself. Err... All these look real different from what I remember. Why's that? The map I wanted... Lemme sketch for you it real quick—Oh, I want a 'map of Tara'? Let's have a look then... Aye, that's the one! But we usually just call 'em maps, no Tara. —Excerpt from a reader's inquiry at the library's information desk Operator: Brigid Time: recent Books borrowed: Atlas of Victoria (3rd edition, 1072) (Recommended classification: Transport & Travel) Traveler's Maps of Leithanien (Hardcover edition) Maps of Ursus (Bilingual boxset edition) A Grand Overview of the Lands of Yan (Recommended classification: Historical fiction) ...... Origins of the Taran Script (writing workbook included) Due to often missing return deadlines, Operator Brigid will have to undergo a more detailed registration process whenever borrowing books or applying for extensions. Additionally, considering she borrows for a specific purpose and mostly only borrows from a single category of materials, and how some of these maps are the only surviving copies, we strongly suggest she use the photocopier in the future. The photocopier's so slow! I'll return 'em next time I'm back! Brigid —A line of shaky handwriting written on the library loan record, reconstructed with difficulty after being noticed by an operator familiar with her writing style
text.zh:
干员水灯心三个月前的借阅记录：
《塔拉地区地图概览（1098年再版）》

我想借一份地图，我自己画的那份弄丢了。
哪里的地图？就是地图啊，你把位置指给我，我自己去找吧。
呃……这里的地图，好多都长得跟我印象里的不一样，这是为什么？
我要找的地图……我给你画个大概形状吧，长这样——看着像“塔拉地图”？我看看呢。
哦，就是这个！但我们一般就管它叫地图。
——某日图书室咨询台前一位读者的询问，仅摘录部分

干员水灯心近期借阅记录：
《维多利亚地图册（1072年第三版）》（建议分类：交通旅游）
《莱塔尼亚实用地图》（精装版）
《乌萨斯地图》（盒装双语对照版）
《炎国地图大观》（建议分类：历史小说）
……
《塔拉语字母源考》（附书写教程）

由于常常晚于规定期限归还，干员水灯心在借阅书籍或申请延期还书时会需要进行更详细的登记。另外，鉴于借阅目的明确、借阅类型较为单一，且部分书籍为孤本的情况存在，我们会在之后强烈建议她使用整本复印功能。

复印太慢、下次回的时候还！水灯心
——写于借阅记录表上的一行扭曲字迹，经熟悉该字迹的干员辨认之后勉强还原了内容

text.en:
[Secondary Security Screening record]
1. A straw burdenbeast, 20cm x 16cm x 7cm, handmade. No suspicious liquids detected, shiny surface is due to burdenbeast oil.
2. A small piece of cheese, appears moldy. Testing confirms it is not moldy. The spots on its surface are where this type of cheese gets its characteristic flavor from.
3. A bone knife, clear traces of hand-polishing. Dull, can barely cut fruit.
4. Two medals, appear to be promotion medals issued by Rhodes Island HR. After further investigation, owner is already in our records as Brigid.
5. A glass bottle, height approx. 7cm, mouth diameter 3cm, filled with a clear liquid, labeled 'Dossoles'. Testing shows the liquid in the bottle is 100% artificial seawater, with some special method used to keep it clear with 0 precipitation or sediment.
......
11. A collection of anonymous Taran poems with a note attached. Note says: 'The grass here is different from other lands, while the sky here's bluer than yesterday's. All belongs to tomorrow, and tomorrow's always a brand new day, a day unlike any other.'

...Aside from a couple things, most of this stuff has to be taken out of your bags for the security inspection, then a second one if you want any of it to reach the Doctor's desk. You really not worried about all that hassle?
—Closure

Huh? No one ever told me to open my bag. I just jumped in over that little gate over there, even made sure to say hi to the lady minding the door!
—Brigid

?
—Closure
text.zh:
【二次安检的物品记录】
1.一枚草编驮兽，尺寸约20cm*16cm*7cm，手工艺品。没有可疑液体附着，上面的光泽来自驮兽兽油。
2.一小块奶酪，看起来发霉了。经检测，没有发霉，上面的斑点正是这种奶酪的风味所在。
3.一柄骨刀，手磨痕迹明显。不算锋利，勉强可以拿来切水果。
4.两枚徽章，看样式是罗德岛人事部颁发的晋升勋章。据查，所有者已记录在册，为水灯心。
5.一个玻璃瓶，高约7cm，瓶口直径3cm，装有澄亮液体，标签上写着“多索雷斯”。据检验，瓶中液体为100%人工海水，以特殊方法保持了透光性，未生成任何沉淀物。
……
11.夹有字条的塔拉语无名诗集一本。字条内容：“这里的青草与别处有所不同，这里的天空也比昨日更加蔚蓝。一切都是明天，明天必然是不同的一天。”

……除了个别几样，多数东西过安检的时候都要掏出来检查吧，放到博士办公桌上还得过二次安检，这家伙完全不怕麻烦的？
——可露希尔

啊？但没人叫我打开包呀。我从那边的小门直接跳进来的，还和门口的小妹妹说了你好！
——水灯心

？
——可露希尔
